events.event_narrative: US Highway 20 was closed from 17 miles east of Butte City to 2 miles west of Idaho Falls on the 30th.  Snowfall, strong winds with blowing and drifting snow and reduced visibility was the reason for the closing.
The COOP observer in Bern measured 11 inches of snow on the 30th and 31st.
The COOP observer in Bone recorded 10 inches of snow the last 3 days of the month.

Idaho Highway 47 was closed from Ashton to 2 miles north of Warm River.   The COOP observer in Island Park measured 17 inches of snow through the last 3 days of the month.   Extensive blowing and drifting of snow was reported.

Interstate 84 was closed on the 31st from 10 miles east of Heyburn to the Utah border due to reduced visibility in blowing and drifting snow and snowfall.  Minidoka COOP reported 4 inches of snow on the 30th and 31st.
The Malad City COOP observer reported 7 inches of snow on the 29th and 30th.
Four to 7 inches of snow fell in the Pocatello/Chubbuck area on the 30th and 31st.
The Inkom COOP observer reported 9 inches of snow on the 30th and 31st.
Interstate 84 was closed from 10 miles east of Heyburn to the Utah border due to snow and blowing and drifting snow reducing visibility on the 31st.
The COOP observer at Richfield recorded 6 inches of snow on the 30st and 31st.
Idaho Highway 47 was closed from Ashton to 2 miles north of Warm River. on the 30th   8 to 10 inches of snow was measured 8 miles north northeast of Tetonia with 7 inches in Driggs.

Idaho Highway 33 was closed from Newdale to Tetonia and US Highway 20 was closed from 17 miles east of Butte City to 2 miles west of Idaho Falls on the 30th due to heavy snowfall and strong winds causing blowing and drifting snow with reduced visibility.   Snowfall amounts were the following:  7 inches 5 miles south southwest of Osgood, 5 inches Menan, 7 inches Rigby, 10 inches St Anthony, and 8 inches Sugar City.
A spotter measured 10.5 inches of snow 4 miles west of Victor.

The Bern COOP observer reported 13 inches of snow during the storm with 8 inches on the 5th.   The Bear Lake School District 33 was closed on both the 5th and the 6th due to the combination of heavy snowfall and gusty winds.
Estimated snow amounts over the storm period were 42 inches at Franklin Basin and 33 inches at Emigrant Summit.

Idaho transportation department reported a foot of snow in Victor by early morning on the 5th.   A trained spotter 4 miles west of Victor reported 23 inches of snow for the 3 day period.  A total of 22 inches was estimated at the Pine Creek Pass SNOTEL site.  Teton School District 401 was closed on January 5th due to the heavy snow and high winds making roads nearly impassable.
Estimated snow amounts during the storm from SNOTEL sites were  Bear Canyon 10 inches, Smiley Mountain 15 inches, Stickney Mill 10 inches, and Swede Peak 11 inches.

The snowfall estimation at the Sheep Mountain SNOTEL site was 18 inches.  Wind gusts of 40 to 60 mph were common and on the 5th the Grace School District 148 and Soda Springs School District 150 were closed.  Idaho Highway 34 was closed from 2 miles north of Soda Springs to the Wyoming border was closed due to the snow and wind on the 5th as well.

Very heavy snow combined with periods of winds gusting 40 to 60 mph to cause very hazardous travel conditions.  US Highway 26 was closed from Ririe to Swan Valley on both the 4th and 5th.   Estimated SNOTEL amounts were Giveout 20 inches, Slug Creek 22 inches, and Somsen Ranch 20 inches.   Idaho Highway 34 was closed from Soda Springs to the Wyoming border on the 5th.

Heavy snow and wind gusts over 40 mph created extremely difficult travel conditions for several days.   Estimated SNOTEL amounts were:  Island Park 14 inches and White Elephant 13 inches.   8 inches fell at the Island Park COOP site.

Snow and high winds gusting over 40 mph caused extremely difficult travel.   Minidoka School District 331 and Cassia County School District 151 were both closed on January 4th.  The COOP observer at Oakley recorded 8 inches of snow and the COOP observer at Minidoka Dam recorded 6 inches of snow.
Snowfall estimates at the Mill Creek Summit SNOTEL sites were 35 inches.

Heavy snow combined with wind gusts of over 40 mph to create hazardous travel throughout the region.    The COOP observer at Malad City recorded 9 inches of snow.   Several crashes occurred near Malad Summit on interstate 15 with crashes and slideoffs near mile marker 24 during the morning of the 5th.   Oneida School District 351 closed due to the hazardous road conditions on the 5th.

Snow and wind gusts of 40 to 60 mph caused extremely hazardous travel from the 6th mainly in the morning hours.   On the 4th 1 to 2 inches of snow fell north of Pocatello with central and south Pocatello receiving 5 to 6 inches.   The following schools were closed on the 4th due to the hazardous road conditions:  Pocatello/Chubbuck School District 25, Snake River School District 52, Blackfoot School District 55, Aberdeen School District 58, American Falls School District 381.  Total snow amounts ranged from 3 to 9 inches.

The combination of heavy snow and winds gusting over 40 mph for several days brought hazardous travel to the region.   The March Valley School District 21 was closed on the 4th, 5th and 6th.   Snow amounts recorded by COOP observers were 6.5 inches at Downey, 13 inches at Inkom, and 9 inches at McCammon.
Heavy snow with strong winds occurred through a 3 day period.   Snow amounts estimated at the Vienna Mine SNOTEL was 4 feet.   The Stanley COOP observer recorded a foot of snow in the storm.

Estimated snow amounts from the SNOTEL sites were:  Chocolate Gulch 15 inches, Dollarhide Summit 30 inches, Galena 24 inches, Galena Summit 32 inches, Hyndman 13 inches and Lost Wood Divide 19 inches.  The Ketchum COOP reported 9.5 inches of snow.

Snow combined with 40 to 60 mph wind gusts caused hazardous travel for three days.   US Highway 26 was closed from Ririe to Swan Valley on the 4th and 5th and Idaho Highway 33 was closed from Newdale to Tetonia on the 4th.   Ririe School District 252 was closed on the 4th due to the hazardous travel conditions.

Whiteout conditions caused by 40 plus mph wind gusts created a 40 vehicle crash on US Highway 20 in the east bound lane on January 7th.   It initially occurred when a semi crashed into a stopped vehicle that was stopped due to the low visibility.   Ambulances were involved in the pile up.  The location was in the Henry's Lake flats in between Idaho Highway 87 and Island Park.   Two police deputies were struck as well.   Only very minor injuries were reported in the pile up with no deaths.   The crash occurred at around 3 pm MST and US Highway 20 was closed for several hours as well as Idaho Highway 87 from Island Park to the Montana state line for several hours.   Both were re-opened on the 8th.  Snowfall was not heavy in the 1 to 3 inch range but the extremely gusty winds created the whiteout.

A 45 year old man was found dead near the WinCo grocery store on January 24th on the 1000 block of Yellowstone.   Temperatures were in the teens and it is believed extended exposure to cold temperatures contributed to his death.

A crash caused by slick roads and blowing snow occurred in Chubbuck just before 8 am on February 1st at the corner of West Tyhee and North Philbin roads.   Two children were transported to Portneuf Medical Center with injuries.
An inch or so of snow brought very slick road conditions to Pocatello the morning of the 16th with at least 8 accidents including one involving a school bus.
Nine inches of snow was reported 4 miles west of Victor.

The combination of snow and high winds caused significant blowing snow closed Idaho Highway 47 from Ashton to 1 mile north of Warm River.   Idaho Highway 32 was closed from Tetonia to Ashton.   Ashton recorded 5 inches of snow with the storm.

Only about 3 inches of snow fell but strong winds caused extensive blowing and drifting snow.   Idaho Highway 87 closed 3 miles north of Island Park to the Montana state line by the afternoon of the 21st.  Idaho Highway 47 also closed on the morning of the 21st from Ashton to 1 mile north of Warm River.
Wind chill values in the -25 to -35 range occurred with the coldest a -34 degree reading 6 miles north of Monteview at 725 AM on the 23rd.

Extreme cold wind chills followed the passage of a Canadian cold front.   -40 degrees or colder were common by the morning of the 23rd.    The coldest were -48 at Monida at 645 AM and -48 at China Point at 815 AM.  Both of these sites were Idaho Transportation Department sites on interstate 15.

Extreme cold wind chill readings occurred behind a cold frontal passage.   Coldest readings on the 23rd were -46 at Henry's Lake at 730 AM, -35 near Spencer at 112 AM, and 033 at Osborne Bridge at 445 AM.  Island Park recorded -30 at 654 AM.
Very cold wind chill readings of -25 to -30 were widespread with the coldest -30 at Dead Man Canyon at 725 AM.
Extremely cold wind chill readings occurred overnight on the 22nd into the 23rd.   Moburg Canyon recorded -30 at 839 AM and Juniper Interchange recorded -25 at 800 AM on the 23rd.
An extremely strong Canadian cold front brought wind chill readings of -37 at the Smiley Creek Airport at 800 AM on the 23rd and -27 at the Stanley Airport at 0751 AM on the 23rd.

Wind chill readings of -20 to -30 occurred in the Teton Valley behind a strong Canadian cold front.   -29 was the coldest reading on the 23rd in Ashton at 0700 AM.  Botts recorded -27 at 430 AM and River Rim -25 at 0400 AM.

Widespread -20 to -35 wind chill readings occurred overnight on the 22nd into the 23rd.   The coldest on the 23rd were:  -33 at Kettle Butte at 0715 AM, -30 at Roberts at 0200 AM, and -30 at Sage Junction at 0645 AM.   The Idaho Falls Regional Airport recorded -21 at 0553 AM.

Estimated snowfall from SNOTEL sites were the following:  Giveout 15 inches, Slug Creek Divide 16 inches, and Somsen Ranch 12 inches.   The snow and wind caused a semi trailer to jacknife on US Route 26 5 miles east of Irwin with multiple accidents.
Estimated SNOTEL amounts were 16 inches at Bostetter Ranger Station and 24 inches at Howell Canyon.
The Emigrant Summit SNOTEL estimated 16 inches of snowfall.

Eight to 10 inches of snow fell in the Ashton area.   On March 9th Ashton Elementary School and North Fremont High School were closed due to heavy snowfall and high winds causing hazardous travel conditions.   On March 10th Teton School District 401 was closed due to extreme wind chill temperatures.
The Vienna Mine SNOTEL estimated 16 inches of snowfall.
Snow, wind and extreme cold wind chill values caused the closing of Teton School District 401 on March 10th.

Several accidents occurred on Interstate 15 near Shelley including 8 vehicles and a semi.   Brief heavy snowfall caused slush to build up on the roads and was thought to cause the accidents on northbound interstate 15.

The peak wind gust was 70 mph recorded at the Botts ITD site.  River Rim recorded 60 mph and Driggs airport 55 mph.   The The Driggs Spud Drive-In Theater movie screen crashed to the ground overnight during early morning hours of the 5th.    It was built in 1953 and was on the National Register of Historic Places.

The highest wind gust recorded was 66 mph at Kettle Butte.   2 miles north northeast of Sugar City recorded 60 mph with 58 mph at the Idaho Falls Airport and 59 mph at the ITD Roberts site.   Interstate 15 closed from about 3 pm MDT to 6 pm MDT on the 4th from milepost 119 in Idaho Falls to milepost 134.5 in Roberts due to the high winds and blowing dust.
Fifty to 60 mph wind gusts were common after a cold frontal passage with a peak gust recorded at 62 mph 4 miles west of Galena.
Widespread 50 to 60 mph gusts were recorded with the peak measured at 61 mph at Cotton Ridge RAWS site.
Wind gusts behind a strong cold frontal passage measured 50 to 60 mph with the highest 59 mph 1 mile east northeast of Richfield and 55 mph at Kinsey Butte.
Widespread 50 to 65 mph wind gusts were present following the passage of a strong cold front.  The peak was 65 mph at Moburg Canyon with 57 mph at Pilot Gold and 54 mph at Yale ITD site.
Widespread 40 to 60 mph wind gusts occurred following a strong cold frontal passage.   The peak gust was 57 mph at Aberdeen with over 40 mph at Chubbuck, Pocatello and Taber.

Widespread 50 to 65 mph wind gusts were recorded following a strong cold frontal passage.   The peak gusts were 64 mph at Dead Man Canyon and the base of Howe Peak.   Howe recorded 54 mph and Arco 51 mph.
Extreme wind gusts in the 50 to 65 mph range were frequent after a strong cold frontal passage.  The ITD site at Pine Creek Pass recorded 62 mph and Pine Creek RAWS recorded 52 mph.
A strong cold frontal passage brought strong wind gusts to the entire region with the peak gust 65 mph recorded at the Camas ITD site on Interstate 15.

Extreme wind gusts in the 60 to 75 mph range were widespread in the Arco and Mud Lake Desert region.   A 74 mph gust was recorded 9 miles south southwest of Mud Lake with 66 mph at Telegraph Hill and Puzzle with 64 mph at Tom Cat Summit.   Monteview and Haber recorded 61 mph gusts and Atomic City 59 mph.

Snow and strong winds caused whiteout conditions on interstate 84  with a multiple vehicle accident influenced by the weather occurring just south of the Yale Road Exit at around 5:30 MDT.  RWIS station ITD 12 near the incident reported 0.24 mile visibility at 415 PM and wind gusts as high as 66 mph at 445 PM.   Wind gusts over 50 mph through 645 PM.   Nine people were transported to hospitals.   AS many as 12 semi tractor trailers were involved.  Interstate 86 then closed from 630 PM MDT until 115 AM MDT on the 12th.
A week of cold temperatures and moisture brought heavy snow to high elevations.   SNOTEL estimated were 20 inches at Bostetter Ranger Station and 34 inches at Howell Canyon.
Very heavy snowfall fell during the week with estimated amounts at SNOTEL sites of 26 inches at Sedgwick Peak and 17 inches at Wildhorse Divide.
An estimated 15 inches of snow fell at the Oxford Springs SNOTEL site.
Snowfall amounts estimated at SNOTEL sites were 21 inches at Emigrant Summit and 27 inches at Frnaklin Basin.
An estimated 18 inches of snow fell at the Sheep Mountain SNOTEL site.   The COOP observer at Bone recorded 8 inches of snow.
Estimated snow amounts at SNOTEL sties were 15 inches at Giveout, 16 inches at Slug Creek Divide, and 19 inches at Somsen Ranch.   The COOP observer at Swan Valley reported 14 inches of snow.
Estimated snow amounts at SNOTEL sites were 12 inches at Crab Creek and 21 inches at White Elephant.   The COOP observer at Island Park recorded 16.5 inches of snow through the period.
An estimated 16 inches of snow fell at the Milll Creek Summit SNOTEL site.
An estimated 29 inches of snow fell at the Vienna Mine SNOTEL site.

The Ketchum COOP observer recorded 11 inches of snow.   SNOTEL snowfall estimates were the following:  Dollarhide Summit 23 inches, Galena Summit 15 inches, Hyndman 15 inches, Lost Wood Divide 10 inches, Garfield Ranger Station 27 inches, Smiley Mountain 18 inches, Stickney Mill 16 inches, and Swede Peak 17 inches.
The COOP observer at Craters of the Moon recorded 10.4 inches of snow with the extended period of winter weather.

A single engine Cessna 208B crashed into Gem State Processing in Heyburn a potato processing plant.   The pilot was heading into the Burley Municipal Airport and crashed into the building at around 835 AM MDT.   It occurred during a heavy snow showers and the visibility at the airport was around 1 mile between 8 and 9 AM.   It is possible the visibility was a factor and the pilot was killed in the accident.
Sixty to 70 mph wind gusts were common following the passage of a cold front.  Wind gusts on the morning of the 29th were 70 mph at Yale, 68 mph at Idahome, 65 mph at Pilot Gold.
A 60 mph wind gust measured at station FW4083 2 miles northwest of Pocatello.
Mesonet site BLK 1 mile east southeast of Blackfoot recorded a 61 mph wind gust.
Mesonet site ABE 1 mile northeast of Aberdeen recorded a 65 mph wind gust.
Mesonet site MIN recorded a 64 mph wind gust 6 miles northwest of Minidoka.
Mesonet site BAS at base of Howe Peak recorded a 62 mph wind gust.
Mesonet site 3699 D6 Puzzle 6 miles northwest of Atomic City recorded a 62 mph wind gust.

Interstate 15 closed from Roberts south to Idaho Falls due to blowing dust causing visibilities of 1/4 mile with widespread gusts of 50 to 60 mph.   Some gusts measured were:   58 mph at Idaho Falls Airport, 59 mph at Kettle Butte, 53 mph at Osgood, and 53 mph at Ririe.  The interstate was closed from 3:20 PM MDT until 10:48 PM MDT.
The Botts Idaho Transportation site measured a wind gust of 60 mph.   Ashton recorded 53 mph and River Rim 50 mph.
A 61 mph wind gust was measured at the Puzzle Idaho Transportation site.  Other gusts were 56 mph at Telegraph Hill and 55 mph at Atomic City.

The peak wind gust was measured at 70 mph at the Kettle Butte Idaho Transportation Department site.   The Idaho Falls ASOS recorded 62 mph at 1:34 Pm MDT.   Four miles northwest of Shelley recorded 57 mph.   A large Dominoes Pizza sign at the Shelley branch was destroyed and knocked over in the wind.   Several trees were split or blown over in Idaho Falls.   A tractor blew over due to cross winds on US Route 20 northeast of St Anthony.
A strong cold front brought significant winds with 60 mph measured 5 miles north of Owinza and 59 mph in Richfield.

Strong winds occurred in the Snake River Plain behind a cold front with 62 mph measured 3 miles west of Taber and 58 mph recorded at the Pocatello Regional Airport ASOS site.  Extensive minor tree and out building and fence structure damage also occurred.

A strong cold front brought extremely strong winds to the Arco and Mud Lake Desert region.   Big Southern Butte recorded 73 mph with 67 mph at Craters of the Moon and 60 mph at Cox's Well with Idaho National Laboratory sites recording 50 to 60 mph gusts as well.
A 61 mph wind gust was measured 1 mile east northeast of Howe during a day with several hours of 50 to 60 mph gusts behind a cold frontal passage.
Strong winds occurred with a cold frontal passage with 59 mph recorded in Niter and widespread 45 to 55 mph gusts at Grace and Soda Springs.
A boy scout cabin was destroyed in Island Park due to extremely strong winds associated with a cold frontal passage.

Extremely strong cross winds contributed to a pickup pulling a 28 foot trailer to overturn on southbound Interstate 15 near milepost 29 south of Downey.   The trailer blew over after the pickup and trailer jack-knifed.    The interstate was completely blocked for 40 minutes and was partially blocked for an additional hour and 20 minutes.   The crash occurred at around 4:15 PM MDT.
A thunderstorm outflow wind of 58 mph was measured 12 miles northwest of Atomic City at the INL Reactor Tech Complex.
The Kettle Butte site on US Route 20 recorded a thunderstorm outflow wind gust of 58 mph.
A funnel cloud photographed near Dubois.

One to 2 inches of rain fell in Fremont County over a 48 hour period and caused extensive flooding.   A lot of flooding in the Rea area in the Yale Creek estates and Shotgun Complex areas north of Kilgore Yale Road.  Flooding reported at Island Park Village Golf Course.  Rushing water flooded private roads/driveways i Pine Crest area.   Red Rock Pass Road and Forest Service Road 58 washed out near Duck Creek.  Yale Creek flooded across S Beaver Sprigs Rd with damage to the road.
A 67 mph wind gust was recorded 6 miles southwest of Victor with about 1,200 customers losing power reported by Fall River Electric.  Tree damage was reported to have affected power lines.
Widespread 50 to 60 mph wind gusts occurred behind a cold front with a peak of 60 mph northwest of Atomic City.
A cold front brought 50 to 60 mph wind gusts to the Teton Valley with a 59 mph gust measured at Clementsville.
Widespread 50 to 60 mph wind gusts occurred with 55 mph measured at Atomic City and 57 mph southwest of Mud Lake.
A funnel cloud photographed just north and northwest of Tetonia.
A funnel cloud photographed west of Tetonia.
Over quarter sized hail was reported in Ammon with a photograph on social media.

A 2 story 5,000 square foot residence was struck by lightning causing a large fire.  It occurred 2 miles northeast of Iona along E. Panorama Dr.  A firefighter was injured in the fire.   An estimated 800,000 dollars worth of damage occurred to the home.
A thunderstorm outflow wind of 72 mph measured at the NOAA ARL Rover site.
A 62 mph wind gust measured at the INL Reactor Tech complex.
A 62 mph thunderstorm outflow wind gust measured at the Camas ITD site on interstate 15.
A 60 mph wind gust measured in Monteview.
A 59 mph thunderstorm outflow wind gust measured at Monteview.
A 59 mph thunderstorm outflow wind gust was measured at the Idaho Falls Regional airport ASOS site.
A 59 mph thunderstorm outflow wind measured at the Hamer ARL FRD site.
A 58 mph thunderstorm outflow wind gust measured at the Big Southern Butte mesonet site.
A 58 mph wind gust measured at the Materials Fuels Complex.
A 58 mph wind gust was measured at at the Telegraph Hill ITD site.
A lightning caused wildfire burned around 280 acres 8 miles south of Malta.   It began on July 12th and was controlled on July 14th.  No structures were threatened or damaged.
A 64 mph thunderstorm outflow wind measured north of Owinza.
A 58 mph thunderstorm outflow wind measured at Telegraph Hill ITD site.
One inch hail fell near Thunder Ridge High School.   Photograph provided.
A 61 mph wind gust from thunderstorm outflow measured at the Kettle Butte ITD site.
A 60 mph thunderstorm outflow wind was measured at the Rover ARL site.
Portion of tree downed by a thunderstorm wind in Shelley.
Large tree limbs downed on power lne on South Boulevard near E 23rd St in Idaho Falls.   Power outage for 1,400 customers reported by Idaho Power.
A 64 mph wind gust measured at the Canyon Creek mesonet site.
Thunderstorm winds felled a tree which fell on a power line starting a small wildfire.
A 68 mph thunderstorm outflow wind was recorded at the Ririe mesonet site.
The COOP observer in Bern estimated a 60 mph thunderstorm outflow wind.
Private weather station measured a 62 mph wind gust in Dubois at the intersection of Main St and Oakley Ave.
Moburg Canyon mesonet site recorded thunderstorm outflow wind gust of 65 mph.
Wires downed and debris in road due to wind damage in Chubbuck near intersection of Yellowstone Ave and Ward Dr.
A lightning strike nocked a portion of a large tree onto power lines taking them down and lit the tree on fire along Hawthorne Rd in Chubbuck.
Fall River Rural Electric reported several trees down on power lines just southwest of Macks Inn resulting in power outages.
The GRAI1 mesonet site recorded a 59 mph thunderstorms outflow wind.
A thunderstorm outflow wind of 66 mph measured on Idaho Highway 34 near Blackfoot River Rd.
A thunderstorm outflow wind gust of 63 mph was measured at the Monida Pass ITD mesonet site.
An 89 acre grass fire occurred near Lake Wolcott and Rupert.   No known cause was found and no structures were damaged.

A 265 acre wildfire began at about 1 am on July 23rd across from Century High School on the other side of South 5th Avenue.   The fire spread away from teh road to the northeast overnight in the early morning hours of the 23rd.  The fire was fully contained by 9 pm on July 24th.   No structural damage was reported.

At 8:45 PM MDT Clark County Fire Department and Camas Creek RFPA were dispatched to 4 fires.  they were along the east side of northbound land and in the median at mile marker 178 on Interstate 15 just south of Spencer.  It is believed fires were possibly sparked by someone changing a tire.   Northbound interstate 15 was closed for two hours until 11 pm MDT when one lane reopened.   The interstate had no restrictions after 1 M MDT on the 24th.
A large dust devil was video'd in Downey on July 29th and posted on facebook.
A 58 mph wind gust measured at private weather station at intersection of E 300 S and S 450 E.
A large tree was blown down near a wooden fence near the cozy coffee in Heyburn.   Other large tree limbs reported down.
Fence destroyed near intersection of S 300 W and W 50 Rd S near Rupert.
A tree fell onto a Minivan near Rupert.
The public reported multiple trees downed in the city of Rupert.
Seven large trees were blown down with some uprooted at the Rupert Country Club.   Some were as large as two feet in diameter.
Several trees were downed at the Teton County Courthouse in Driggs.   One tree took down a light pole.
Quarter sized hail photographed near Irwin.
Spotter reported 1 inch hail just south of Irwin.

Several reports of rainfall in the 0.80 to just over an inch range from about 4 pm MDT to 5:30 pm MDT caused extensive nuisance street and parking lot flooding in the Idaho Falls area.   One foot of water was reported across the intersection of Druvor St and Lowell Dr.  Flooding was reported near Albertsons at the intersection of E 17th St and S Holmes Ave.  Many reports of street and parking lot flooding in the Ammon area.  The intersection of Austin Ave and 12 St was flooded.  Parking lot flooding up to 1 foot deep in the plaza including TJ Max.  Areas of water were 1 to 2 feet deep in the Grand Teton Mall parking lot and over the bottoms of some vehicles.  Ashment Ave flooded north of E 17th St and there was flooding in business parking lots along S 25th E including across the street from Target.
A 326 acre wildfire west of the Pocatello airport began on August 10th and was contained by 8 pm.

The Ross Fork wildfire was reported during the afternoon of August 9th northeast of Pocatello near the intersection of Ross Fork and Ross Fork Creek roads   It was a grass fire that several fire agencies assisted on.  It grew to 6,400 acres and high winds caused it to jump lines.   Residents were evacuated from Ross Fork Creek Road on the 11th.  After several bouts of losing control the fire was contained and only one outbuilding was destroyed.   Several homes were not damaged.   Containment occurred on August 11th by 6 pm.
A 60 mph thunderstorm outflow wind was measured at the INL Specific Manufacturing site.

Flash flooding occurred north of Roy due to an inch of rain.  Minor road damage on Lawery Lane with the South Fork Rock Creek and Simms Rd  showing damage.   Debris was reported across Idaho route 37 by a local farmer.   A basement also was reported flooded.
Evidence of flash flooding across Hess Road northeast of Holbrook with minor residual damage.

One to 3 inches of heavy rain fell in much of Fremont County causing extensive flooding.  15 people were stranded east/southeast of Macks Inn along the Henry's fork River between Big Springs and Macks Inn due to the rain.   Many were suffering hypothermia and were treated on scene.  Multiple private roads on the Ashton Hill were washing out.  A running track was flooded at North Fremont High School.   Moving water was filmed across fields and roads in the area of N 3700 E and E 1400 N.  Crops and fields suffered damage in the Marysville area.  Several sections of the Ashton-Tetonia Rail Trail were flooded, washed out and covered in mud.  3 cabins reported flooded north northwest of Squirrel.  The Henrys Fork River rose one half foot between 5:45 Pm MDT and 9 PM MDT.
A brush fire began August 16th 5 miles northwest of Carey and grew to 650 acres.  Farms and homes were threatened but no damages were reported.  The wildfire was actively controlled on August 19th.
INL Naval Reactor mesonet site measured a 58 mph wind gust.
The Rover mesonet site 9 miles south southwest of Mud Lake recorded a 59 mph thunderstorm outflow wind gust.

The Ross Fark wildfire began in Camas County August 14th and spread into Blaine and Custer Counties in late August into early September.   It was timber litter, timber and short grass that fueled the fire.  By September 4th the fire expanded from 3 thousand acres to over 5 thousand acres.  Blaine County Sherriff's office issued a mandatory evacuation notice on September 4th for the Sawtooth City, Smiley Creek, Lake Alturas, and the Beaver Creek areas in the Stanley Basin all cabins and campgrounds.   State Highway 75 was shut down 5 miles south and north of Smiley Creek.  A disaster declaration was declared on September 6th by Blaine County.  The fire had grown to 14 thousand acres by September 6th.  Local engines from Ketchum, Sun Valley, Hailey, Wood River Fire and Rescue and Bellevue were assigned to protect buildings around Smiley Creek and Alturas Lake. on September 5th.   By the 7th the fire had run to and across highway 75.  By the 7th   Type 2 team was assigned.  Two structures were burned down.  By September 7th the following access to lakes and drainages were closed:  Pettit Lake and Trailhead, Yellowbelly Lake, Pole Creek, Upper Salmon River Headwaters, Frenchman Creek, and Alturas Lake.  Air quality became very unhealthy in Smiley Creek, Haily and Ketchum due to the smoke from the fire.  FEMA authorized federal funds to help with firefighting costs which neared 6 million dollars.  The fire grew to over 31 thousand acres by the 8th with much of the fire growth caused by high winds.  Highway 75 remained closed between mile markers 146 and 172.  By September10th the fire caused Galena Lodge to be closed for the season due to the fire as it reached over 35 thousand acres.  By mid September the fire reached close to 38 thousand acres and stopped growing and was 64 percent contained by the end of the month and closures were greatly reduced.
A 61 mph wind gust was measured at the Clementsville ITD site.   Several sites reported over 40 mph wind gusts.

A strong cold front brought the following winds to the Arco Mud Lake Desert:  5 miles WSW Craters of the Moon 59 mph, 1 mile NNW Craters of the Moon 57 mph, Sand Dunes 57 mph, 6 miles NW Atomic City 57 mph, INL Materials Fuels Complex 56 mph, 9 miles SSW Mud Lake 54 mph, 14 miles ENE Atomic City 53 mph, Lost River Rest Area 53 mph, INL Critical Infrastructure 53 mph, INL Reactor Teck Complex 52 mph, big Southern Butte 52 mph, Atomic City 51 mph, INL Radioactive Waste Mngmt 51 mph.
A small greenhouse was destroyed at Farnsworth Middle School just west of Rigby.  Jefferson County Emergency Management reported the damage.
A 65 mph wind gust was measured at the Rigby agrimet site RGBI.
One inch hail reported by trained spotter in Swan Valley.
Power lines were reported down with damage to power pole in Victor.
The Timmerman Hill ITD site measured a 59 mph thunderstorm outflow gust.
The agrimet station RPTI1 recorded a 58 mph wind gust.
A 58 mph wind gust measured at Ohio Gulch RAWS.
A 61 mph gust measured at the Dead Man Canyon FRD site.
A 68 mph wind gust measured at the ITD INL Puzzle site.
A 59 mph gust measured at Pilot Gold.
The Raft River RAWS measured a 73 mph wind gust.
Several large trees damaged with a few down along East Fork or Rock Creek east, southeast of Rockland.
A funnel cloud reported south of Pocatello near the Portneuf gap.

Extensive street and road flooding occurred on the evening of the 21st in the Pocatello/Chubbuck area as rains in excess of a half inch fell.  The intersection of East Oak St and Yellowstone Ave flooded.  The Center Street Underpass accumulated 18 to 24 inches of water.  Flooding at N 3rd Ave and E Fremont St affected a business.  Hawthorne Rd flooded with deep water at the interstate 86 underpass and was closed from 830 pm to 10 pm MDT.  US Route 30 also closed between Hawthorne Rd and W Cedar St.
The Gas Caves RAWS recorded a 58 mph wind gust.

The Sawtell Peak Fire began August 31st but was contained on September 9th and burned only 37 acres but 66 personnel were assigned to the fire and strong winds threatened Island Park but it was contained with no damages.

A fire began on September 4th in the Morgan's Bridge area of eastern Bingham County and reached 1,300 acres and was fully contained on September 6th.  The fire threatened power lines but no homes or structures.

A fire ignited north of Chubbuck at 1:45 MDT September 8th on BLM land.  It spread to the Fort Hall Indian Reservation and private land.  Some structures were threatened and led to some evacuations on the reservation.  Portions of Ross Fork Road and 2 and a half mile road were closed on Thursday the 8th.   The fire reached 8,700 acres and was fully contained on September 11th.  No structures ended up damaged and no injuries occurred.

The Pocatello ASOS at the airport recorded the hottest September temperatures ever recorded with 102 degrees on the 3rd.   Two other days reached 100 degrees and 5 record highs were recorded during the month.

The ASOS at the Idaho Falls regional airport recorded it's hottest September temperatures at 100 degrees on the 3rd.    It was the first ever 100 degree September temperatures recorded in Idaho Falls.   Six record high temperatures were recorded during the month.

The ASOS at the Burley municipal airport recorded it's hottest September ever with 101 degrees on September 6th which was the 1st ever 100 degree or hotter temperatures ever recorded in the month.   Three record high temperatures were recorded for the month.
The ASOS at Challis recorded the hottest September ever with 99 degrees recorded on September 3rd.   Five record high temperatures were recorded during the month.

The Sand Dunes mesonet site recorded a 64 mph gust at 605 PM MDT on the 21st.   59 mph gusts measured at Rover and Craters of the Moon mesonet sites.   Very strong winds continue through the morning of the 22nd with several more gusts in the 50 to 60 mph range.

Extensive blowing dust reduced visibility to near zero north of Idaho Falls on interstate 15 and it closed from exit number 128 to 135 at 248 PM MDT and was reopened before midnight.    Wind gusts in the region were extensive in the 50 to 55 mph range with the peak 56 mph at Kettle Butte.
A 59 mph wind gust was measured at Dead Man Canyon at 545 PM MDT.   Several gusts in the 50 to 56 mph range were also recorded.

An early spring snowstorm brought heavy snow to the Snake River Plain. Early morning snowfall totals were 5 inches at the Pocatello airport and Fort Hall. Six to 7 inches fell in Chubbuck with 6 to 8 inches on the Pocatello benches at elevations above 5,000 feet.
A strong wind gust destoryed a chimney on a roof of a home in St Anthony.
Sustained winds of 52 mph were measured in Minidoka with gusts to 67 mph.  Sustained winds of 40 mph occurred in Rupert with gusts to 61 mph.
Wind speeds of 47 mph with gusts to 56 mph were recorded at the Pocatello ASOS.  Sustained winds of 39 mph with gusts to 53 mph were recorded at Fort Hall.

Sustained winds of 47 mph with gusts to 71 mph were measured 20 miles southwest of Malta.  Sustained winds of 46 mph with gusts of 57 mph were recorded in Albion.  And sustained winds of 44 mph with gusts to 54 mph were recorded 20 miles southwest of American Falls.

A 70 mph wind gust was measured in Rexburg.  A 65 mph wind gust was measured in Rigby.  A 69 mph wind gust was measured 15 miles southeast of Arco.  Interstate 15 was closed north of Idaho Falls.  40 mph sustained winds were recorded 8 miles west of Blackfoot.  A wind gust of 60 mph was measured 20 miles west of Idaho Falls.
Sustained winds of 45 mph with gusts to 60 mph were measured in Bern.
One inch hail reported near Roy.

Twenty-seven power poles were knocked down with Rocky Mountain Power reporting 1,500 customers without power very early on November 2nd with the Idaho Falls airport reporting a 74 mph wind gust at 1:30 AM MDT.   Much of the damage was in the Idaho Falls and Shelley area as well as the power outages.  Most gusts were in the 45 to 55 mph range with a couple exceeding 60 mph.

A 66 mph wind gust was measured at the Pocatello Regional airport at 12:42 AM MDT on the 2nd.  Idaho Power reported 314 customers without power early morning on the 2nd in the Pocatello area with power restored by 10 AM.

A 60 mph wind gust was measured near Niter at 3 AM MDT on the 2nd.
Sixty to 65 mph wind gusts were measured at the intersection of US Highways 20 and 26 as well as Big Southern Butte.  These occurred between 12 Midnight and 2 AM MDT on the 2nd.
Extensive wind gusts over 60 mph occurred during the morning of the 5th mostly between 5 AM and noon.   The peak of 72 mph occurred at the Rover mesonet southwest of Mud Lake.

On the morning of the 5th a strong cold front brought many gusts over 60 mph to the Upper snake River Plain including 62 mph at the Rexburg airport and 58 mph at the Idaho Falls airport.  Interstate 15 closed north of Idaho Falls at around 1245 PM MDT due to blowing dust and reduced visibility.

A 62 mph wind gust was measured at Taber with several gusts over 50 mph recorded.

The Medicine Lodge mesonet site measured a 79 mph wind gust.

The Franklin Basin SNOTEL site measured an estimated 12.5 inches of snowfall and the Emigrant Summit site 5.6 inches.

The first heavy snowfall of the season fell in the Centennial Mountains.  An estimated 22 inches of snow fell at the White Elephant SNOTEL site with 11.3 inches at the Island Park SNOTEL.   The Island Park COOP observer recorded 8.2 inches of snow with 6 inches near Macks Inn.
The Vienna Mine SNOTEL site received an estimated 13.2 inches of snow.   The Stanley Ranger Station COOP site measured 4 inches.
One to 3 inches of snow fell in the Ashton region with wind gusts over 30 mph created hazardous driving conditions with 7 slide offs and 3 crashes reported.

Just before 3 pm a pickup truck crashed into a semi tractor trailer and both individuals in the pickup truck died due to the accident.   One individual in the semi was airlifted to a local hospital with injuries.  The accident occurred 1 mile south of Macks Inn on US Highway 20.  Small hail accumulating to 3 to 4 inches in a 30 minute time frame was believed to be a significant contributing factor in the accident according to Idaho State Police.   The Highway was shut down for 4 hours due to the accident.
Wind gusts were widespread 50 to 70 mph on the 19th as a cold front moved through the Raft River Region.   A peak of 67 mph was measured near Idahome.

A strong cold front changed rain to snow and combined with strong winds to bring power outages reported by Idaho Power for over 1,500 people in Power, Bingham and Bannock Counties in the Aberdeen, Crystal and Pocatello areas.  A total of 2 to 5 inches of snow fell in the Pocatello and American Falls region.
One foot of snow measured in Albion with 6 inches 5 miles west southwest of Almo.

Ten to 12 inches of snow fell in the Shoshone area with 6 inches in Richfield and 5 inches in Dietrich.   Idaho Power reported power outages in Shoshone, Richfield and Dietrich due to the heavy wet snow and strong winds.

Heavy snow fell on Thanksgiving with 11.5 inches 4 miles east southeast of American Falls, 8 inches in Aberdeen, and 5 to 7 inches in the Pocatello and Chubbuck area.   Idaho Power due to the heavy snow and wind reported power outages in Aberdeen, Springfield, Moreland, Pingree, and Blackfoot on Thanksgiving night.

Extremely heavy snow fell in the Eastern Magic Valley over the Thanksgiving holiday.   Reported amounts were 10 to 13 inches in Burley, 13 inches in Declo, 14 inches in Paul and Rupert, and 16 to 18 inches in Heyburn.   Some damage occurred due to the extremely heavy snow.   A pine tree snapped off in Declo, a tarp and metal gazebo collapsed at a private residence in Burley and large tree limbs also downed in Burley.

Localized dense fog developed on interstate 86 just east of Pocatello to the Pocatello airport exit and a 30 vehicle crash occurred with multiple injuries and one death involved.   Visibility was under one quarter mile at the Pocatello airport ASOS at the time and Idaho State Patrol determined fog was a contributing factor.  The interstate was closed east bound at the crash site for over 7 hours.

A total of 32 inches of snow was measured by a spotter 4 miles west of Victor.   A foot  was measured at 8 pm on the first and it kept adding up through the morning of the 4th.  An estimated 24 inches fell at the Pine Creek Pass SNOTEL site through December 3rd.  11.5 inches was measured 3 miles north of Victor by another trained spotter.
An estimated 32 inches of snow fell at Bostetter Ranger Station and 51 inches at Howell Canyon SNOTEL sites.

Two to 3 inches of snow fell in Rexburg and Idaho Falls and law enforcement reported multiple slide offs and accidents on US Highway 20 just south of Rexburg on the morning of the 1st.  Slick roads were the likely cause of many of the accidents.

An estimated 26 inches of snow fell at the Sedgwick Peak SNOTEL and 17 inches at Wildhorse Divide.  10.4 inches of snow fell 5 miles north of Inkom.  16.5 inches of snow was measured 3 miles north northwest of Lava Hot Springs and 11 inches in Inkom with 10.9 inches measured at McCammon.
A total of 31 inches of snow was estimated at the Oxford Springs SNOTEL site.
An estimated 35 inches of snow fell at the Emigrant Summit and Franklin Basin SNOTEL sites.
An estimated 11 inches of snow fell at the Giveout SNOTEL site with 21 inches at Slug Creek Divide and 16 inches at Somsen Ranch.  7.5 inches was measured at a Soda Springs site.

An estimated 11 inches of snow fell at the Mill Creek Summit SNOTEL site.

The following snowfall amounts were estimated at SNOTEL sites:  Bear Canyon 15.6 inches, Garfield Ranger Station 22.5 inches, Smiley Mountain 13.5 inches, and Stickney Mill 11.7 inches.

A two vehicle collision resulted in the death of one of the passengers.  Idaho State Police investigaed a vehicle fatality collision which occurred on Monday, December 4, 2023, at 7:05 A.M. on State Highway 33 at mile marker 57 east of Terreton.||A 2008 Chevrolet Silverado was traveling eastbound on SH33. A 2018 Volvo semi-truck hauling a trailer was traveling westbound on SH33. The Chevrolet crossed the center line where it struck the Volvo head on.||The driver of the Chevrolet, a 23-year-old-man from Terreton, was not wearing a seatbelt and succumbed to his injures at scene. The driver of the semi-truck, a 24-year-old-man from Louisville, KY, was wearing a seatbelt and was transported to a local hospital.  Slick roads were thought to be a contributing factor.
A total of 13.5 inches of snow was measured by the Bern COOP observer with 8 inches on the 3rd.

Heavy snow and strong winds brought snow squall conditions from 8 to 9 am in Pocatello and Chubbuck with wind gusts 30 to 40 mph and visibility under one quarter mile in heavy snow.   3.6 inches of snow fell at the Pocatello Regional Airport with 6 to 8 inches in Chubbuck, Fort Hall and Pocatello.  There was a department of Highways report of around 12 inches in Pocatello.  Multiple vehicle rollovers and many accidents were reported along interstate 15 near Fort Hall as well with the heavy snow and winds.
Heavy snow fell with strong winds gusting to 40 mph.  13.5 inches of snow was measured 3 miles north northwest of Lava Hot Springs with 8.8 inches 6 miles north of Inkom and 8 inches in Inkom.

An estimated 11 inches of snow was recorded at the Emigrant Summit and Franklin Basin SNOTEL sites.  A semi tractor trailer jackknifed on state Highway 36 near Emigration Summit along with other slide offs were reported and the highway closed around 8 AM.

Six inches of snow was recorded 3 miles north northeast of Driggs and wind gusts of 30 to 40 mph caused slick roads in Idaho Highway 32 causing a slide off of a large oversized load 2 miles northwest of Judkins.
Nine inches of snow was measured in Bern by the COOP observer.

A multi  vehicle accident occurred on interstate 84 north of North Pine closing the eastbound lane with snow and winds thought to be a factor in the accidents.  Winds were gusting to over 50 mph at times.
About 1 to 2 inches of snow fell causing hazardous roads and black ice.   Jefferson County School District 251 delayed opening by 2 hours due to the hazardous roads.
About 1 to 2 inches of snow fell causing hazardous roads and black ice.   Jefferson County School District 251 delayed opening by 2 hours due to the hazardous roads.

A multi vehicle crash occurred at around 740 AM near mile marker 89 near Blackfoot on interstate 15 that backed up traffic for miles.  It was suspected freezing fog and black ice may have played a role in the accidents.  The interstate was shut down for two hours and it was not until 10 AM that everything was cleared out.

Dense fog contributed to several crashes on interstate 86 near mile marker 55 west of Pocatello.  Nine crashes occurred in both the east and west bound lanes at around 930 AM and the interstate didn't re open until 345 PM.  Some vehicles caught on fire and up to 10 injuries occurred.

A couple of inches of snow combined with 50 to 65 mph wind gusts caused interstate 84 to be closed from 633 AM to 849 AM near mile marker 258 in the Sweetser Summit area due to an issue with a semi.  At 946 AM an 18 wheeler was blown over on interstate 84 near mile marker 229 south of Yale Road.  Visibility between 1/4 and 1/2 mile occurred from 2 AM to 315 AM northwest of Idahome on the interstate.

Two to 4 inches of snow fell and combined with strong winds to create hazardous travel.  Rocky Mountain Power reported 400 customers without power by 530 AM due to the winds and snow in the Ashton area and north.  A jackknifed semi trailer occurred on US Highway 20 just north of Idaho Highway 87 blocking the road at 909 AM.  Fremont County reported numerous crashes and slide offs in the Island Park area.

One to 4 inches of snowfall combined with strong winds to cause hazardous travel and power outages in the region.  Close to 300 customers were reported without power in the Menan area.  Fremont County emergency manager reported minor injuries from a vehicle rollover west of St Anthony.

A national weather service employee reported 6.1 inches of snow in Moreland and another 5.8 inches in Blackfoot.   Amounts were lighter further south with 1 to 2 inches in Pocatello and American Falls.
Localized heavy snow fell with the COOP observer in Rigby measuring 6 inches with 5 inches in Rexburg and 3.5 inches at KIFI in Idaho Falls.

Snow squalls were widespread between 2 pm and 4 pm with widespread wind gusts 55 to 70 mph verified with visibility near zero.   5.5 to 6 inches of snow was measured in Rupert.   Trees were downed south of Burley with one of the squalls.  Tree limbs were snapped off in Rupert.  The Burley airport reported a 66 mph gust with lightning and 1/4 mile visibility.  Idaho Power reported 7 thousand customers lost power 12 miles west of Burley and near Minidoka and Acequia.
Snow and wind causing low visibility caused a multi-vehicle accident on US Highway 30 north of Grace at 240 PM MST.  It caused the highway to be closed between Lava Hot Springs and Soda Springs.

Snow and wind causing low visibility caused a multi-vehicle accident on US Highway 30 north of Grace at 240 PM MST. It caused the highway to be closed between Lava Hot Springs and Soda Springs.  50 to 60 mph wind gusts were widespread.
A 64 mph wind gust was measured in a snow squall in Albion with 78 mph gusts measured at Cotton Ridge.   Whiteout conditions occurred in Albion.
Wind gusts of 45 to 70 mph were widespread with heavy snow and snow squalls were reported at:  Yale, Idahome, Moburg Canyon, and Sweetzer Summit with visibility below 1/4 of a mile.

Whiteout conditions were reported in Aberdeen, Fort Hall and at the Pocatello airport due to heavy snow and wind gusts of 35 to 50 mph.   0.25 miles visibility was recorded at the Pocatello airport with a 37 mph wind gust.  The snow squalls occurred from 3 to 4 pm MST.
A 58 mph wind gust was measured at Clementsville.  Snow combined with strong winds closed Idaho Highway 33 from Ashton to Tetonia and Idaho Highway 47 from Ashton to Warm River.
Snow and strong winds closed Idaho Highway 47 from Ashton to north of Warm River.  Island Park measured 7 inches of snow on the 8th and 9th.
A school but was hit by a pickup truck and slid into a ditch near Teton Lakes Golf Course in Rexburg.  No injuries occurred.  The town of Parker recorded 7 inches of snow.
A trained spotter measured 8.0 inches of snow 4 miles west of Victor.

Wind gusts of 35 to 65 mph occurred all day and evening in the Bear Lake Valley.  Blizzard conditions were met at the Bear Lake County airport, Emigration Canyon, Bloomington, Bern, Ovid, and Montpelier.   6 inches of snow was measured at Bern.  Road closures were the following:  State Highways 36,32, and 33 as well as US Highway 89 from Montpelier to the Utah border.

The Teton valley had blizzard conditions for the entire morning of the 12th for over 8 hours at the Botts mesonet site with visibility below a quarter mile and winds gusting in the 50 to 60 mph range.  The heavy snow and wind gusts closed both Idaho State Highways 32 and 33 due to the blowing and drifting snow and near zero visibility. Teton County School District 401 was closed for the day.

The Ririe RWIS site met blizzard conditions with over 4 hours of visibility below 1/4 mile with wind gusts 50 to 60 mph.   It had a peak gust of 61 mph at 500 AM MST.  Gusts of 45 to 55 mph were common at other sites throughout the Snake River Plain.  US Highway 26 was closed due to the winds and snow causing drifting snow.  The following schools closed due to the snow, wind and blowing snow:  Idaho Falls District 91, Bonneville Joint District 93, Sugar Salem District 322, and Ririe District 252.

Visibility below 1/4 mile with 30 to 40 mph wind gusts occurred 5 miles west southwest of Victor at the RWIS site on State Highway 31.   The highway was shut down due to the blowing and drifting snow.   A spotter measured 12.8 inches of snowfall 4 miles west of Victor.  Teton School District 401 was closed due to the blizzard.

The Blackfoot River Bridge had visibility at or below 1/4 mile for 3 hours at the RWIS site.  45 to 55 mph wind gusts were widespread throughout the Blackfoot Mountains the entire day.  3 to 5 inches of snow fell and the snow and blowing and drifting snow closed State Highway 34.  The Bone COOP site measured 4 inches of snow.  The Antelope Flats RWIS site carried visibility below 1/4 mile for 6 hours.  State Highway 26 closed due to the blowing and drifting conditions.

Heavy snow and low visibility of 1/4 mile or less led to the closing of US Highway 93 south of Shoshone.  It also closed State Highway 75 north of Shoshone to Timmerman Hill.  Blaine County Schools were closed for the day due to the blizzard.

Three hours plus of 1/4 mile visibility or less and 2 to 4 inches of snow causing extensive blowing and drifting closed State Highway 75 north of Shoshone to Timmerman Hill.  Blaine County Schools were closed due to the blizzard.

Wind gusts for several hours in the 50 to 60 mph range with snow amounts of 1 to 3 inches caused dangerous road conditions and the West Jefferson School District 253 closed schools for the day due to blowing and drifting snow.

A strong cold front brought strong winds with gusts 45 to 55 mph widespread throughout the day with occasional blizzard conditions with visibility under 1/4 mile but lasting for under one hour for the most part through the morning.  Snowfall generally ranged in the 1 to 3 inch range from Aberdeen to American Falls to Pocatello/Chubbuck.  The road conditions caused Pocatello/Chubbuck School district 25 to close as well as Idaho State University.

A winter storm with snow and high winds caused dangerous road conditions and road closures.  State Highway 34 closed from Conda to the Wyoming border.  State Highway 36 closed from the State Highway 34 intersection to Ovid.   Snowfall amounts were in the 2 to 4 inch range with the COOP observer in Preston measuring 3 inches.

A strong cold front brought a combination of snow and strong winds with gusts of 40 to 50 mph.   Island Park COOP site measured 7 inches of snowfall.  Idaho State Highway 47 was closed due to blowing and drifting snow from Ashton to Bear Gulch.

Blizzard conditions closed State Highway 31 from Swan Valley to Victor and US Highway 26 from Ririe to Swan Valley.   3 inches of snow fell in Swan Valley and the Wan Valley School District 92 closed due to road conditions and extensive blowing and drifting snow in 45 to 55 mph wind gusts and occasional blizzard conditions.

Teton County Idaho Search and Rescue reported a skier was badly injured in an avalanche that occurred between Idaho Highway 33 and Mount Oliver.  23 team members responded including three K9 teams.  Patient was found and transported via ambulance with significant upper extremity, facial injuries and head trauma.
Widespread 50 to 60 mph wind gusts combined with 1 to 3 inches of snow caused extensive blowing and drifting snow and difficult travel.

Extreme winter weather occurred with 50 to 60 mph wind gusts causing blowing and drifting snow with a trained spotter in Acequia measuring 3 inches.  Extensive blowing and drifting snow caused difficult travel conditions.
Wind gusts of 50 to 60 mph combined with snowfall created extensive blowing and drifting snow and the trained spotter in Almo measured 4 inches of snow.
Snow with wind gusts of 50 to 60 mph caused State Highway 36 to close from the intersection with State Highway 34 to Ovid.
Wind gusts of 60 to 70 mph combined with light snow caused extensive blowing and drifting snow.
Nearly 6 inches of snow fell at the Pocatello Regional Airport (5.8 inches).   7 inches fell in Aberdeen with 6 inches at American Falls and 4.5 inches in downtown Pocatello.

Heavy snow fell in the Eastern Magic Valley on the 13th and 14th with the following snow amounts measured:  Minidoka 4.6 inches, Oakley 8.0 inches, Acequia 7.5 inches, Rupert 9.0 inches, and Burley 5.5 inches.
The COOP observer in Bern measured 9 inches of snow and 6.5 inches fell in Montpelier.
Measured snow amounts were the following:  Downey 6.0 inches, Inkom 6.0 inches, and 3 miles north northwest of Lava Hot Springs 9.0 inches.
Significant snowfall measured by COOP observers were 6.5 inches at Preston and 6.0 inches at Malad City.

Interstate 84 was closed from the intersection of interstate 86 to the Juniper Rest Area due to blowing and drifting snow and 40 to 60 mph wind gusts.  It was closed overnight on the 14th into the 15th and through the morning.

Wind gusts of 40 to 60 mph caused extensive blowing and drifting of snow and caused Idaho Highway 77 to be closed in sections including in the Elba and Almo areas.  Idaho Highway 81 was also closed from Declo to Malta.
A spotter measured 14.5 inches of snow 4 miles west of Victor.
The Inkom COOP observer measured 9 inches of snow.
COOP observers measured 8 inches of snow at Bern and 4 inches east of St Charles.
The Preston COOP observer measured 5.9 inches of snow.
The COOP observer in Bone measured 7.0 inches of snowfall.

An avalanche spilled across State Highway 75 at Galena Summit forcing the road to be closed on the morning of the 18th through about 315 Pm MST.  It was closed from Ketchum to Stanley from milepost 145 to 165.  4 inches of snow had fallen in Ketchum.

An avalanche spilled across State Highway 75 at Galena Summit forcing the road to be closed on the morning of the 18th through about 315 PM MST.  It was closed from Ketchum to Stanley from milepost 145 to 165.  The Stanley COOP observer measured 6.4 inches of snowfall prior to the event.

US Highway 26 closed from Ririe to Swan Valley from 1207 AM MST to 1057 AM MST on the 18th.   Wind gusts of 40 to 50 mph combined with snowfall as the Swan Valley COOP observer reported 4.0 inches caused extensive blowing and drifting snow and near impossible snow removal.

US Highway 26 closed from Ririe to Swan Valley from 1207 AM MST to 1057 AM MST on the 18th.   Wind gusts of 40 to 50 mph combined with snowfall caused extensive blowing and drifting snow and near impossible snow removal.   Snowfall reports were generally 1 to 3 inches with the event.
Black ice caused multiple crashes on interstate 15 between Chubbuck and Blackfoot in both directions including near the Fort Hall exit due to the black ice.  The cause was freezing fog and drizzle.

Iced over roads and black ice reported on Idaho Highway 75 between Hailey and Bellevue with multiple spinouts and slide offs near the Woodside Boulevard intersection.  Freezing fog and drizzle caused the black ice.
SNOTEL site at Sedgwick Peak estimated 14.3 inches of snow around 48 hours.
SNOTEL snow estimates for the system were Emigrant Summit at 18.7 inches and Franklin Basin at 11.9 inches.

Heavy snow amounts estimated by SNOTEL were 12.9 inches at Crab Creek, 13.2 inches at Island Park and 22.6 inches at White Elephant.  The Island Park COOP site totaled 14.5 inches.  The public reported 13 inches of snowfall in Warm River.
Estimated snow amounts from SNOTEL sites were Dollarhide Summit 16.1 inches and Galena Summit 13.7 inches.  The COOP observer in Ketchum measured 13 inches.
Locally heavy snow in northern parts of the Lower Snake River Plain.   5 inches fell in Firth and 6 inches in Moreland.
A trained spotter in the town of Dickey recorded 12 inches of snowfall.
A semi truck rolled over on interstate 86 on east bound interstate 86 at mile marker 27.1 near American Falls.  It blocked both east bound lanes.
A semi trailer jackknifed on interstate 86 eastbound near Yale Road blocking all eastbound lanes.  The road was snow covered as shown by area webcams.
A spotter measured 15.1 inches of snow 4 miles west of Victor over a two day period with the Pine Creek Pass SNOTEL site carrying an estimated 13.8 inches.
SNOTEL snowfall estimates were 11.3 inches at Bostetter Ranger Station and 13.2 inches at Howell Canyon.
The Sedgwick Peak SNOTEL had an estimated 16.3 inches of snow.
Estimated SNOTEL snow amounts were 18.6 inches at Emigrant Summit and 20.7 inches at Franklin Basin.
The public measured 9.1 inches of snowfall at Driggs.
The snowfall estimate at the White Elephant SNOTEL was 13.8 inches.  The Island Park COOP observer measured 7.6 inches and 6 inches fell at Macks Inn.
An estimated 14.9 inches of snow fell at the Mill Creek Summit SNOTEL site.
An estimate of 26.2 inches fell at the Vienna Mine SNOTEL site.

SOJTEL snow estimates were:  10.1 inches at Chocolate Gulch, 13.3 inches at Dollarhide Summit, 12.8 inches at Galena, and 14.3 inches at Galena Summit.  Lost Wood Divide estimated 14.8 inches.   The Ketchum COOP observer measured 8 inches of snowfall.
Significant snowfall fell in the Wood River foothills.   Amounts were 6-7 inches in Bellevue, 6-7 inches in Hailey, and 6 inches in Picabo.

Significant snowfall fell in the Pocatello/Chubbuck area in the morning with measured amounts of 3 to 5 inches which all fell in a 3 and a half hour period.  For that period snow was falling at a rate of an inch or slightly higher than an inch per hour.  Roads became snow and slush covered with a NWS employee witnessing several slide offs in the south part of town.
US 89 reported snow covered and slick with several slide offs by 8 am.    8.1 inches of snow were measured in Paris.
Snowfall created hazardous road conditions with a collision on US 91 between Franklin and Preston involving 1 semi and 1 car and one lane blocked at 9 am.

Widespread 50 to 60 mph wind gusts caused whiteout conditions on eastbound State Highway 33 from Newdale to Tetonia.  Several crashes occurred including a 7 vehicle one that closed State Highway between Newdale and Tetonia at 230 PM MST.  There were multiple jackknifed semi trailers.  The crashes blocked the road for three and a half hours.  rocky Mountain Power reported 120 customers without power due to wind in Idaho Falls.

Wind gusts of 50 to 60 mph were widespread and caused whiteout conditions with several accidents on State Highway 33 from Newdale to Tetonia.   Multiple semi trailers jackknifed.  7 inches of snow was reported to have fallen in Driggs with the storm.  State Highway 32 was closed from Ashton to Tetonia due to whiteout conditions as well with blowing and drifting snow.
About 70 customers without power reported by Fall River Electric cooperative in the Island Park area as 60 to 70 mph wind gusts were measured.

Fifty to 60 mph wind gusts were widespread and 1 to 3 inches of wet snow also fell and contributed to a power line downed in Chubbuck and Yellowstone road was blocked between Linden and Chubbuck Road at around 420 PM.  Idaho Power reported about 120 customers were without power.
Fifty to 65 mph wind gusts were widespread in the Arco and Mud Lake Desert regions.
Widespread 55 to 70 mph wind gusts were recorded at several mesonet sites behind the passage of a strong cold front.
Fifty to 65 mph wind gusts were widespread behind a cold front with 61 mph measured at the Burley Municipal Airport.
Widespread 50 to 60 mph wind gusts occurred behind a cold frontal passage with widespread blowing and drifting snow causing whiteouts on roads.

A very powerful storm brought a combination of heavy wet snow and strong winds to cause extensive damage the first 4 days of March.  Snow amounts ranged from 10 to 18 inches with the majority falling on the 1st and 2nd.   A cold front early on the 2nd brought 40 to 60 mph wind gusts and combined with the heavy snow to cause extensive tree damage with many trees downed.   Power outages reported by Idaho Power and Rocky Mountain Power numbered over 50 thousand customers from Firth to Blackfoot to American Falls to Pocatello.  Several reports of downed power lines in Blackfoot, and Pocatello.   Fifteen power poles snapped off along US Highway 91 between Blackfoot and Fort Hall.  Several accidents on interstate 15 on the 2nd and interstate 86 as well along the interstate 15 south bound ramp with several vehicles damaged.   Snow and wind continued on the 3rd and 4th as temperatures were much colder and blowing and drifting snow across roadways were a bigger problem.   Due to snow and wind the following schools closed on the 4th:  Snake River District 52, Blackfoot District 55, Firth District 59, Aberdeen District 58, Pocatello/Chubbuck District 25, American Falls District 381, and Idaho State University.    The two day precipitation total of 2.01 inches on the 1st and 2nd at the Pocatello Airport was a two day record for the city.  11.6 inches of snow was measured as well the 1st through the 3rd.   11 inches fell in downtown Pocatello with up to 14 to 16 inches on the benches.   American Falls COOP reported 11.8 inches and Blackfoot reported 10 inches.

A strong Pacific storm system brought heavy snow, strong winds which caused excessive damage due to the heavy and wet nature of the snow.   Several trees were downed with extensive power outages.   Windy conditions and colder temperatures caused some road closures on the 4th.  15 thousand customers from Rigby to Rexburg to Idaho Falls to Lewisville were without power on the 2nd.  10 to 16 inches of snow fell with 12 inches in Idaho Falls with 15 inches near the Idaho Falls Airport and 10 inches in Rexburg.   The Rigby COOP reported 9 inches.  Extensive reports of downed power lines.    A power pole snapped in Idaho Falls.   Dozens of trees downed in Idaho Falls.  A large carport collapsed on top of 14 vehicles at Westwood Park Village on Vega St in Idaho Falls.  A storage building collapsed as well at S yellowstone Highway and W 65th S south of Idaho Falls.  Power lines down throughout Lewisville as well.  A vehicle rollover along US Highway 20 on the morning of the 2nd between Idaho Falls and Sugar City.  Most of the property damage occurred due to the heavy snow on the 1st and 2nd.  By the 4th wind and blowing snow closes E Sunnyside Road in Hawks landing area and east in Idaho Falls.   US Highway 26 closed as well on the 4th from Ririe to Swan Valley due to blowing and drifting snow . Bone road closed in Iona.  Idaho Highway 33 closed from Newdale to Tetonia.

Heavy and wet snow fell in the Eastern Magic Valley and combined with strong winds to cause travel issues.   Idaho Highway 81 was closed from Malta to Declo on the 2nd and Interstate 84 was closed from Interstate 86 to the Utah border as well.   5 miles east of Acequia recorded 8.5 inches of snow and Minidoka Dam recorded 12 inches of snow with the storm.

A strong Pacific system brought in extreme moisture with very heavy snow in the Blackfoot Mountains.   The Bone COOP observer recorded 42 inches of snow the first 4 days of the month.   2 to 4 feet were common.   The North Gem School District 149 was closed on the 4th due to the snow and wind conditions and dangerous travel.

Heavy and wet snow combined with strong winds to create travel issues on the 1st and 2nd.   Holbrook recorded 6 inches of snow.  10 miles southeast of Rockland measured 7 inches of snow.  Interstate 84 closed from Interstate 86 to the Utah border due to the conditions and also Idaho Highway 81 from Malta to Declo.  Power outages were reported from Rockland through Holbrook as well due to the heavy and wet snowfall and winds.

Extremely heavy and wet snow fell.   8 inches fell in Lava Hot Springs, 9 inches fell in McCammon and the Inkom area reported between 12 and 22 inches of snow.   Their was a transformer explosion in Inkom overnight on the 1st into the morning of the 2nd with extensive power outages.
A strong Pacific storm brought heavy snow to the Sawtooths and Stanley basin with the Stanley COOP observer recording 15.7 inches of snow.

Extremely heavy snow fell in the Caribou Range and combined with strong winds to cause power outages and road closures on the 2nd with very wet snow. Heavy snow fell and combined with strong winds to bring extensive travel problems with periods of road closures for 4 days.   15 inches of snow was measured in Driggs. Driggs and the Teton Valley had extensive power outages on the 2nd.   US Highway 20 was closed from Ashton to the Montana border on the 2nd. The Vanity Wildfire began September 3rd from lightning strikes about 42 miles west of Challis and burned 600 acres near the Halstead Fire of 2012 site. Forest Service Road #40008 Beaver Creek Rd from Vanity Summit to Josephus Lake was closed due to the fire . About 25 fire fighters were assigned to the fire. Subalpine fir was the main fuel.

The Wapiti fire began July 24th from lightning strikes near Grandjean in the Boise National Forest for eventually spread into the Sawtooth and Salmon Challis National Forests in the latter part of August and continued burning through September in the Sawthooths and Salmon Challis. Idaho State Highway 21 was closed from Stanley to Lowman in late August and remain closed unto September 18th. The Idaho Transportation Board approved 2 million dollars of highway repair for Highway 21 due to several miles of guardrail replacement as well as sign replacement and damaged pavement. The fire burned over 129,000 acres. Stanley schools were closed the first 7 days of classes in the 2024 school year due to extreme air quality issues from wildfire smoke.

A fatal auto accident occurred at 216 PM MST on US Highway 26 at mile marker 391 near the north end of Palisades Reservoir.  A 66 year old male was killed and a 67 year old female was injured in what the Swan Valley Fire Department reported as very dangerous conditions.  US 26 was closed from 240 PM to 640 PM from Palisades Dam to the Wyoming border.   US Highway 26 also closed at 9 AM on the 15th due to blowing snow and reduced visibility. A fire began July 11th near Red Road near St Anthony Sand Dunes on the afternoon and was completely extinguished on the 13th.  The fire was quickly put out by fire fighters from several counties and a tanker dropped fire retardant on the fire on Saturday the 12th.   It was a grass fire that burned just over 2,000 acres and no structures were threatened.

A fire started by natural causes burned about 1,695 acres about 10 miles south of Malad.  It began July 15th and was 100 percent contained by the evening of the 17th.  It was a grass and brush fire in difficult terrain and was initially difficult to contain in gusty winds.  No structures were threatened.

A lightning caused fire began on the afternoon of the 15th 2.5 miles east of Thatcher and burned just under 200 acres which reached into junipers and maples.  The fire was near structures but no damage occurred and no evacuations were required.  It was completely contained on the 17th.

A 70 acre fire began at around 1240 pm MDT on the 23rd along interstate 15 in the Gibson Canal area just south of Blackfoot burning tall grass and sagebrush.  No structures were damaged and the fire was contained by the 24th.

A 100 acre wildfire developed southeast of Treasureton across from Treasureton Reservoir east of Highway 34.  Some structures were threatened but no damage ended up occurring in the fire which burned grass, brush, juniper and maple.
The Summit fire began July 25th from a lightning holdover and grew to 650 acres. It was just south of Oakley. It did not threaten any structures.

The Sand Creek Fire was started by lightning and spread rapidly on August 15th.  The fire was 8 miles west of Ashton in the Sand Creek area, near Lower Arcadia Reservoir.  Strong winds spread the fire rapidly.  Evacuations were ordered for those living in the area by the 16th.  This affected residents in the Cedar Ridge Subdivision including the surrounding 5 mile radius near Sadorus Hill.  Structures were threatened and one outbuilding was destroyed.  The fire covered 851 acres and burned grass, brush, juniper, aspen and conifer.  It was 100 percent contained by the 18th.

The Split Top Fire was reported around 9 pm on August 23rd and burned 5,447 acres of grass and brush about 15 to 20 miles west/northwest of Aberdeen near the Split Top and Arco-Minidoka roads. March 2026 was the warmest ever occurring at the Pocatello ASOS site at the Pocatello Regional Airport.  The average monthly temperature of 46.6 degrees was over 2 degrees warmer than the previous all time record of 44.2 degrees set in 1986.   The all time warmest temperature of 77 degrees for the month occurred three straight days from the 18th through the 20th.

March 2026 was the warmest ever occurring at the Idaho Falls ASOS site at the Idaho Falls Airport. The average monthly temperature of 45.6 degrees was over 2 degrees warmer than the previous all time record of 42.9 degrees set in 1986. The all time warmest temperature of 78 degrees for the month occurred on the 20th.

March 2026 was the warmest ever occurring at the Burley ASOS site at the Burley Municipal Airport. The average monthly temperature of 48.2 degrees was over 1 degree warmer than the previous all time record of 47.1 degrees set in 1992. The all time warmest temperature of 80 degrees for the month occurred on the 20th.

March 2026 was the warmest ever occurring at the Challis ASOS site.  The average monthly temperature of 44.0 degrees was marginally warmer and tied the previous all time record of 44.0 degrees set in 1934. The all time warmest temperature of 75 degrees for the month occurred two straight days on the 19th and 20th.

March 2026 was the warmest ever occurring at the Stanley ASOS site.  The average monthly temperature of 35.1 degrees was over a half degree warmer than the previous all time record of 34.5 degrees set in 2015. The warmest temperature of the month of 64 degrees on the 20th fell one degree short of the all time warmest March temperatures of 65 degrees.

An 800 acre wildfire began August 10th in the Cedar Creek area 15 miles east of Blackfoot.  The fire got to within a half mile of the Aldridge Post Office and School House on Blackfoot River Road but no damage was caused by the fire.  It was contained on August 13th.
A 1,000 acre wire fire ignited on August 26th near the Ririe Reservoir and moved about 5 miles east of the Reservoir.  The fire was considered contained on August 28th.  No damage occurred.

The Willow wildland fire use fire began with a lightning strike on July 14th and was allowed to continue to burn through September 25th.  It burned 4,510 acres of timber.  It was located just west of Island Park or 12 miles south of Henry's Lake.  It shut down some forest service roads from Yale-Kilgore Road to the Montana state line and from Keg Springs Road to Willow Creek Road.  The fire did not damage any property or homes.

The Flag Knoll wildland fire use fire began with a lightning strike on July 21st and was allowed to burn through September 3rd when rain ended it.  The fire was located about 13 miles south of Swan Valley.  It burned over 500 acres of timer and brush.  No damages were caused by the fire.

events.cz_name: BIG AND LITTLE WOOD RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: A prescribed burn of 250 acres jumped to 800 acres due to unexpected winds jumping containment lines.  The fire located near Galena closed State Highway 75 for 4 hours on September 12th from 6 pm to 10 pm between Galena Summit and Stanley.  The fire was contained on September 17th.

Very heavy snow fell in the Eastern Magic Valley beginning early in the morning on October 11th and continuing through the morning of the 12th.  Total snow amounts topped out at 17 inches in Rupert, 15 inches in Heyburn, and 13 inches in Burley.  Interstate 84 was closed for an extended period of time from the 11th through the 12th from the Interstate 86 intersection through the Utah border.  Several minor accidents and road slideoffs werer reported by law enforcement throughout the region.

Snow begain falling early morning on October 11th and continued through the morning of the 12th intermittently.  American Falls recorded 9 inches.  The National Weather Service office at the Pocatello airport recorded 7 inches with 5 to 6 inches in Pocatello and Chubbuck city propers.  Several auto accidents were reported on the icy roads including one fatality near American Falls on interstate 86 near exit 44 on the 11th at 6am.
Heavy snow was reported at high elevation SNOTEL sites.  Twenty inches fell at Mill Creek Summit and 17 inches was recorded at Smiley Mountain.

Several minor auto accidents reported on the 11th.

Interstate 15 was closed at the Hamer exit through the Montana border by 9 am on the morning of October 11th and remained closed through the morning of the 12th.

The combination of snow and wind closed interstate 15 from the Hamer exit in the Upper Snake River Plain through the Montana border.  The interstate closed on the morning of October 11th and remained closed through the morning of October 12th.

Extensive blowing and drifting snow caused interstates 84 and 86 to be closed in the southern portion of the zone. The Blaine County Emergency Manager reported several tree limbs down in the city of Hailey.  This occurred along with downed power lines and roof damages to residences.
The Arco mesonet site measured 63 mph wind gusts from a thunderstorms.  Several trees were blown over in the city of Arco and the wind destroyed a large plate glass window in a flower shop.

Sustained winds of 40 to 45 mph and gusts of 55 to 65 mph caused extensive damage and road closures in the region.  Interstate 15 was closed from Idaho Falls to Roberts due to blowing dust and visibilities under 1 mile.  State highway 33 was closed west of Mud Lake from mile post 42 to 44.  A grain elevator in Rexburg was felled by the winds causing $40,000 worth of damage.  Several large trees were felled in Rigby and Zions Bank in Rigby lost their sign.  Several large trees were also felled in Idaho Falls.
Sustained winds of 40 to 45 mph were measured at Sterling and Blackfoot.  Winds gusted to 55 to 60 mph and an aluminum shed was destroyed in Blackfoot with a 40 foot tree blown over.
Wind gust of 60 mph with visibility in blowing dust at 1/4 mile.
Sixty-one mph wind gust at Kettle Butte.
Several trees were downed in Burley by a microburst wind with several trees on houses and extensive shingle damage reported.  Light fixtures were shattered on several homes.
Microburst caused damage near Paul.  Several large trees taken down, some on top of automobiles.  Sheds were moved off foundations as well.
Broke car wind shield.
