Flooding reported near Weston with roads flooded.
Rural roads flooded north of Holbrook with 0.57 inches of rain in 15 minutes reported.
A lightning strike to a large tree in Taylorsville killed 13 dairy cows who were underneath it for shelter during a thunderstorn.
Extensive marble sized hail caused thousands of acres of wheat to be lost at a farm near Taber.
Two mudslides were reported on Warm Springs Road due to heavy rain at the Castle Rock burn area.
Extremely heavy rainfall at 1.5 inches in 15 minutes caused trees to be uprooted with the Arbon Valley Highway flooded in multiple spots.
Funnel cloud sighted 1.5 miles west of Riverside.
A total of 0.41 inches of rain was measured 4 miles north northeast of Holbrook in a 25 minute period causing flooding on several Oneida County roads.
One inch of rain fell in a 20 minute period over the Castle Rock burn area causing mud and debris to flow over Warm Springs Road.
Street flooding along with flooding in the courthouse was reported in St Anthony as a result of over 1 inch of rain in a 40 minute period.
Extensive rainfall through the month caused flooding in Swanlake near Swan Lake.  Several homes had 2 to 3 inches of water with one basement completely full with water.
Heavy rains during the month of June caused exposed houses in the Hidden Valley subdivision in Pocatello to flood.  As much as 4 inches of water was found in homes exposed to hillsides.
Extensive street flooding from heavy rains in Blackfoot residential areas.
A 74 mile per hour wind gust reported in Blackfoot.

Flash flooding caused by as much a 2 inches of rain in a 2 hour period caused extensive flooding in the south portion of Pocatello.  By 1:15 pm EDT 10th Street and Carter Avenue were completely flooded and not passable.  The Juniper Hills and Riverside golf courses south of the city were completely underwater.  South 5th Avenue was closed due to the water on the street.  US 91 was closed from the South 5th exit to the Portneuf exit.  43 homes and several businesses were reported flooded.  Water up to hoods of cars were reported on Bannock Highway near Riverside Golf Course.   Water submerged cars in the Gables assisted living center on South Grant Avenue.  Roads were closed throughout the Indian Hill section of Pocatello with knee deep water on most roads.  A disaster area declaration was declared for Bannock County at 3:30 pm MDT.  The rains created an 8 foot sink hole at Constitution Park.  Sink holes developed at some local residences as deep as 12 feet.  Extensive road damage occurred due to rushing debris.
Pocatello Regional Airport recorded 4.00 inches of rainfall for the entire month of June.  This was the wettest June on record as well as the wettest month ever recorded for this location.
Heavy rain from a thunderstorm caused a mudslide over the Castle Rock burn area causing Warm Springs Road to be closed.  The mud was 2 feet deep and 30 feet wide on the road.
Birch Creek came out of its banks flooding and closing a local road northeast of Almo.

Over one inch of rain in less than one hour near Inkom and the runoff caused the Rapid Creek and Portneuf River to exceed their banks.  Extensive flooding occurred throughout the city of Inkom.  About 30 homes and businesses flooded with as much as 5 to 12 inches of standing water in them.  Jackson Creek Road was washed out.  Bannock County was declared a disaster area by 3 pm MDT on July 4th.
Over 1 inch of rain in less than an hour caused minor street flooding throughout the city of Pocatello.  The Red Lion Hotel reported standing water inside their establishment.
Strong thunderstorm dropped several trees in the private Camp Perkins campground at Alturas Lake.  Trees also fell across Highway 75.

Heavy snow fell in the South Central Highlands with 11 inches at Bostetter Ranger Station and 12 inches at Howell Canyon.
Heavy snow fell in mountainous areas of the Cache Valley.  12 inches was reported at Oxford Springs.

Prodigious amounts of snow fell above 7,000 feet in the Sawtooth Mountains as a powerful early spring storm moved through the area.  27 inches fell at Smiley Mountain.  18 inches fell at Mill Creek Summit and 17 inches fell at Bear Canyon.  14 inches of snow fell on Banner Summit and Highway 21 was closed due to avalanche danger.

events.cz_name: BIG AND LITTLE WOOD RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: An early spring storm brought heavy snow to the Wood River Region above 7,000 feet.  Heaviest amounts recorded were 24 inches at Vienna Mine, 15 inches at Lost Wood Divide, 18 inches at Galena Summit, 15 inches at Dollarhide, and 14 inches at Galena.
A powerful early spring storm brought 12 inches of snow to the Meadow Lake SNOTEL.
The Pine Creek Pass SNOTEL received 12 inches of snow from an early spring snowstorm.

Less than warning criteria snowfall amounts occurred in the Upper Snake River Highlands causing road closures on Saturday morning April 3rd.   8 inches of snow fell in Ashton and 8.5 inches fell in Island Park.   State Highway 33 was closed from Newdale to Tetonia from milepost 107 to milepost 131, and State Highway 32 was closed from milepost 0 to milepost 28 due to reduced visibility.

An early spring storm brought heavy wet snowfall to the Idaho Wasatch.  16 inches of snow fell at the Slug Creek SNOTEL and the Franklin Basin SNOTEL.  Spotters reported 10 inches at Bern, 9 inches at Montpelier, and 8 inches at Georgetown.

An early spring storm dropped heavy snowfall in the Upper Snake River Plain.  6 to 8 inches was reported by spotters in Rigby.  6 inches fell in Idaho Falls and 5 inches was reported in Shelley.  The following school districts were closed on April 6th:  Idaho Falls district 91, Bonneville district 93, Jefferson district 251, Shelley district 90, and Ririe district 252.

Very strong non-thunderstorm winds caused damage to buildings in the city of Chubbuck. 20 to 25 feet of roof from Inter Mountain Storage was torn off and blown across the street. And a greenhouse suffered extensive damage in the city as well. In Pocatello the wind uprooted trees and caused roof damage.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a large sign at Simplot in St Anthony.  The same storm also blew over a fuel shed on the south side of town near Simplot.
The average temperature in May of 48.5 degrees at the Pocatello Regional Airport broke the previous all time record cold average temperature for the month of 48.8 degrees set in 1953.

High winds with gusts of 60 to 80 mph caused interstate 15 to be closed at 1:42 pm through at least 10 pm between Idaho Falls and Roberts.   Blowing dust dropped visibilities to near zero.   A 71 mph wind gust was measured at Howe and a 76 mph wind gust was measured at Kettle Butte 11 miles west of Osgood.
Several sites reported wind gusts over 60 mph including the Pocatello Regional Airport ASOS measuring 62 mph.   60 mph was measured at the Arbon Valley ITD site and the Fort Hall ARL site.
Heavy snow fell above 6,000 feet.   10 inches fell at Howell Canyon with 9 inches at Bostetter Ranger Station and 11 inches at Magic Mountain.

Valley Creek came out of its banks due to heavy rains and several campsites, homes and farms were flooded.  Local roads were covered with water as well.  Flooding occurred near Stanley Lake at campsites as well.  Flooding was reported of backcountry roads and campgrounds from Stanley south to Alturus Lake and Beaver Creek areas.  A rock slide also occurred on route 75 between Clayton and Sunbeam.  Fifty miles of road were damaged with two culverts and two roads washed out.
Sixty mph wind gust from thunderstorm.
A 71 mph wind gust was measured by a spotter in Bern.
A spotter reported a 60 mph wind gust near Georgetown.
Thunderstorm winds demolished a new hay barn.
Power pole snapped by thunderstorm wind causing power outage.
Fifty-eight mph wind gust near Taber.
Sixty mph wind gust at Craters of the Moon.
Craters of the Moon mesonet measured 79 mph wind gust.
Arco INL site recorded 64 mph wind gust.
Dead Man Canyon INL site measures 61 mph wind gust.
Naval Reactor INL site recorded 58 mph wind gust.
A lightning strike hit the Basalt water system destroying computer equipment and leaving 600 people without water for 2 hours.
Measured wind gust of 64 mph.
Thunderstorm winds of 59 mph mesausred in Hamer.

A wildfire began on July 14th at the Idaho National Laboratory and was the largest range fire in the site's history. The fire consumed 100,000 to 120,000 acres as it was propelled by 30 to 40 mph sustained winds on July 14th with gusts of 50 to 60 mph. It began near the site's main entrance between US Highway 20 and the main entrance. The fire travelled more than 40 miles in 5 hours driven by the wind. Low visibility from smoke closed Interstate 15 between Roberts and Dubois at 9:15 pm on the 14th until 11:45 pm. Highway 33 was also closed due to visibility from the I-15 intersection to 10 miles west of Mud Lake. Only minor exterior damage was done to one building on the site and some overhead power lines were downed. Nearly the entire site came out un-damaged by the large fire.
Sixty-two mph wind at Aberdeen.
Several trees reported downed in Aberdeen by the Emergency Manager.
Power lines reported downed by thunderstorm winds 6 miles north of Aberdeen.
Sixty-one mph wind gust measured 6 miles northwest of Minidoka.
Sixty mph wind gust 2 miles west southwest of Aberdeen.
Sixty mph wind gust 2 miles west of Pocatello Regional Airport.
Sixty mph wind gust 1 mile north northwest of Rockford.
Trees downed in the City of Blackfoot reported by law enforcement officers.
Sixty mph wind gusts reported by trained spotter 3 miles east northeast of Blackfoot.
Fifty-eight mph wind 20 miles southeast of Malta.
Sixty mph wind gust at Pocatello Regional Airport.
Hamer ARL FRD mesonet site recorded 63 mph wind gust.
Sixty mph wind gust at Aberdeen.
Sixty-one mph wind gust 5 miles northwest of Moreland.
Seventy-six mph wind gust at Central Facilities INL mseonet site.
Sixty-seven mph wind gust at Critical Infrastructure INL mesonet site.
Seventy-one mph wind gust at Fanning Field in Idaho Falls.
Large tree fell on top of a home in Malad City.  Residents had to evacuate home.
Sixty-nine mph wind gust at Sugar City.
Two power lines down with one caused by a large tree falling on it.
Trained spotter reported shingles blowing off of a roof 5 miles west of Clementsville.
Roof damage in Arimo reported due to thunderstorm winds.
Spotter reported 61 mph wind gust.
Preston mesonet site reported sixty-four mph wind gust.
One inch hail fell 6 miles south southeast of Lorenzo.

events.cz_name: BIG AND LITTLE WOOD RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: Lightning started the 8,000 acre Bear Trap wildfire east of Carey near Laid Law Park.
Lightning strikes caused a wildfire 8 miles northeast of American Falls reaching 12,500 acres.  No structures were damaged by the fire.
A 3,300 acre wildfire caused by a lightning strike was 5 miles south of Massacre Rocks. No structural damage in the open land fire.
A 6,700 acre wildfire near Arbon was caused by a lighting strike.  No structural damage in the open land fire.
A 2,000 acre wildfire  caused by lightning strike occurred 15 miles west of Stanley.  It initially caused road closures and campground evacuations.   No property damage occurred.
A fire which began 1 mile northeast of Atomic City burned 14,139 acres on the INL site.  The fire temporarily closed Highway 20 and non-essential personnel were evacuated from the site.
Visibility reported to be less than 1/4 mile on interstate 15 from milepost 135 to 155 south of Hamer.

Thirty foot trees were uprooted and blown over taking down an anchor-wire to a large antenna.  This occurred 1 mile east southeast of Rexburg.    A small airplane was blown off the runway of the Idaho Falls Regional Airport then flipped while it was being towed.
Large tree blown down by high wind on Stanford Avenue in Pocatello.

Wind gusts estimated over 60 mph uprooted a large spruce tree in Challis and it took out a Custer Telephone cable TV line.  Salmon River Electric reported power outages in the Yankee Fork and Rod and Gun Club areas.   The Yankee Fork outage was due to a tree falling on the Yankee Fok distribution line.  About 50 people lost power for 3 hours.   Times estimated from newspaper and ASOS reports in the area.
Lightning caused a 2,500 acre wildfire southwest of Rockland from September 14th through the 20th.  The fire was in open land with no structural or property damage reported.
Twelve inches of snow fell at Smiley Mountain and 9 inches fell at Bear Canyon.

events.cz_name: BIG AND LITTLE WOOD RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: Sixteen inches of snow fell at Vienna Mine with 12 inches at Dollarhide and 11 inches at Galena and Lost Wood Divide.
High winds caused damage to power lines and a power outage to more than 2500 customers.

Two fully grown pine trees uprooted by strong winds in Idaho Falls.   The trees were over 2 foot in diameter.   Craters of the Moon reported 60 mph wind gusts.  Over 50 mph wind gusts reported in Terreton and Howe.
Several 1/2 inch tree branches snapped off trees in the Grace area.

Nine inches of snow was reported 5 miles east southeast of Warm River. Additional reports were 7 inches in Ashton, and 4 inches in Victor. US route 20 was closed from Ashton north due to a crash involving semi trucks on heavy slush covered roads.
A strong cold front brought strong winds behind the front to many regions of the eastern Magic Valley.   Rupert recorded a 61 mph gust with 55 mph at the Burley airport and 66 mph at Minidoka.

Very strong winds occurred behind a cold front in the South Central Highlands.  70 mph gusts were recorded 9 miles west of Black Pine with 58 mph 9 miles northwest of Idahome and 57 mph 7 miles northwest of Idahome.

Strong winds reported in Upper Snake River Plain behind a strong cold front.  61 mph reported 11 miles west of Osgood and 62 mph at Craters of the Moon.  A large tree was downed in Idaho Falls blocking two lanes of Sunnyside Road, a major thoroughfare in the city.  55 to 60 mph gusts were widespread at the INL site.

Strong winds behind a Pacific cold front affected the lower Snake River Plain.   59 mph was measured at the Pocatello airport and 60 mph was measured 1 mile northeast of Aberdeen.   60 mph was also measured 11 miles west of Neely.
Strong winds behind a Pacific cold front produced a 64 mph wind gust 1 mile west of Gray and 60 mph 3 mile northeast of Chesterfield.
A 62 mph wind gust was recorded by a COOP observer in Bern post cold frontal passage.  Sustained winds of 40 mph reported for 2 hours.

Heavy snow targeted the Upper Snake Highlands from the evening of the 18th through the morning of the 21st.  15 inches fell in Ashton and both highway 32 and 33 were closed down on the 20th through the morning of the 21st.  10 inches fell at St Anthony.  11 inches fell at Crab Creek and Island Park with 29 inches at White Elephant.
Heavy snow targeted the Caribou Highlands from the evening of the 18th through the morning of the 21st.  9 inches fell at Sedgwick Peak and Pine Creek Pass.
Heavy snow targeted the Idaho Wasatch from the evening of the 18th through the morning of the 21st.  13 inches fell at Emigrant Summit and 14 inches at Franklin Basin.
Heavy snow targeted Sawtooth Mountains from the evening of the 18th through the morning of the 21st.  12 inches fell at Smiley Mountain with 15 inches at Mill Creek Summit.
The Hilt's Creek SNOTEL 10 miles northeast of Mackay recorded 13.5 inches of snow.

Three to 5 inches of snow fell with wind gusts of 50 to 60 mph.   Whiteout conditions were reported 5 miles southwest of Gannett.  Interstate 84 closed from the junction with Interstate 86 to the Utah border and US Highway 30 was closed between mileposts 228 and 252 from Murtaugh to Burley due to whiteout conditions.

Sigificant snow fell with a strong cold frontal passage in the Sawtooth Mountains.  18 inches fell at Bear Canyon, 11 inches at Stickney Mill, 19 inches at Smiley Mountain, anda 18 inches at Mill Creek Summit.

Sustained winds of 30 to 40 mph combined with heavy snow caused Highways 32, 33, 47, 87, and US Highway 20 from Ashton to the Montana state line to be shut down.  Snow amounts during the event were 18 inches at Crab Creek, 12 inches at Island Park, and 21 inches at White elephant which picked up 50 inches total since November 21st.

Three to 5 inches of snow fell in the Upper Snake River Plain combined with 50 to 60 mph wind gusts caused Interstate 15 north of Idaho Falls to be closed as well as all roads in Bingham County.   Several school districts closed as well.

Two to 4 inches of snow fell in the Lower Snake River Plain and combined with 50 to 60 mph wind gusts for blizzard conditions.   The Pocatello/Chubbuck, American Falls, and Sho-Ban schools all closed due to the conditions.

Interstate 84 from the Interstate 86 intersection to the Utah border closed due to whiteout conditions and blowing snow.   Heaviest snow amounts were 11 inches at Howell Canyon and 9 inches at Oxford Springs.

Extremely heavy snow fell in the Caribou Highlands and combined with strong winds to produce whiteout conditions.   Amounts recorded were the following:  Pine Creek Pass 11 inches, Sedgwick Peak 21 inches, Sheep Mountain 9 inches, Somsen Ranch, 10 inches, and Wild Horse Divide 7 inches.

The Franklin County Sheriffs Office reported 30 accidents and 50 abandoned cars stuck in snow.   No reports of snow amounts were received, but 2 foot drifts were reported on some roads and zero visibility was reported to be near zero from 11 am through 2 pm by the Sheriffs office in Franklin County.   Franklin County schools were closed for the day.
Eight inches of snow fell at Emigrant Summit.   19 inches fell at Frannklin Basin with 7 inches at Slug Creek and 8 inches at Giveout.

events.cz_name: BIG AND LITTLE WOOD RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: Twelve inches of snow fell in Hailey.   SNOTEL reports were the following:  19 inches at Dollarhide, 9 inches at Chocolate Gulch, 17 inches at Galena Summit, 12 inches at Garfield Ranger Station, 11 inches at Lost Wood Divide, 9 inches at Hyndman, and 15 inches at Swede Peak.
Heavy snow fell in the Lost River Pahsimeroi region.   20 inches fell at Hilt's Creek with 12 inches at Meadow Lake and 9 inches at Moonshine.

Six to 9 inches of snow fell in the Pocatello/Chubbuck area.   7 inches was measured at the Pocatello Regional Airport which set a calendar day record for the month of Novemver.   7 inches also was measured in Blackfoot.
Twenty inches of snow fell at Howell Canyon with 8 inches at Oxford Springs.   Interstate 84 was closed due to whiteout conditions from the Interstate 86 junction to the Utah border.
Thirteen inches of snow fell at Sedgwick Peak and 17 inches at Wild Horse Divide.
Twelve inches of snow fell at Emigrant Summit with 11 inches at Franklin Basin and 14 inches at Slug Creek Divide.

November of 2010 was the second snowiest November on record for the Pocatello Regional Airport. The 17 inches that fell for the month was second only to the 27.5 inches that fell in 1985. The month was highlighted by 16 inches of snow that fell from November 20th through November 28th. The 7.0 inches that fell on November 28th set a record for the snowiest calendar day ever for November.
Fifteen inches of snow fell at Bear Canyon with 17 inches at Smiley Mountain and 11 inches at Mill Creek Summit.

events.cz_name: BIG AND LITTLE WOOD RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: Sixteen inches of snow fell at Lost Wood Divide with 12 inches at Vienna Mine, 11 inches at Swede Peak, and 10 inches at Hyndman, Garfield Ranger Station, and Dollarhide.
Fourteen inches of snow fell at Meadow Lake SNOTEL with 10 inches at Moonshine.
Tractor trailers sliding off interstate 86 and 15 between 8 and 9 am from ice covered roads from freezing rain closed both interstates for brief periods.
Twelve inches of snow  fell at Smiley Mountain and Mill Creek Summit with 11 inches at Bear Canyon.
Ten inches of snow fell at Howell Canyon and Oxford Springs.
Thirteen inches of snow fell at Sedgwick Peak.

events.cz_name: BIG AND LITTLE WOOD RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: Total snow amounts were 19 inches at dollarhide, 11 inches at Chocolate Gulch, 20 inches at Galena, 17 inches at Galena Summit, 18 inches at Garfield Ranger Station, 21 inches at Lost Wood Divide, 11 inches at Swede Peak, and 22 inches at Vienna Mine.

events.cz_name: BIG AND LITTLE WOOD RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: SNOTEL sites rported the following snow amounts:  Dollarhide 11 inches, Chocolate Gulch 9 inches, Galena Summit 11 inches, Lost Wood Divide 9 inches, Swede Peak 11 inches, and Vienna Mine 9 inches.

A spotter reported 12 inches of snow at Island Park.  SNOTEL sites rported 14 inches at Crab Creek, 17 inches at Island Park Reservoir, and 34 inches at White Elephant.  State HIghway 47 was closed between Ashton and Warm River.  State highway 32 was closed.

A trained spotter reported 13 inches of snow 4 miles north northeast of Holbrook.  SNOTEL amounts were 18 inches at Bostetter, 12 inches at Howell Canyon, 11 inches at Oxford Springs, and 12 inches at Magic Mountain.
Seventeen inches fell at Sedgwick Peak, 8 inches at Sheep Mountain, and 14 inches at Wild Horse Divide.
A spotter reported 10 inches of snow in Bern.  SNOTEL sites reporting were Emigrant Summit with 17 inches and Franklin Basin with 25 inches.
Ten inches of snow fell at the Meadow Lake SNOTEL site.
A flat-roofed cinder block commercial building roof collapsed. The building in Rexburg housed both Rocky Mountain ATVs and Custom Auto. Heavy snow collected on the roof was the cause of the collapse.

A weak upper level system brough localized heavy snow in the Pocatello metro area with 5 to 7 inches reported throughout the Pocatello area.  The timing of the snow which the majority fell between 4 am and 7 am on the 25th caused a two hour delay in the Pocatello/Chubbuck local school district 25 and several private schools in Pocatello to be closed.   National Weather Service employees reported 6.5 inches in West Chubbuck and 6.0 inches in East Pocatello.   3 inches fell in American Falls.

events.cz_name: BIG AND LITTLE WOOD RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: Ten inches of snow fell at Vienna Mine, Swede Peak, Garfield Ranger Station, Galena Summit SNOTEL sites. 12 inches of snow was recorded at Dollarhide.
Ten inches of snow fell at Bear Canyon SNOTEL with 11 inches at Smiley Mountain.

events.cz_name: BIG AND LITTLE WOOD RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: Eleven inches of snow fell 2 miles north northwest of Hailey with 9 inches at Bald Mountain.

Several school closings occurred on both February 1st and 2nd due to extreme cold including Clark County District 161...Fremont County District 215...and Teton County District 401.  Wind chill readings of -25 to -35 degrees were recorded at Island Park, DUbois and Driggs.
School closings on February 2nd including Jefferson District 251...West Jefferson District 253.  Rexburg reported wind chill readings of -25 degrees on the 1st.
Soda Springs District 150 closed on February 1st and 2nd due to extreme cold as well as Swan Valley district 92.

events.cz_name: BIG AND LITTLE WOOD RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: The Smiley Creek Airport recorded a -46 degree wind chill on the morning of the 1st and Lone Pine recorded -33 degrees.
Road Creek reported wind chill readings of -30 degrees on February 1st between 7 am and 9 am.
The Bear Lake County Airport recorded wind chill readings of -25 to -30 degrees from 4 am through 9 am on the morning of February 1st.

Six inches of snow fell at the Pocatello Regional Airport.  Accidents were reported on Interstate 15 south of the city of Pocatello and Idaho State Police reported 12 accidents and 24 slide offs between 4 pm and 10 pm in and near the city of Pocatello.   A rollover on southbound interstate 15 between Chubbuck and Fort Hall occurred.
Heavy snowfall amounts were 10 inches at Malad Summit, 11 inches at Stone, 8 inches at Oakley, and 8 inches at Buist.
Twelve inches of snow was reported at Weston with 10 inches reported at Preston by trained spotters.

A foot of snow was reported at Bern with 13 inches at St Charles and 8 inches at Montpelier by trained spotters.  SNOTEL sites reporting heavy snow were Emigrant Summit with 14 inches and Franklin Basin with 16 inches.

Extensive damage and warning level winds occurred with the passage of a cold front the evening of March 10th. Two trees were downed into a house in Burley. Several trees down at Burley parks and golf course.

Extensive damage and warning level winds occurred with the passage of a cold front the evening of March 10th. Power lines were downed south of Rupert along Idaho route 24. Much of Minidoka County had power outages causing a black out for nearly 2 hours. The city of Rupert had a complete power outage. Power was restored to many areas by 8 pm.

Extensive damage and warning level winds occurred with the passage of a cold front the evening of March 10th. A roof was blown off a building in American Falls into power lines with power outages in the city for up to an hour.  Wind speeds of 78 mph were measured in American Falls.  The winds also downed some power lines.
Sixty-two mph wind gust recorded at Pocatello Regional Airport.
Sixty-one mph wind gust recorded 5 miles north of Portneuf.
Police dispatchers reported a deck blown over a house in the city of Chubbuck.
Winds of 66 mph were measured at Montpelier with power outages in the western side of the valley in Bear Lake County due to strong winds blowing down power lines.

Significant amounts of snow fell from noon on the 15th through the evening of the 16th. Some of the more impressive totals were: 16 inches at Bear Canyon, 16 inches at Smiley Mountain, and 12 inches at Mill Creek Summit.
Significant amounts of snow fell from noon on the 15th through the evening of the 16th. Some of the more impressive totals were: 12 inches at Crab Creek and 21 inches at White Elephant.

events.cz_name: BIG AND LITTLE WOOD RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: Significant amounts of snow fell from noon on the 15th through the evening of the 16th. Some of the more impressive totals were: 13 inches at Dollarhide, 11 inches at Galena, 13 inches at Galena Summit, 18 inches at Lost Wood Divide, and 26 inches at Vienna Mine.
Significant amounts of snow fell from noon on the 15th through the evening of the 16th. Some of the more impressive totals were: 10 inches at Hilts Creek, and 16 inches at Medow Lake.
The Burley airport reported a wind gust of 58 mph at 353 pm MDT. Tree damage was also reported as a 10 inch diameter pine tree was downed.
A two day storm brought extremely heavy snowfall totals to the mountains of southeast Idaho. Heaviest recorded amounts were: 11 inches at Bear Canyon and 27 inches at Smiley Mountain.

A two day storm brought extremely heavy snowfall totals to the mountains of southeast Idaho. Heaviest recorded amounts were: 9 inches at Pine Creek Pass, 14 inches at Sedgwick Peak, 9 inches at Sheep Mountain, 9 inches at Wild Horse Divide, and 12 inches at Palisades.

A two day storm brought extremely heavy snowfall totals to the mountains of southeast Idaho. Heaviest recorded amounts were: 21 inches at Emigrant Summit, 17 inches at Franklin Basin, and 9 inches at Giveout.

events.cz_name: BIG AND LITTLE WOOD RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: A two day storm brought extremely heavy snowfall totals to the mountains of southeast Idaho. Heaviest recorded amounts were: 28 inches at Dollarhide, 17 inches at Chocolate gulch, 9 inches at Galena, 26 inches at Galena Summit, 9 inches at Lost Wood Divide, 12 inches at Hyndman, 20 inches at Swede Peak, 22 inches at Vienna Mine, and 15 inches in the town of Ketchum.
A two day storm brought extremely heavy snowfall totals to the mountains of southeast Idaho. 20 inches of snow fell at Hilts Creek.
Sixty-four mph wind gust at the Rover site.
Sixty-one mph wind gust at Hamer.
Forty to 45 mph sustained winds occurred from 12 noon MDT time through 720 pm MDT at the Hamer and Rover sites.

The Portneuf River at Pocatello reached flood stage of 8.5 feet on May 8th and remained over flood stage through the rest of the month peaking at 9.95 feet on May 28th.  Extensive low land flooding occurred in Inkom.  Pasture and livestock corrals were flooded in the vicinity of the Portneuf River and marsh Creek confluence.  Lowland flooding occurred along the river between Portneuf Gap and the Cheyenne Avenue Bridge in Pocatello.  Flooding of lowlands and a recreation trail in Pocatello occurred from Sacajawea Park to Pacific Recylcing Park.

The Snake River at Blackfoot reached flood stage of 10 feet on May 10th and remained over flood stage the remainder of the month peaking at 12.04 feet on May 29th.  The Riverton area had widespread flooding resulting in the closure of Riverton Road with several homes threatened.   The Rose Levee broke on May 27th resulting in the washout of about 200 feet of levee structure.  Flows occurred through the Rose Ponds recreation area flooding campgrounds and a walking path.   The Archery Range Road was flooded causing the evacuation of a resident from their property.  In Blackfoot, sub-water seepage into Jensen's Grove caused minor flooding of the park and an industrial storage lot behind the Super 8 Motel and Blackfoot Medical Center.  Flooding of lowlands and agricultural fields occurred adjacent to the river between Rost and Tilden Bridge.   The Snake River at Shelley reached flood stage on May 16th at 12 feet and peaked at 13.15 feet on May 28th which was major flood stage.  County Road 700 North southwest of Firth was closed.  In firth, the Riverview Arena was partially underwater and extensive flooding of lowlands and agricultural fields occurred adjacent to the river between Firth and Rose.

The Henry's Fork River near Rexburg reached flood stage of 9.5 feet on May 15th and remained above through the end of the month. The river peaked at 10.96 feet on May 26th. Extensive low land flooding occurred. Beaver Dick Park was flooded as were some river access recreational areas. Water covered portions of the road in the Warm Slough Access to a depth of around one foot.

Extensive lowland and field flooding occurred along the Bear River upstream of Stewart Dam.  Two homes in the dingle area surrounded by water.  Water covered a portion of Pegram Road near the town of Pegram.  Water flowed across Poverty Flat Road near the intersection with Pegram Road.  Extensive lowland flooding also occurred along the Thomas Fork near the Wyoming Border.  Water flowed across county roads and some livestock corrals were inundated with water.  Humerous small creeks draining east into Bear River and Bear Lake exceeded their banks and caused damage and washouts  along back country roads.  Montpelier Creek caused flooding of some prpoerties in the canyon east of the town of Montpelier.

Extensive lowland flooding along Pine Creek and damage to some secondary roads.  Numerous mud slides along Highway 31 leading to Pine Creek Pass.  Rainey Creek exceeded its banks and caused minor flooding of lowland and some driveways in the Swan Valley area.  Fall Creek was periodically out of its banks and impacted a dirt road.

Small stream flooding occurred in the Slug Creek and Diamond Creek drainages flowing toward Wyoming.  Tincup Creek overflowed its banks and flooded some fields.  Many back country roads were damaged or washed out.
Flooding of pasture and agricultural fields occurred.  Some roads in the Kilgore area were flooded and several roads werre raised to avoid the flood waters.

Extensive road damage and washouts occurred along Kelly Canyon Road.  Extensive lawland and agricultural field flooding occurred and a few properties had minor flooding in yards.  One home 3 miles east of Roberts just off Highway 48 had water in the basement.  Teh Menan Buttes Public Access boat ramp flooded and a recreational day use area and boat ramp adjacent to Highway 48 flooded.  Levees were raised in the Roberts area and Scotts Slough by the Menan Buttes Bridge to avoid flood waters.

One mile north of Ashton  a potato cellar wit machinery inside was flooded with 3 feet of water.  Four cabins at the Log Cabin Motel in Ashton were flooded.;   A mudslide temporarily closed one lane of Highwy 20.  USFS Wood 1 Road was washed out.   0.50 inches of rain fell in a span of 30 minutes.  Rocks and trees were across Highway 20/47 near Ashton/Marysville.
Heavy rain on top of snowmelt caused Badger Crerek to flood causing damage to County Road 10000 North.   It was closed for several weeks.
One inch hail reported in Ovid.
Trained spotter reported 1.75 inch hail in Wardboro.
A trained spotter reported 2 inch hail in Montpelier.
One inch hail reported by spotter 1 mile north of Montpelier.

An EF0 tornado hit the city of Moreland along Pioneer Road between 800 and 900 West between 6:50 and 7:00 pm MDT On June 23rd.   four homes received damage.  A shed at one home was destroyed and a garage to the back of another home was destroyed.  A third home had wood sidign removed and damaged trees.  A camper was flipped over and was on it's top at a 4th home.   A storm survey was done and it was determined to be an EF0 tornado.  The Jensen Grove Park near Blackfoot had 19 trees either snapped or uprooted by the storm.
Sixty mph wind near St Charles.
Sixty-two mph wind gust at Bern measured by trained spotter.
Large tree was downed 1 mile south southeast of St Charles.

Straight line non thunderstorm winds caused power poles to snap off 10 miles southeast of Ashton.   Additional downed power lines occurred 13 miles southeast of Ashton, 11 miles southeast of Ashton, and 3 miles west of St Anthony.
Olive tree downed over a fence near Sacajewea Park.
Large oak tree downed in Iona.

The Teton River near St Anthony was above flood stage several times in June beginning on June 7th and continuing off on on through the 30th.   The highest crest of 6.61 feet occurred on June 15th.   Numerous agricultural fields and low level lands were flooded affecting some farm equipment.  Minor bank erosion occurred along the levee.  The Henry's Fork at St Anthonywas at flood stage from June 7th through June 9th.  The river crested at a record level of 8.84 feet on June 8th.  One home 2 miles east of St Anthony was flooded with 3 to 4 feet of water in the basement.   Some outbuildings were flooded.  Keefer Park in St Anthony flooded and a city water pipe was damaged from debris in the river.  Extensive flooding of lowlands and pasturelands occurred near St Anthony.  A portion of South River Road was covered with floodwaters.

The Henry's Fork near Rexburg was above flood stage from June 1st through June 30th with the exception of the period from June 4th through the morning of June 7th.   Major flood stage was reached and crested at 11.85 feet on June 9th.   Extensive flooding of agricultural and low lands occurred.  Beaver Dick Park flooded, river access recreation areas flooded as did portions of county roads.  Water covered a road in the Warm Slough Access to a depth of over one foot.  Water flooded the crawl space to one home.

The Snake River at Heise rose above flood stage of 8 feet on June 6th through the morning of June 8th peaking at 8.31 feet on June 8th.  Lowland flooding occurred and the extended period of high flows caused erosion and structural concerns at the Archer Highway north Twin Bridge.

The Snake River near Shelley was above flood stage from June 1st through June 12th at 12 feet peaking at 13 feet on June 10th which was major flood stage.  County Road 700 North southwest of Firth was closed.   Homes on that road were surrounded by water with yards and outbuildings flooded.   In Firth the Riverview Arena was partially underwater and extensive flooding of lowland and agricultural fields occurred between Firth and Rose.

The Snake River at Blackfoot was above flood stage from June 1st through June 19th.  It was below flood stage from June 13th through June 16th.  Water levels reached moderate flood stage and crested at 11.79 feet on the evening of June 10th.   There was widespread floodign in the Riverton area resulting in the closure of Riverton Road with several homes threatened.  A number of homes and access roads were threatened in the Thomas area near Riverbend Road and Wilson Road.  Berm construction and sandbagging appeared to have been successful in those areas.  Archery Range Road near the Rose Overpass was submerged and impassable for a period.  In Blackfoot, sub-water seepage into Jensens Grove caused minor flooding of the park.  Flooding of lowland and agricultural fields occurred adjacent to the river between Rose and Tilden Bridge.

The Portneuf River at Pocatello remained above flood stage through June 18th.  The river crested at 9.28 feet on June 11th.  Extensive lowland flooding occurred near Inkom.   Pasture and livestock corrals were flooded in the vicinity of Portneuf Gap and the Cheyenne Avenue Bridge in Pocatello.  Downstream of the concrete flood control channel through Pocatello minor flooding of lowland and a city recreation trail occurred from Sacajawea Park to Pacfic Recycling Park.

High flows on the Snake River flooded over 1,100 acres of cropland.  The Menan Buttes Public Access boat ramp and a recreational day use area and boat ramp adjacent to Highway 48 remained flooded.  A power line which under the river near Lorenzo was unburied and snapped due to the high flows.

Extensive lowland and field flooding occurred along the Bear River upstream of Stewart Dam.  Two homes in the dingle area were surrounded by water.  Waterh encroached on some outbuildings and agricultural supp0lies were flooded in low lying areas.  Water covered a portion of Pegram Road near the town of Pegram.  The Bear border river gauge was inundated with water.  Extensive flooding of fields occurred along the lower end of teh Thomas Fork near the confluence with the Bear River.
Heavy rain caused roads to flood at Costco and at City Hall and 6th Street.
Several small streams exceeded bankfull.  Open fields were flooded.
Several tree branches downed in the city of Fish Haven.
Fifty-eight mph wind gust at the Kettle Butte ARL site.
Rainfall of 0.30 inches in 15 minutes caused extensive street flooding in the city of Challis.

The Henry's Fork River near Rexburg was above flood stage to start July and remained above flood stage until July 8th.  The river crested at 9.92 feet on July 2nd.  Minor floodign of farmland and lowland occurred.  Portions of Beaver Dick Park were flooded as well as some recreational river access sites.

The Teton River near St Anthony was above flood stage at the end of June and remained above flood stage until July 9th peaking at 6.37 feet on July 1st.  flooding of agricultural fields and lowlands near the river occurred.

Extensive lowland and field flooding continued through much of July along the Bear River upstream of Stewart Dam.   Water continued to surround a couple homes in the dingle area and water continued to impact a portion of Pegram Road near the town of Pegram.  Water levels on the river receded considerably beginning July 24th.

Heavy rains and small hail caused flooding in Arco.  Roadways in town flooded with damage reported by law enforcement.  Hail was up to 2 inches deep in some parts of town.  The basement in the new court house in Arco was flooded as well.
INL Central Facilities site carried several minutes of above 60 mph wind gusts due to a thunderstorm.  It peaked at 67 mph at 5:20 pm MDT.
Lost River Rest Area reported a 58 mph wind gust at 5:10 MDT.
The Reactor Tech Site at INL reported a 65 mph wind gust at 5:15 pm MDT.
The Critical Infrastructure INL site reported a 70 mph wind gust at 5:25 pm MDT.
Big Southern Butte registered a wind gust of 66 mph at 5:50 pm MDT.
One inch hail was reported by spotters in Fort Hall and east of Fort Hall.
A spotter reported 1 inch hail 4 miles east northeast of American Falls.
One inch hail at Soda Springs.
Thunderstorm winds caused power lines to arc and be damaged closing HIghway 33 near Rexburg from 7 pm to 9 pm MDT between 3000 and 4000 W.
Early on August 21st a thunderstorm caused trees to into a house on Pioneer Road in Idaho Falls killing an 82 year old man in his bedroom. Trees were also downed on East Lincoln Road.
The Taber Mesonet site reported an 83 mph wind gust at 10:35 pm MDT and another 63 mph gust at 10:50 pm MDT.

A fire in Bannock County near Chinese Peak was started by juveniles playing with matches.  It burned 1,280 acres and destroyed one home and adjacent barn.  The fire began at 2 pm MDT on August 15th and was 100 percent contained by August 18th.

Lightning caused a fire in northeastern Bannock County on the Fort Hall Indian Reservation.  The fire began at about 1 pm MDT on August 20th and burned about 600 acres.  2 and a half mile road was closed  for fire crews and some homes on the road were threatened but were never needed to be evacuated.

A lightning strike caused nearly 50,000 acres to be burned north of the Idaho Nuclear Technology and Engineering Center facility.  The fire mostly scorched sagebrush and grasslands and was contained with no radiological hazards or any structural damages.  The fire began at about 1 pm on August 25th and was contained by August 28th.

Multiple power outages were caused by heavy snow in the Idaho Falls area.  6 inches fell in Idaho Falls with downed tree branches and limbs collapsing on power lines.  1500 people reaported without power as of 4 pm in the region.  1 to 3 inches were reported in Rexburg...Rigby...and Shelley.

events.cz_name: BIG AND LITTLE WOOD RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: One foot of snow fell at the Sedgwick Peak SNOTEL site.  7 inches fell at Sheep Mountain and Soda Springs with 5 inches at Wild Horse Divide.  4 inches fell at Somsen Ranch and 3 inches at Pine Creek Pass.
Slug Creek Divide SNOTEL reported 11 inches of snow.  Emigrant Summit reported 5 inches and Giveout 3 inches.
Interstate 15 between Idaho Falls and Roberts shut down at 12:45 PM for over an hour due to zero visibility from blowing dust.  It was closed from milepost 119 to milepost 134.

High winds caused another dust storm between Idaho Falls and Roberts and closed interstate 15 from milepost 119 to 134 from 11 AM through 4:15 pm on November 25th.  Several inches of dust accumulated on the road and a 3 car collision occurred due to the low visibility.

events.cz_name: BIG AND LITTLE WOOD RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: Twelve inches of snow fell at Dollarhide with 9 inches at Galena and 11 inches at Vienna Mine.
Six inches of snow fell at Bear Canyon with 7 inches at Smiley Mountain and 10 inches at Mill Creek Summit.
Spotters reported a foot of snow in the Preston and Weston areas in the Cache Valley.
Spotters reported 16 inches of snow in St Charles and 9 inches in Montpelier.   SNOTEL amounts were 8 inches at Slug Creek, 23 inches at Franklin Basin, and 11 inches at Emigrant Summit.

Snow behind a cold front brought widespread 2 to 4 inch snow amounts to the Lower Snake River Plain with multiple automobile accidents on interstate 15. One rollover occurred in Fort Hall and another rollover occurred in Pocatello just south of the Pocatello Creek southbound on ramp.  Multiple weather related accidents were reported in Blackfoot as well.
Interstate 15 closed between Idaho Falls and Roberts and mileposts 119 to 135 due to strong winds. The winds caused visibilities to drop to zero. The interstate closed at 11:27 AM.
Several snow amounts over 10 inches were recorded in Bear Lake County.  10 inches fell at Slug Creek with 10 inches at Giveout and 13 inches at Franklin Basin.
Extreme cold with -20 to -30 wind chill readings affected the Upper Snake Highlands.
Strong northerly winds of 10 to 20 mph caused wind chill readings of -20 to -25 degrees.
Northerly winds of 10 to 20 mph combined with temperatures in the single digits to bring wind chill readings below -20 degrees.
Thirteen inches of snow fell at Mill Creek Summit SNOTEL site.

events.cz_name: BIG AND LITTLE WOOD RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: Eighteen inches of snow fell at Dollarhide SNOTEL with 10 inches at Galena, 13 inches at Lost Wood Divide, and 25 inches at Vienna Mine.
The Pine Creek Pass SNOTEL reported 9 inches of snow.

Interstate 15 between exits 119 and 135 was closed due to blowing dust caused by dry conditions and winds between 40 and 50 mph.  The interstate was closed between 6:30 am and 6:45 pm.  Visibility was reduced to zero miles along that stretch.
Wind gusts of 50 to 60 mph tore off a metal roof and the flying debris caused damage to the McCammon District Library and a transformer on a power pole knocking out electricity to 20 residents.

Interstate 15 was closed for a second straight day from mile marker 119 to 130 from Idaho Falls to Roberts.  Visibility again reduced to zero miles from blowing dust caused by 30 to 40 mph winds with higher gusts.
Pocatello Airport ASOS recorded a wind gust of 60 mph with a thunderstorm during a cold frontal passage.
Spotter recorded a 75 mph wind gust with a thunderstorm along a strong cold front.
A member of the general public used amateur equipment to measure a 72 mph wind gust at Minidoka.
Bear Canyon received 10 inches of snow with 13 inches recorded at both Smiley Mountain and Mill Creek Summit.
Twenty inches of snow fell at the Black Bear SNOTEL with 16 inches at White Elephant.
Nine inches of snow fell at the Howell Canyon SNOTEL site.
The Slug Creek Divide SNOTEL site recorded 12 inches of snow.

events.cz_name: BIG AND LITTLE WOOD RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: Snow amounts were 13 inches at Dollarhide, 15 inches at Galena, 13 inches at Galena Summit, 13 inches at Lost Wood Divide, and 23 inches at Vienna Mine.
Heavy snow fell above 7000 feet in the Sawtooth region.   50 inches fell at Mill Creek Summit with 14 inches at Smiley Mountain, 10 inches at Stickney Mill, and 15 inches at Bear Canyon.

Heavy snow and wind affectd the Upper Snake Highlands for several days which closed roads as well as schools.   28 inches of snow was recoreded at White Elephant with 10 inches at Island Park.   Teton, Idaho school district 401 was closed on January 19th due to road conditions.  Visibility dropped to near zero on US Highway 20 on the 18th causing a severe traffic accident blocking traffic for 3 hours.   Idaho route 33 was closed from Newdale to Tetonia on January 19th.   Idaho Highway 32 was closed between Tetonia and Ashton due to snow.

Extremely heavy snow amounts occurred in the South Central Highlands.   55 inches fell at Magic Mountain with 23 inches at Oxford Springs, 54 inches at Bostetter Ranger Station, and 58 inches at Howell Canyon.

Several days of heavy snow occurred in the Caribou Highlands with SNOTEL sites recording extreme amounts.   Totals were 29 inches at Pine Creek Pass, 25 inches at Sedgwick Peak, 18 inches at Somsen Ranch, 9 inches at Sheep Mountain, and 10 inches at Wildhorse Divide.
Heavy snow fell for more than two days in the Idaho Wasatch.   17 inches fell at Slug Creek Divide with 28 inches at Emigrant Summit, and 17 inches at Giveout.

events.cz_name: BIG AND LITTLE WOOD RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: A multiple day winter storm brought incredible snow amounts to the Big and Little Wood River Region.   An amazing 77 inches was recorded at Vienna Mine with 22 inches at Swede Peak, 34 inches at Lost Wood Divide, 22 inches at Chocolate Gulch, 17 inches at Garfield Ranger Station, 41 inches at Galena, 35 inches at Galena Summit, and 18 inches at Hyndman.
Multiple day snow amounts were 13 inches at Morgan Creek and 23 inches at Meadow Lake.
A strong Pacific storm brought heavy snow to the Sawtooth region.   22 inches fell at Banner Summit with 12 inches at Mill Creek Summit, and 14 inches at Stickney Mill.
Eleven inches of snow fell at Black Bear with 10 inches at Crab Creek and 11 inches at Island Park.
Nineteen inches of snow fell at Bostetter Ranger Station.
Eleven inches of snow fell at Pine Creek Pass with 11 inches at Somsen Ranch and 19 inches at Wildhorse Divide.
Sixteen inches of snow fell at Emigrant Summit with 17 inches at Slug Creek Divide.

events.cz_name: BIG AND LITTLE WOOD RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: Spotters reported 10 inches of snow at Hailey and 11 inches at Bellevue.   SNOTEL sites were: 15 inches at Chocolate Gulch, 19 inches at Garfield Ranger Station, 14 inches at Galena Summit, 19 inches at Hyndman, and 12 inches at Vienna Mine.
Eighteen inches of snow fell at Meadow Lake with 10 inches at Morgan Creek.

Several thousand dollars worth of damage due to flooding from extensive rainfall during the week. In Oneida County highways 36 and 38 damaged with mud and debris. Old Highway 191 near Malad Summit covered with mud and debris also.

Several thousand dollars worth of damage due to flooding from extensive rainfall during the week. In Lincoln County two rural houses flooded along with several road washouts.  Much of 420N washed out along with 720N 825 E and several BLM roads.   Several roads damaged in the city of Shoshone.

Interstate 15 between the cities of Idaho Falls and Roberts was closed for more than 24 hours due to blowing dust caused by strong winds. It was closed from January 18th around noon through January 19th at 5:30 PM.
A semi tractor-trailer flipped due to 60 mph winds 5 miles north of McCammon at 11:30 AM on interstate 15.  Wind gust of 60 mph measured 20 miles northwest of Soda Springs.

Fifteen hundred people were without power in the Pocatello and Chubbuck area due to wind caused power outages.  Taco Johns in Pocatello had a sign blown over by the wind.  Extensive roof shingle damage was reported in Pocatello.

Sustained winds of 40 to 50 mph with gusts of 60 to 75 mph were widespread in the Upper Snake River Highlands.  70 to 80 mph wind  gusts were recorded at Atomic City, Craters of the Moon and several INL observation towers.  In Idaho Falls several homes reported roof and shingle damage.  The Red Lion hotel lost parts of its roof as did the Stop and Shop in Firth.   During the peak of the storm Idaho Power reported 4,400 people without power.
An observer measured a 78 mph wind gust at Bern.   Power outages occurred in Bern and Pegram.  Several roofs damaged.
Sustained 40 to 50 mph winds with gusts of 60 to 70 mph were present in the Eastern Magic Valley.   Minidoka carried a gust of 68 mph and Richfield a gust of 65 mph.
Sustained winds of 40 to 50 mph continued most of the day with gusts of 63 mph measured at Malta and 64 mph measured at Moburg Canyon.

Sheet flooding reported from Devil Creek Reservoir north to Malad summit along the old highway.  Near intersection of State Highway 38 and 17200 West water flowing over readways with several fields flooding.  0.40 inches of rain reported near Holbrook.  From Arbon town site south to Highway 38 creeks rising.  North Road washed out and South Road under two feet of water.   Three feet of standing water in fields near Holbrook.

Portneuf and Inkom Roads near Inkom closed due to running water on roadways with debris.  Flooded sections of road destroyed and replaced.  Garden Drive in Chubbuck flooded in a thousand foot stretch covered with several inches of water.
Flooding along old Highway 30 between Bancroft and Pebble reported by emergency manager.
Several roads flooded with debris in the southern part of the Arbon Valley due to rain and snow melt.

Extensive flooding of houses occurred in Ammon and just southeast of Ririe in Bonneville County.  Homes along Tildy Lane and Tildy Circle had basements flooded with several feet of water in Ammon as a canal overflowed from snow melt.  The neighborhoods near 55th East and Lincoln Road and the Cortland Ridge neighbrohood near Woodland Elementary school in Ammon also affected by the flooding.  Birch Creek near Ririe flooded causing flooding at a home on US Route 26 and 160th East Road.
One of the canals in Newdale was broken open due to possible home flooding and it was breached into fields near Rexburg.
Mill Creek Summit northeast of Stanley reported 22 inches of snow.
Widespread heavy snow occurred in the Upper Snake River Highlands.   Crab Creek reported 16 inches with Island Park getting 20 inches and White Elephant 28 inches.
Several high elevation sites in the South Central Highlands reported heavy snow totals.  Bostetter Ranger Station reported 17 inches with 22 inches at Howell Canyon and 12 inches at Oxford Springs.

The following snow amounts were reported at SNOTEL sites in the Caribou Highlands:  24 inches at Pine Creek Pass, 25 inches at Sedgwick Peak, 16 inches at Somsen Ranch, 10 inches at Sheep Mountain, and 15 inches at Wildhorse Divide.
The following snow amounts were reported at SNOTEL sites in the Idaho portion of the Wasatch Mountains:  17 inches at Emigrant Summit, 14 inches at Giveout, and 33 inches at Slug Creek Divide.

events.cz_name: BIG AND LITTLE WOOD RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: Heavy snow fell at high elevation SNOTEL sites in the Wood River region.  19 inches fell at Dollarhide Summit with 14 inches at Galena Summit, 10 inches at Lost Wood Divide, and 26 inches at Vienna Mine.
Ten inches of snow fell at Hilts Creek with 11 inches at Meadow Lake and 11 inches at Morgan Creek.

Interstate 15 was closed from Idaho Falls to Roberts due to blowing dust.  A large pine tree was downed on Ada Avenue in Idaho Falls as the strong winds completely uprooted it.  Also in Idaho Falls the Cal Ranch sotre sign was destroyed on Anderson Street and the sign of Salon 720 on Holmes Avenue also destroyed.   66 mph wind gusts in Taber, 61 mph in Idaho Falls and 69 mph in Atomic City recorded.
Sixty-five mph winds measured in Fort Hall with 69 mph in the city of Pocatello and 59 mph at the Pocatello regional airport.   MInor damage reported throughout Pocatello.
Winds of 40 to 50 mph sustained with several gusts over 60 mph reported.   Minidoka reported 65 mph.   61 mph  was reported at Rupert and 64 mph reported at Richfield.
Sixty mph wind gust recorded at Moburg Canyon with widespread 40 to 50 mph sustained winds.
HIghways 87, 47, 32, and 20 were all closed due to snow and strong winds causing blowing snow.   Other roadways in Teton and Fremont Counties also closed due to the blowing and drifting snow.

events.cz_name: BIG AND LITTLE WOOD RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: Sixteen inches of snow fell at Vienna Mine with 6 inches at Galena Summit and 5 inches at Garfield Ranger Station.
US Highway 30 closed from Soda Springs to 3 miles west of Georgetown due to high winds and blowing snow.
The Sawtooth Mountains had heavy snow with widespread amounts over 9 inches.  Bear Canyon reported 9 inches.  Mill Creek Summit reported 9 inches as well as 12 inches at Smiley Mountain.

Heavy snow fell in the Upper Snake Highlands with the following snow amounts:  17 inches at Crab Creek, 10 inches at Island Park, and 21 inches at White Elephant.   The storm spilled over into March 1st and schools were closed on March 1st in Fremont County due to the overnight snow of February 29th continuing into the early morning hours of the 1st of March.   Those schools were also released early on February 29th in the afternoon.
US Highways 26 and 33 were closed due to heavy snow and reduced visibilities due to blowing snow between Ririe and Swan Valley.  10 inches of snow was recorded at Sedgwick Peak.
Nine inches of snow recorded at Emigrant Summit.

events.cz_name: BIG AND LITTLE WOOD RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: Heavy snow amounts were the following:  9 inches at Chocolate Gulch, 20 inches at Dollarhide Summit, 12 inches at Garfield Ranger Station, 12 inches at Galena, 15 inches at Galena Summit, 9 inches at Hyndman, 9 inches at Lost Wood Divide, 12 inches at Swede Peak, and 21 inches at Vienna Mine.
Ten inches of snow was recorded at Hilts Creek and Meadow Lake.
Nine inches of snow fell at Banner Summit.  16 inches fell at Bear Canyon with 34 inches at Stickney Mill and 26 inches at Smiley Mountain.
Ten inches fell at White Elephant and 11 inches at Black Bear SNOTEL.

events.cz_name: BIG AND LITTLE WOOD RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: Sixteen inches of snow fell at Vienna Mine.   Other significant totals were:  Swede Peak 10 inches, Hyndman 9 inches, Lost Wood Divide 16 inches, Galena Summit 12 inches, Galena 11 inches, and Dollarhide Summit 14 inches.
Nine inches of snow fell at Medow Lake SNOTEL with 17 inches at Hilts Creek.
Heavy snow fell at SNOTEL sites in the Sawtooth Mountains.  Total amounts were:  20 inches at Bear Canyon, 11 inches at Mill Creek Summit, and 26 inches at Smiley Mountain.

events.cz_name: BIG AND LITTLE WOOD RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: SNow amounts at SNOTEL sites were:  10 inches at Dollarhide Summit, 11 inches at Galena, 17 inches at Galena Summit, 11 inches at Hyndman, 14 inches at Lost Wood Divide, 9 inches at Swede Peak, and 21 inches at Vienna Mine.

Extensive sheet flooding occurred in the March 10th to March 20th time frame from St Anthony to Ashton and Chester.   In the chester/Hog Hollow area damage occurred to road 3100 East.  Serious damage occurred to graveled road 800 North and several county roads in the Hog Hollow area.  Major erosion damage at the enterprise Canal Bridge occurred.  Private property damage occurred on a private road on 700 North just east of 3100 East.  By March 15th county Road 3000 East north of Twin Bridges was closed.  A Disaster Declaration was declared in Fremont County on March 15th.  Moderate damage occurred on County Road 3200 East due to runoff.  Heavy flooding occurred in Chester near County road 1000 North and 3000 East closing those roads.  Hog Hollow Road was closed due to significant damage.  Several pastures covered with 2 to 3 feet of water.  HIghway 32 was flooded but remained open.  Extensive flooding in Ashton and damage to the sewage lagoon.  Two residences in Ashton had water in basements.

Localized flooding occurred in Dubois from March 10th through the 17th caused by melting snow on frozen ground as well as ice jams in Beavercreek.  Local flooding of streets occurred as well as some water in basements but substantial property damage was avoided.

Runoff from snowmelt in the hills around Slaughterhouse Canyon east of Bellevue caused extensive runnign water to flood local roads in Bellevue.  Water reached 2 feet deep against houses and garage doors but only minor house flooding occurred with no significant damage.  Extensive sandbagging protected most homes from the rising waters.
The INTEC/Grid 3 INL site measured a peak wind of 67 mph reaching severe criteria at 18:55 EST.
Fifty-nine mph wind gust measured at Atomic City.
Fifty knot wind gust measured at the Gas Caves RAWS site from thunderstorm wind.

Post cold frontal winds combined with freshly tilled fields to cause a massive dust storm along interstate 84 in the Burley area.  The reduced visibility caused one massive pileup involving 18 cars in a major accident.  East bound traffic was shut down for several hours along the interstate.   Two people were taken to the hospital but there were no fatalities or serious injuries reported.
High winds tore off a canopy atop gas pumps at the Valley Wide Coop store around 5 pm. It damaged two vehicles.
Thunderstorm winds destroyed flag pole and chicken coop at residence in Roberts and items blown 200 feet from house.
Widespread 40 to 50 mph sustained winds occurred at the Idaho National Laboratory with gusts of 60 to 70 mph.   The winds damaged a building under construction at around 5 pm MDT.
For the 2nd day in a row high winds were widespread at the Idaho National Laboratory. Measured sustained winds of 50 mph occurred at times with gusts over 60 mph.

Three fires which were all man made occurred in Bannock County.  One was near the Power County border near West Siphon Road and started on a salvage yard and high winds pushed it through 20 acres of land burning cars, propane tanks.  In Chubbuck a fire started between Ward and Laurel Drives and two unoccupied homes were destroyed in the quarter acre fire.  It also got into an industrial yard burning a fence and pallets.  In Pocatello a brush fire covered 60 acres off of Sunrise Way and Satterfield Drive.   The fire cost fire departments $25,000 and Bannock County was declared a disaster area at 6 pm MDT.

A fire began 6 miles west of Shelley on June 17th and extremely strong winds through June 18th expanded it to 300 acres.  The fire occurred in the lava fields without significant fuel and was 100 percent contained by the evening of the 19th.

A 50 acre wildfire began just east of exit 80 off of interstate 15 near Fort Hall on June 19th.  The fire began at 6 pm EDT and threatened homes and area structires.  the fire was contained at 8 pm and was in total control by June 20th.
A one-hundred acre fire developed 16 miles east of Blackfoot June 20th.
A 385 acre fire developed just east of Dubois on June 21st.  It was under control by the afternoon of June 22nd.
A 200 acre fire developed 11 miles northeast of Preston on June 22nd.  It was human caused and was contained by by June 23rd.
An 88 acre wildfire began on June 23rd 11 miles east of Blackfoot.  The fire was contained by the evening of June 24th.
A wildfire began about 2 pm MDT 3 miles south of Firth on June 25th.  It only covered a few acres but destroyed a barn in it's path.  It was a grass fire and the estimated damage was $20,000.
A wildfire began June 26th 3 miles north of Malad City and burned 351 acres.

A planned controlled burn blew out of control on June 29th.  The planned burn of 180 acries ended up burning 1100 acres near the town of Bancroft in Caribou County.  Local fire departments were able to have the fire controlled by 9 pm and no structures were damaged on the private land fire.

A 1038 acre wildfire began at about 2:30 PM on June 28th in the Charlotte Road area of Mink Creek just south of Pocatello.  About one-thousand people were evacuated from their homes.  The Gibson Jack, Johnny Creek and Mink Creek area down to Portneuf Road were all evacuated in the afternoon.  Bannock County commissioners issued a disaster delaration for Bannock County.   66 homes were eventually destroyed by the fire along with 29 outbuildings and numerous motor vehicles.  The cost of fighting the fire was estimated at 2 million dollars.  Property damage estimates were 472 million dollars.   The fire was contained by Monday July 2nd.
Seventy-eight mile per hour wind gust recorded at Burley airport with power outages in Cassia County and trees downed.

Minidoka County sherriff office reported power outages with trees taking down power lines. Roofs and buildings damaged and wheel lines blown into roads.   Most of the damage reported in the city of Rupert.
Lightning started an 8 thousand acre fire 11 miles west of Springfield on July 10th.  The fire continued on open land and did not threaten any structures.
Lightning started a 9 thousand acre fire 4 miles southwest of Atomic City on July 10th.  This fire damaged no buildings or structures.

Lightning began an 800 acre fire 23 miles southwest of Pocatello on July 11th.   The fire grew to 8000 acres before being contained.  Power County officials closed Knox and Big Canyon Roads on July 12th to keep traffic away from the flames.  No structures were damaged.
Lightning started the Rooster Rock Fire on July 11th.   The fire consumed 2500 acres about 15 miles southwest of Pocatello.  It did threaten two structures but did no damage prior to containment.
Lightning started a 1200 acre fire 4 miles southeast of Atomic City.    It was contained on open land with no damage.
A 700 acre fire caused by lightning began on July 22nd and ocurred in between American Falls and Minidoka over open fields.
Lightning started a 34,000 acre fire 10 miles southeast of Shoshone.   It occurred in open land and no damage occurred to structures.

Lightning started a fire 7 miles northwest of Stanley on July 27th.   By the end of the month the fire had grown to nearly 4,000 acres.  Several hiking trails were closed becasue of the fire.   The fire continued for multiple months eventually growing to well over 100,000 acres.
Lightning caused a wildfire about 10 to 15 miles east of Blackfoot over open land. The fire eventually grew to 16,000 acres and continued to burn into August. The lightning struck on July 27th.

A thunderstorm downed trees onto power lines and 3 thousand people lost power in the Chubbuck area.  Several branches blown off trees and a small fire started due to a transformer blowing out.  Some minor damage to houses as well occurred.

The Halstead fire approximately 18 miles northwest of Stanley which began on July 27th grew to nearly 128,000 acres by the end of August.  The following closures went into effect on August 3rd:  all access points to the Cape Horn Area, all access to the Seafoam Bubble, all access to the Frank Church River of no Return Wilderness east of the Middle Fork Wild and Scenic Corridor, east of bluebunch ridge, and north of Lola Creek, National Forest lands north of Hwy 21 and 75 to Sunbeam and west of Yankee Fork Road to Loon Creek Guard Station.   The Pinyon Peak Road was closed in its entirety.   All of the campgrounds listed were closed:  Beaver Creek, Lola Creek, Marsh Creek transfer, Josephus Lake, Bench, Banner, Park City, Elk Creek, Sheep Trail, Trap Creek, Vader Creek and Thatcher Creek.   HIghway 75 was closed between Lower Stanley and Gardner Creek.

Lightning strikes started several fies on August 5th in what became known as the Minidoka Complex.   The largest of these was the Cave Canyon Fire.   The wildfire was about 15 miles southeast of Twin Falls and eventually grew to 88,909 acres.  The fire became 100 percent contained on August 16th.  No property damage occurred and the main closures were forest service roads.
Lightning started two wildfires east of Pocatello in the mountains on August 8th. Both the Marsh Creek and South Toponts Wildfires grew to around 100 acres before being contained.
A fire started by lightning on August 28th grew to 420 acres and destroyed 2 homes about 20 miles west of Montpelier.  Several temporary evacuations were ordered in the mountainous terrain.
A 700 acre wildfire began on August 27th about 10 miles south of Arco in the lava fields burning grass and brush. No property was threatened by the blaze.

The Connor Creek wildfire began at around noon on August 29th about 2 miles east of Elba.   The fire grew to 2,000 acres before being contained.  Numerous primary residences were within 1 mile of the fire but none were lost.
At mile post 169 on highway 26 four trees and 2 power lines were downed by thunderstorm winds.  Power lines fell on the highway and only one lane was open for several hours.
The Minidoka mesonet site measured a 60 mph wind gust.
A 58 mph wind gust was recorded in northeast Bingham County at a weather site at the Idaho National Laboratory.
A tornado was spotted with confirmation with photos east of Declo.   The tornado occurred in open land and caused no damage and was not long lasting.
A weak tonado was confirmed with photographs about 4 to 5 miles east northeast of Albion.   It was in open land and did no damage.
Idaho Power lost three 60 foot towers near East Road in American Falls.
On September 10th winds downed a power line in Egin and 4,300 Fremont County residents lost power for about 4 hours from 3 pm EDT to about 7 pm EDT.

The Halstead Fire which began on July 27th continued to burn about 18 miles north of Stanley through the month of September reaching a size of 179,000 acres.   The fire approximately 18 miles north of Stanley continued and cuased occasional air quality alerts throughout the area to the east and southeast of the region.  by the end of the month it was considered nearly 75 percent contained.

A strong Pacific cold front moved through southeast Idaho the morning of October 16th and brought strong winds to the Snake River Plain.  A 7,000 square foot wooden shed was destroyed by 70 mph wind gusts in American Falls.  Damage was estimated at $150,000.  Also near American Falls an irrigation pivot tower was downed along with 3 power poles near Neely.   A tree was downed in Pocatello on Mountain Drive with tree damage south of Pocatello.
A strong Pacific cold front moved through southeast Idaho the morning of October 16th and brought strong winds to the Snake River Plain.  72 mph winds were measured at Craters of the Moon.
Six to 10 inches of snow fell in Sugar City and Rexburg.  Madison County sheriff's office reported mulltiple minor automobile accidents.   A pair of semis slid off of US Highway 20 near Thornton.
Eight to 12 inches of snow fell in Ashton and St. Anthony.

Snowfall in the Lower Snake River Plain on the evening of the 25th only measured 2 to 4 inches but the road problems it created caused one fatality.   On the morning of the 26th, a Chubbuck man age 62 lost control of his pickup truck on Highway 39 near American Falls and slid into the opposite lane and was hit by an oncoming semi truck.   Two accidents occurred on interstate 15 near Pocatello between midnight and 5 am on the 26th as well.

events.cz_name: BIG AND LITTLE WOOD RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: Nine inches of snow fell at Galena with 10 inches at Galena Summit.   Heavy snow also fell at Lost Wood Divide with 10 inches and Vienna Mine with 18 inches.
Ten inches of snow fell at Bear Canyon and Mill Creek Summit with 13 inches at Smiley Mountain.

A powerful Pacific storm system brought 3 days of heavy snow to elevations above 7000 feet.  38 inches fell at Smiley Mountain with 28 inches at Mill Creek Summit and a storm high of 43 inches at Bear Canyon.
Eighteen inches of snow fell at Black Bear with 34 inches at White Elephant.

events.cz_name: BIG AND LITTLE WOOD RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: Heavy snow fell above 7 thousand feet as a very moist Pacific system moved slowly through the region.   42 inches fell at Dollarhide Summit at 8,420 feet.   28 inches fell at Galena Summit with 31 inches at Hyndman and 29 inches at Lost Wood Divide.
A strong and wet Pacific storm system brought 27 inches of snow to Hilt's Creek.
Fifteen to twenty automobile accidents occurred in the Pocatello area as freezing rain began in the early morning hours on the 10th and continued through morning rush hour.

Sustained 40 mph winds occurred in the Upper Snake River Plain from early morning through noon on the 17th.  Atomic City, Ririe, Rover site and several INL sites reported the over 40 mph sustained winds.
SNOTEL sites reporting heavy snow were:  Smiley Mountain with 11 inches, Mill Creek Summit with 11 inches, and Bear Canyon with 12 inches.
The White Elephant SNOTEL site reported 18 inches of snow.
The Sedgwick Peak SNOTEL site recorded 10 inches of snow.

events.cz_name: BIG AND LITTLE WOOD RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: Trinaed spotters reported 8 inches of snow in Bellevue and 9 inches in Hailey.   SNOTEL snow amounts were: 13 inches at Swede Peak, 14 inches at Lost Wood Divide, 12 inches at Hyndman, 12 inches at Galena Summit, 13 inches at Galena, 11 inches at Garfield Ranger Station, and 12 inches at Chocolate Gulch.
Ten inches of snow fell at Emigrant Summit.

events.cz_name: BIG AND LITTLE WOOD RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: Snowfall totals at SNOTEL sites were the following:  Galena Summit 13 inches, Galena 12 inches, Chocolate Gulch 9 inches, Vienna Mine 11 inches, and Swede Peak 9 inches.
Wind chill readings of 20 to 30 below zero were recorded at Minidoka with 10 to 20 mph sustained northeast winds.

The West Jefferson School District number 253 was closed on January 3rd due to extreme cold conditions.   Wind chill readings of 20 to 35 below zero were common with northeast sustained winds of 10 to 25 mph during the early morning hours.

Wind chill readings of 20 to 30 below zero were widespread on the morning of January 3rd.  Grace School District number 148 and North Gem School District 149 were closed due to the extreme cold conditions.

events.cz_name: BIG AND LITTLE WOOD RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: Six inches of snow fell in Hailey and Bellevue by the morning of the 10th.   SNOTEL measurements were:  9 inches at Vienna Mine, 12 inches at Lost Wood Divide, 9 inches at Dollarhide Summit, 9 inches at Galena, and 13 inches at Galena Summit.

Five inches of snow fell in Shoshone in the early morning hours on the 10th.   A combination of snow and wind caused early closing of schools on the 10th in Cassia County, Minidoka County as well as the Richfield schools.    Snowfall amounts ranged from 2 to 6 inches in the region.

Snow and strong winds caused over 70 accidents in the Lower Snake River Plain based on police and state highway reports on the 10th and 11th.   The city of Blackfoot closed schools one hour early on the 10th.   Blackfoot and Pocatello schools were closed on the 11th along with Idaho State University.   Snow amounts ranged from 3 inches at the Pocatello airport to 5 inches in Chubbuck and Pocatello with 7 inches on the benches east of Pocatello.    Around 6 inches fell in Blackfoot.
A Pacific storm brought heavy snowfall to the Caribou Highlands.   20 inches fell at Wildhorse Divide with 13 inches at Sedgick Peak.   The Pebble Creek Ski Area received 16 inches.

The city of Rigby reported blizzard conditions at 350 pm on the 10th with visilibity under one quarter mile and snow covered roads.  Idaho National Laboratory Contractors released early due to snow and blowing snow.   Snowfall amounts ranged from 2 to 6 inches in the region.   Over 30 traffic accidents reported as well.
HIghway 36 between Preston and Dayton was closed late on the morning of the 10th through the 11th.   6 to 12 inch snowfall amounts occurred with extensive blowing and drifting of the snow.
Eleven inches of snow reported at Bear Canyon and 9 inches at Smiley Mountain.
One foot of snow fell at Kilgore with 7 inches at Dubois.   Nine inches fell at Victor with 10 in Chester.   SNOTEL reports were:  17 inches at White elephant, 13 inches at Crab Creek.

A Pacific storm brought high wind and heavy snow to the South Central Highlands.  INterstate 84 was closed from the Utah state line to Interstate 86.  Highway 81 was closed from Malta to Declo.   SNOTEL snowfall amounts were:  37 inches at Magic Mountain, 22 inches at Bostetter Ranger Station, and 47 inches at Howell Canyon.
Blizzard conditions reported in Bern on the evening of the 10th with zero visibility and 50 mph wind gusts.   Emigrant Summit reported 14 inches of snow.

Heavy snow and strong winds occurred as a strong Pacific storm moved through the region.   SNOTEL snow amounts were the following:  Meadow Lake 9 inches, Morgan Creek 19 inches, and Hilts Creek 14 inches.
Temperatures colder than 20 degrees below zero forced school closures in the Bonneville, Idaho Falls, and West Jefferson schools.
Temperatures below 20 degrees below zero caused the Marsh Valley schools to be closed on the 14th.
Bear Lake schools closed on the 14th as temperatures dropped to below 20 degrees below zero.

Ten inches of snow fell in Rexburg.  7 inches fell in both Rigby and Idaho Falls from the 27th through the morning of the 28th.  Ririe, Shelley, Firth, Bonneville, Idaho Falls, Jefferson County, and Snake River schools were all closed on the 28th.
A spotter reported 10 inches of snow 6 miles west southwest of Malta.   Bostetter Ranger Station reported 13 inches of snow.   Howell Canyon had 14 inches and Oxford Springs had 13.
The Sedgwick Peak SNOTEL site reported 10 inches of snow.
Emigrant Summit measured 13 inches of snow.

Blizzard conditions affected much of the region.   13 inches of snow fell in Ashton with 11 inches at Crab Creek and 15 inches at the White Elephant SNOTEL.  Idaho route 32 was closed from Tetonia to Ashton due to reduced visibilities and blowing snow.  At times snow fell at the rate of 2 inches per hour in Ashton.

Four to 6 inches of snow fell in Idaho Falls with 8 inches in Rexburg.  Strong winds brought several minor accidents on roadways.  Wind gusts up to 40 mph caused visibilities to drop to under 1/4 of a mile.  The winds caused three cross-arms supporting power lines to break around 2:47 a.m.   The break caused a power outage for 181 customers until 2:30 p.m.

Strong winds and heavy snow caused blizzard conditions with the visibility at the Pocatello regional airport 1/4 mile or less for 3 hours in the morning.   4 to 6 inch snowfall was common in Chubbuck and Pocatello during the day on the 23rd.  Several minor traffic accidents were reported.
Seventeen inches of snow fell at Howell Canyon.   50 to 70 mph wind gusts were common throughout the morning of the 23rd throughout the South Central Highlands.
Heavy snow and winds created visibilities near zero causing US Route 26 to be closed from Ririe to Swan Valley.   9 inches of snow fell at Sheep Mountain with 14 inches at Wildhorse Divide.

events.cz_name: BIG AND LITTLE WOOD RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: Nine inches of snow fell at Dollarhide with 11 inches at Vienna Mine.
One to 3 inches of snow and winds in excess of 30 mph caused Idaho route 33 to be closed from Newdale to Tetonia for an hour and a half on the morning of the 17th.

A strong cold frontal brought light snow and wind gusts in excess of 50  mph.   1 to 3 inches of snow was common but blowing and drifting snow caused reduced visibilities and a three car collision claimed the life of a 12 year old girl on route 89 near Paris, Idaho.

A heavy snow shower caused slick roads and reduced visibilities on Highway 37 just north of Rockland. The conditions caused a two car collision which resulted in a fatality at around 6:15 pm on March 22nd. One to 4 inches of snow was common across the region during the day on the 22nd.

Emigrant Summit reported 6 inches of snow. Giveout reported 5 inches of snow and Slug Creek Divide reported 9 inches of snow. Power lines were downed due to wet snow at 2 pm on the 8th in Paris and at 10 pm in Montpelier. The power was out in Montpelier from 10 pm on the 8th until 2:30 am on the 9th.

Fifty to 60 mph wind gusts caused a dust storm on interstate 86 in between Chubbuck and American Falls reducing visibility to zero. The visibility caused a 16 car crash west of the Arbon Valley/Rainbow Road exit between American Falls and Chubbuck. Both lanes of a 12 mile stretch of interstate 86 was closed from 4:45 until 9:45 pm between exits 49 and 61.  A peak wind gust of 55 mph was measured at the ASOS at the Pocatello Regional Airport.

Widespread 50 to 70 mph wind gusts occurred behind the passage of a strong cold front.   Taber measured 68 mph for a peak wind with 62 mph at Atomic city, 56 mph at Idaho Falls, and 57 mph at Rexburg.
Fifty to 60 mph wind gusts occurred throughout the Magic Valley.   Minidoka had a peak gust of 59 mph at 4 pm.

Fifty to 65 mph wind gusts were common throughout the Lower Snake River Plain.   Blackfoot recorded a 61 mph wind with 57 mph at fort Hall and 55 mph at Pocatello.   winds blew off 6 feet of siding from a Chubbuck residence.

A very strong cold front passed through eastern Idaho and wind gusts of 55 to 75 mph occurred in the Upper Snake River Plain. The Idaho Falls airport peaked at 67 mph at 3:41 pm. Craters of the Moon recorded a 69 mph gust. A 100 year old tree fell at the Tautphaus Zoo in Idaho Falls and trees also fell at Pinecrest Golf course in the city. Interstate 15 was shut down for hours in between Idaho Falls and Roberts.  2,460 Rocky Mountain Power customers were without power in Idaho Falls and Ammon for several hours.   Power was restored after 5 pm MDT.
