Sustained winds of 58 mph were measured 7 miles southeast of Ashton with gusts to 67 mph.   A power pole was downed in Fremont County.   Idaho Highway 32 was closed from Tetonia to Ashton due to high winds and reduced visibility in blowing dust.
A weak tornado was confirmed with photographs and radar signatures just southeast of Monteview between 4:10 pm MDT to 4:20 MDT.  The tornado was in open fields and no damage occurred.
The Fremont County emergency manager took several well defined photographs of a dust devil east of Newdale at around 1:15 pm MDT.
One inch hail reported in city of Chubbuck.
One inch hail reported at corner of Pocatello Creek Road and Alameda.
One inch hail reported at home of National Weather Service Employee.
One inch hail reported by National Weather Serivice employee in the town of Palisades.

Lightning damage occurred in Blackfoot.   One home on S Adams Ave had a window blown out with siding damage and damage to utility lines and appliances in the house.  A telephone was knocked down near the courthouse.   A trailer at the Sage Hill Travel Center was struck by lightning and destroyed.

Sustained winds of 50 to 60 mph began near Howe and Craters of the Moon at around 130 pm MDT and continued through 4 pm MDT.   The highest gust of 82 MPH was recorded at Craters of the Moon at 310 pm MDT.
Fifty-five to 60 mph sustained winds were measured at Hamer and Monteview between 115 and 140 pm MDT.   60 mph wind gusts were measured at Terreton at 4 pm MDT.
A 21 month old girl died in Ammon when she was accidentally left in an automoblie and suffered heat stroke.

Around 100 acres burned on the South Blackrock Wildfire near Inkom.   Blackroad Road was shut down in the area.   The fire was caused by lightning and began on June 29th.   It was contained by July 1st.

The Kimama Wildfire was caused by a lightning strike on June 29th and grew to 300 acres.   The fire was located 3 miles northwest of Paul and was contained by the afternoon of June 30th.    No structures were threatened.
The Pocatello regional airport set record high temperatures three consecutive days.   It was 99 on the 28th, 101 on the 29th and 97 on the 30th.
Three record high temperatures were set at the Idaho Falls Fanning Field airport.  It was 93 on the 27th, 99 on the 29th and 97 on the 30th.
Stanley had record high temperatures of 90 on the 29th and 88 on the 30th.
Challis set a record high temperature of 93 degrees on the 27th.
Burley set a record high temperature of 98 degrees on the 28th.

The Two and a Half Mile Road Fire began by lightning on June 29th and continued through July 3rd before being contained.   The fire was about one mile east of Fort Hall.  The fire was about 1100 acres and grew nearly 1000 acres on July 1st due to swirling and gusty winds.   Only one home was evacuated due to the fire.
Custer County Sheriffs office reported 1 foot of water near Garden Creek affecting power and telephone poles.
Multiple trees downed in Shoshone with power outages reported.   5000 dollars worth of damage reported from tree limbs falling onto a house.
Numerous downed trees in DIetrich area.   One tree limb fell onto RV in Dietrich causing 1 thousand dollars worth of damage.
Mesonet site at Richfield measured a 61 mph wind gust at 8:13 pm MDT.
Craters of the Moon Park had a 61 mph thunderstorm wind gust recorded.
The Shoshone mesonet site recorded a 64 mph thunderstorm wind gust.
Sixty-seven mph wind gust in thunderstorm recorded at Taber.
Spotter in Bern with wind equipment measured 65 mph thunderstorm wind gust.
A tree was downed by winds in Chubbuck falling on two automobiles on Bonanza Avenue between Hawthorne Road and Teton Street.
Heavy rain in thunderstorms caused flooding of one house south of Spencer.
Flash flooding occurred in Pocatello with a foot of water at the Center Street overpass and over 8 inches of water flooding intersections north of Center Street on the Idaho State Campus.

Tornado spotted by public who took photograph of tornado 3 miles west southwest of Wardboro in between Paris and Dingle.   No damage reported as tornado occurred in open area.    Tornado was on the ground at approximately 7:30 pm MDT.
An 8 foot by 10 foot shed blown down by thunderstorm winds in Burley.
Tree blown down 7 miles north northeast of Declo in the Jackson area.
A severe thunderstorm produced a 67 mph wind gust at 3:50 MDT at Aberdeen.
The Moburg Canyon RAWS site reported a 58 mph wind gust at 11:54 am MDT due to a thunderstorm.

The Lodgepole Fire was detected on July 20th about 10 miles west of the city of Challis.   Many evacuations and closures took place in response.  The Mosquito Campground and Mill Creek Campground were closed as well as all roads leading to those areas.   Challis Creek Road, Jeff Flats Road and Sleeping Deer Road were all closed.  Challis Creek was evacuated on July 22nd and was evacuated at times through the end of the month by the Custer County sheriff.   Power lines would occasionally be shut off in the Challis Creek area due to safety reasons for the public and firefighters.  Lodge pole pine and Douglas Fir were the main fuels.   787 personnel were deployed to the incident to fight the fire.   By July 31st the fire had burned 20,132 acres and was 15 percent contained.
Arco ARL site measured 69 mph wind.
The ARL Materials Fuels Complex measured a 61 mph thunderstorm wind gust.
The ARL Rover site measured a 64 mph wind gust in a thunderstorm.
A thunderstorm wind gust of 68 mph was measured at the Dubois ARL site.
The Cox's Well ARL site measured a thunderstorm wind gust of 67 mph.
The ITD site at the INL Puzzle recorded a thunderstorm wind gust of 65 mph.
A thunderstorm wind gust of 60 mph was recorded at the base of Howe Peak.
Big Southern Butte recorded a 72 mph thunderstorm wind gust.
The Lead Draw was a 160 acre fire southeast of Scout Mountain that began July 27th and was contained on July 29th.
The 210 Road Fire was a 300 acre fire near Stanley that began July 22nd and was contained July 29th.
The Emery wildfire was a 600 acre fire which began on July 1st and was contained by July 6th.   It was located about 10 miles south of Oakley.
The Jim Brown wildfire was a lightning started wildfire on July 1st 6 miles southeast of Richfield that grew to 14,444 acres before being contained and controlled on July 6th.
The 175 acre Guinn fire was about 6 miles south of Declo and began July 7th.  It was contained and controlled by July 9th.

events.cz_name: BIG AND LITTLE WOOD RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: The Star Gulch fire was started by lightning on July 16th located near the city of Bellevue. It grew to 150 acres and was controlled by July 17th.

The Brown Butte wildfire was located about 10 miles northeast of Shoshone.   It began on July 21st and was controlled by July 23rd.   It burned over 7000 acres.   No homes or structures were threatened.
The Bradley wildfire northwest of Stanley was reported on July 20th and only grew to 50 acres but caused the Bradley Boy Scout Camp and campers to be evacuated. It was controlled by July 24th.

The Wolverine wildfire was started by lightning on July 31st and quickly grew to 250 acres.  It was located about 9 miles east of Firth.  It was contained and controlled by August 2nd.   Thunderstorm downdrafts caused initial explosive growth but no structured were threatened.
A COOP observer in Bern measured a 72 mph wind gust in a thunderstorm.
One inch hail measured in Shoshone.

Heavy rain with 2 to 4 inch amounts in the Chubbuck and Pocatello area caused extensive street, business and home flooding on August 23rd.  The Center Street underpass was closed.   Pocatello Avenue, Seventh Street, North Main and Highway 30 at the railroad bridge, Gold Street overpass, Cedar Street, Pole Line Road, Eldredge Road were closed in Pocatello.   The Interstate 86 underpass on Hawthorne Road in Chubbuck was closed.   The heavy rain began at around 2 pm with the flooding continuing until about 7 pm in the two cities.

The Lodgepole Fire was detected on July 20th about 10 miles west of the city of Challis. Many evacuations and closures took place in response. The Mosquito Campground and Mill Creek Campground were closed as well as all roads leading to those areas. Challis Creek Road, Jeff Flats Road and Sleeping Deer Road were all closed. Challis Creek was evacuated on July 22nd and was evacuated at times through the end of the month by the Custer County sheriff. Power lines would occasionally be shut off in the Challis Creek area due to safety reasons for the public and firefighters. Lodge pole pine and Douglas Fir were the main fuels. 787 personnel were deployed to the incident to fight the fire. The fire continued into August until contained on August 24th.   The fire grew to 22,856 acres but significant growth did not occur in August.
Over one inch of rain fell in less than an hour with 1.31 inches total.   Houses on the southwest side of town had basement flooding with flooding in the downtown construction area.

events.cz_name: BIG AND LITTLE WOOD RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: The Beaver Creek wildfire began with a lightning strike on August 9th northwest of Hailey.   Some evacuations of Deer Creek west of the Big Wood River were ordered on the 15th.   The East Fork of the Wood River between Ketchum and Sun Valley was evacuated on the 16th.  Up to 2,500 people were displaced.  Highway 75 was intermittently closed.   Rapid growth occurred from August 15th through August 21st as it grew from 44 thousand acres to 108 thousand acres helped by gusty winds and low humidity.  As many as 1,721 personnel were assigned to fight the fire.  All told the fire grew to 111,408 acres by August 26th.  One home, a bunkhouse, and six other structures were destroyed.   12 million dollars were spent on fighting the fire.   The fire was considered contained on August 31st.
Trees were reported downed just west of Lava Hot Springs due to thunderstorm outflow winds.
The Mabey wildfire near Bancroft was started by lightning on August 5th and grew to 1,250 acres before being contained.
Lightning started a fire on August 8th south of Malad near the Utah border and covered both states.   The fire eventually grew to 300,000 acres.   The fire was over wilderness areas in Idaho.
Lightning caused a wildfire 3 miles northwest of Lava Hot Springs on August 9th.   It grew to 100 acres before containment.
Strong thunderstorm outflow winds on August 12th downed 3 trees at a Blackfoot home.  It did damage to the roof and some storage sheds.

Radar indicated about 2 to 3 inches of rainfall in southern Cassia County near Utah border.   Birch Creek and Goose Creek roads flooded in the Oakley area and Lynn Road in Almo flooded and washed out.   The roads were strewn with debris, branches and trees.

One to two inches of rain was reported by spotters in Chubbuck and east areas of Pocatello.   Doppler radar indicated 4 to 5 inches over a localized area of Old Town and west Pocatello.   Several homes and businesses were flooded with some evacuations ordered.  Roads closed in the city were Hiline Road to Griffith Road; Hiline Road to El Rancho Boulevard; the Center Street underpass; Pocatello Avenue; Oak Street westbound to Yellowstone Avenue; the intersection of Pole Line Road and Fir Street; the North Main extension at Praxair; and Garrett Way at the railroad tracks.   Hawthorne Road near Interstate 86 was closed in Chubbuck.   Raymond Park in Pocatello was under water.   2 to 3 feet of standing water near Costco and a roof caved in business near Center Street underpass.   A mudslide was reported at West Custer Street and Highland Boulevard in Pocatello.

Flash flooding occurred in the south foothills of Oakley.   Heavy rain over a burn area caused water, debris and mud to flood one basement and several outlying buildings and potato cellars near the Mountain Meadows Ranch.   The flow over burn areas brought ash into the debris and a foot of water and silt entered many ranch buildings and one basement.

One basement flooded in the Bannock Creek District of the Fort Hall Indian Reservation near Rooster Rock.   Cars were washed down a road for a half mile.   Water carried debris out of the mountains into the valley and took out fences along side of road from Rooster Rock to the road going to Bannock Peak.   The main impacted area was from Rattlesnake to the Bannock Creek Community Center.

Heavy rains over the Beaver Creek Fire area caused mudslides in the Hailey area with four mudslides across Croy Creek Road and another which damaged the Animal Shelter of the Wood River Valley.   The slides were as deep as a foot and a half on the north side of Croy Creek Road about a half mile west of the bridge over the Big Wood River in Hailey.   10 of the kennels of the animal shelter and 8 inches of mud in them.   The mudslides began very late in the evening on September 2nd and were cleared by 7:30 AM on the 3rd.
A 63 mph wind gust was measured at Blue Dome.

A heavy rain shower caused flash flooding south of Pocatello including mudslides across roads.   Mudslides occurred on Mink Creek Road from Frazier Egg Farm to Bannock Highway closing the road for an hour.   Some homes on Autumn Drive and Charlotte Drive had basements flooded near the Charlotte Fire burn area.

Rainfall amounts up to 1 inch in one hour caused debris flow in the Timber Gulch area and in the Greenhorn area near Hailey.   The rains over the Beaver Creek fire burn scar contributed to the flooding.
The Kettle Butte ARL site reported a 61 mph wind gust.
One inch hail observed in Island Park.
One and three-quarter inch hail observed north of Macks Inn.
A COOP observer witnessed a tornado with debris being lifted about 5 miles east-southeast of Dubois.   Tornado was in open area with no damage occurring and path unknown.
A tornado was witnessed by the public in open land in Fremont County approximately 10 miles north-northwest of St Anthony.   No damage was reported with the open land storm.
Strong winds with gusts in the 55 to 60 mph range downed a tree onto a house in the city of Rexburg.   Up to 74 mph winds were measured at Rover northwest of Idaho Falls.
Power lines were downed near Parker.   Gusts of 55 to 60 mph measured at Sugar City.

Lightning struck a tree that was connected to a barbed wire fence on a ranch in Tetonia.  The current from the fence killed 15 cattle lined up next to the fence.   Cost to the rancher was between 15 and 20 thousand dollars.
Heavy snowfall occurred as a strong Pacific storm system moved through Idaho on November 16th.   13 inches of snow fell at the Island Park SNOTEL and 21 inches was recorded at White Elephant SNOTEL.
Heavy snow fell in the South Central Highlands with 14 inches measured at the Howell Canyon SNOTEL and 10 inches at the Oxford Springs SNOTEL.
Nine inches of snow was recorded at the Sedgwick Peak SNOTEL site.
Heavy snow amounts in the Idaho Wasatch were Emigrant Summit with 11 inches and Slug Creek with 9 inches.

events.cz_name: BIG AND LITTLE WOOD RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: The Vienna Mine SNOTEL site measured 9 inches of snow.
Heavy snow totals at SNOTEL sites were the following:  12 inches at Stickney Mill, 16 inches at Smiley Mountain16 inches at Mill Creek Summit, and 12 inches at Bear Canyon.
Sixteen inches of snow fell at both the Island Park and Crab Creek SNOTEL sites.

A multiple vehicle accident at around 11 am on the 7th 5 miles south of Idaho Falls closed southbound interstate 15 for several hours.   Snow amounts in the Upper Snake River Plain with the storm ranged from 2 to 4 inches.

The National Weather Service Office at the Pocatello Regional Airport recorded 6.1 inches of snow on the 7th and 8th.    National Weather Service personnel reported 5 inches of snowfall in the cities of Chubbuck and Pocatello.
One foot of snow was recorded at Oxford Springs, Bostetter Ranger Station, and Howell Canyon.

Twelve inches of snow fell at Somsen Ranch and Sedgwick Peak with 16 inches at Wildhorse Divide.   A multiple vehicle accident occurred on interstate 15 near Inkom.  The right lane of interstate 15 southbound near Inkom was closed for 3 hours shortly after 11 am on the 7th.
Sixteen inches of snow fell at Slug Creek Divide with 8 inches at Emigrant Summit.

events.cz_name: BIG AND LITTLE WOOD RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: Sixteen inches of snow fell at Lost Wood Divide, Dollarhide Summit, and Galena.   25 inches of snow fell at Galena Summit with 18 inches at Garfield Ranger Station .
Copper Basin recorded a wind gust of 61 mph on the 2nd and Mill Creek Summit recorded 11 inches of snow.
Several wind gusts of between 40 and 60 mph were recorded on the 2nd with White Elephant getting 9 inches of snow.

Wind gusts of 60 to 70 mph caused a dust storm and the closure of interstate 15 on December 2nd from Idaho Falls to Roberts covering a 16 mile stretch from milepost 119 to 135.   The road was closed at 9:17 am and remained closed until the morning of the 3rd.

events.cz_name: BIG AND LITTLE WOOD RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: Heavy snow fell at high elevation SNOTEL sites with the following amounts recorded:  9 inches at Hyndman, 10 inches at Lost Wood Divide, and 28 inches at Vienna Mine.
Forty to 60 mph wind gusts were recorded on the 2nd with the Meadow Lake SNOTEL recording 12 inches of snow.
On December 6th Fremont County School District 215 and Teton-Driggs School District 401 closed schools due to wind chill readings of 25 to 35 below zero.
Teton County School District 401 and Fremont County District 215 were closed due to wind chill readings in the 25 to 40 below zero range on the 9th.
Wind chill readings in the 25 to 40 below zero range caused the closures of Jefferson School District 251, Idaho Falls School District 91, and several private schools in the Idaho Falls area.

Wind Chill readings of 25 to 40 below zero caused the closure of the following schools:  Aberdeen School District 58, American Falls District 381, Blackfoot District 55, Snake River District 52, and Shoshone-Bannock Jr/Sr High School.
Wind chill readings of 25 to 40 below zero caused the closing of Oneida County School District 351.
Wind chill readings of 25 to 45 below zero caused the following schools to be closed on the 9th:  Grace School District 148, North Gem School District 149, and Soda Springs School District 150.

A fast moving system brought heavy snow to the Upper Snake River Highlands.  10 inches fell in Ashton with 6 inches in Chester and 5 inches in St Anthony.   11 inches fell at the Crab Creek SNOTEL with 10 inches at the White Elephant SNOTEL.
A snowmobiler died near Palisades Peak in Neely's Cove in Bonneville County due to an avalanche.

Fourteen inches of snow fell at the black Bar SNOTEL.   Other SNOTEL amounts were 13 inches at Phillips Bench and 8 inches at White Elephant.   7 inches were reported by spotters in Driggs and Ashton.   Idaho route 32 was closed between Idaho 33 and Idaho 47 from Tetonia to Ashton due to heavy snow and drifting snow at 2 pm MST on the 9th.
The Howell Canyon SNOTEL recorded 18 inches of snow and the Magic Mountain SNOTEL recorded 10 inches.
Ten inches of snow fell at Sheep Mountain with 9 inches at Pine Creek Pass.
Nine inches of snow fell at the Emigrant Summit and Slug Creek Divide SNOTEL sites.
Fifteen inches of snow fell at teh Mill Creek Summit SNOTEL with 9 inches at Smiley Mountain.
Thirteen inches of snow fell at the Black Bear SNOTEL with 9 inches at Phillips Bench and 12 inches at White Elephant.

events.cz_name: BIG AND LITTLE WOOD RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: Nine inches of snow fell at the Galena SNOTEL with 8 inches at Hyndman.   The heaviest amounts were at the Lost Wood Divide SNOTEL with 12 inches and the Vienna Mine SNOTEL with 18 inches.
Ten inches of snow fell at the Somsen Ranch SNOTEL with 12 inches at Pine Creek Pass.
Nine inches of snow fell at the Slug Creek Divide SNOTEL with 11 inches at Emigrant Summit.

The White Elephant SNOTEL recorded 11 inches of snow with 12 inches at Black Bear, 10 inches at Crab Creek, and 10 inches at Island Park.   Ashton reported 6 inches of snow and snow, blowing snow and reduced visibilities caused the closing it interstate 15 from Dubois to the Montana state line.

Although snow amounts were only in the 1 to 3 inch range roadways became very difficult after sunset with several accidents in the Idaho Falls area.   One crash on interstate 15 north of the Dad's truck stop in Idaho falls caused a fatality.
The Snake River and Blackfoot School Districts closed due to wind chill readings colder than 20 degrees below zero the morning of February 6th.

The Idaho Falls School District, Shelley School District, Firth School District, Bonneville School District, Ririe School District, Sugar-Salem School District, and Madison School District all closed on February 6th due to wind chill readings of 20 to 35 below zero.
The Fremont County School District 215 and Clark County School District 61 were closed on February 6th due to extreme cold wind chill readings of 20 to 35 below zero.
Butte county School District 111 was closed on February 6th due to wind chill readings of 20 to 35 degrees below zero.

Heavy snow fell in the Eastern Magic Valley during the morning of the 7th with reports from spotters by early afternoon of:  9 inches in Rupert, 8 inches in Burley, 7 inches in Paul, and 7 inches in Heyburn.

A winter storm brought 3 to 6 inches of snow to the region with several minor traffic accidents and slide offs.   The Pocatello airport received 5 inches of snow before warm temperatures moved in with up to 6 inches on the Pocatello benches.
Snow amounts recorded by SNOTEL sites were:  14 inches at Bear Canyon, 18 inches at Stickney Mill, 14 inches at Smiley Mountain and 27 inches at Mill Creek Summit.
Area SNOTEL reports were:  26 inches at Black Bear, 11 inches at Crab Creek, 12 inches at Island Park, 14 inches at White Elephant, and 42 inches at Phillips Bench.

events.cz_name: BIG AND LITTLE WOOD RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: Area SNOTEL reports were:  26 inches at Dollarhide, 24 inches at Chocolate Gulch, 35 inches at Galena, 34 inches at Galena Summit, 12 inches at Garfield Ranger Station, 33 inches at Lost Wood Divide, 17 inches at Hyndman, 16 inches at Swede Peak, and 48 inches at Vienna Mine.
Area SNOTEL amounts were:  22 inches at Bostetter Ranger Station, 31 inches at Howell Canyon, 24 inches at Oxford Springs, and 20 inches at Magic Mountain.

Area SNOTEL amounts were:  17 inches at Pine Creek Pass, 29 inches at Sedgwick Peak, 15 inches at Sheep Mountain, 17 inches at Somsen Ranch, and 16 inches at Wild Horse Divide.   Lava Hot Springs spotters reported 10 inches before melting.
Observers in Bern reported 18 inches with 21 inches in Montpelier.   SNOTEL reports were:  39 inches at Emigrant Summit, 24 inches at Giveout, and 28 inches at Slug Creek Divide.
Area SNOTEL amounts were:  9 inches at Hilts Creek, 24 inches at Meadow Lake, 15 inches at Moonshine, and 17 inches at Morgan Creek.

events.event_narrative: An avalanche occurred in Blaine County in the Smiley Creek area between Ketchum and Stanley. Four snowmobliers were buried in a meadow area when the avalanche occurred around 2 pm MST. Three of the snowmobliers survived with one fatality occurring.

events.cz_name: BIG AND LITTLE WOOD RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: Area SNOTEL snowfall amounts were:  10 inches at Vienna Mine, 11 inches at Lost Wood Divide, 9 inches at Galena Summit, and 11 inches at Galena.

Blizzard conditions were reported on the morning of the 1st with northerly wind gusts of 35 to 60 mph reported.   US Highway 20 was closed due to low visibility in heavy snow and blowing snow from Ashton through Island Park to the Montana border.   Some motorists on the road were stranded for 18 hours and were delivered food and water on emergency snowmobiles.   4 inches fell in Victor from midnight through 7 am on the 1st.   Total amounts from the 27th through the early morning hours on the 2nd at SNOTEL sites were:  19 inches at Phillips Bench and 13 inches at White Elephant.
Two to 4 inches of snow with strong winds caused numerous accidents and road closures on US Highway 20 from Idaho Falls to Rexburg.   Road was blocked in several areas due to the accidents.

Heavy snow amounts fell in the South Central Highlands from late on February 27th through early morning on March 2nd.   Heavy SNOTEL amounts were:   Bostetter Ranger Station  12 inches, Howell Canyon, 13 inches, Magic Mountain 11 inches, and Oxford Springs 14 inches.

An extended period of heavy snow fell in the Caribou Highlands from late in the day on the 27th of February through the morning of the 2nd of March.   Total SNOTEL amounts were:  Pine Creek Pass 21 inches, Sedgwick Peak 20 inches, Sheep Mountain 9 inches, and Wildhorse Divide 10 inches.
Multiple day snow totals from SNOTEL sites included Emigrant Summit with 21 inches and Slug Creek Divide with 14 inches.
Thirteen inches of snow fell at both the Black Bear and White Elephant SNOTEL sites above 7,500 feet.
Heavy snow fell in high elevations of the Upper Snake River Highlands.   SNOTEL amounts were 9 inches at White Elephant and 13 inches at Phillips Bench.

A powerful cold front moved through eastern Idaho and caused sustained winds of 40 to 45 mph with gusts as high as 64 mph.   A large tree was felled into a cable line in Pocatello on West Sherman Street.   2,800 Idaho Power customers were without power in Chubbuck and Pocatello for a period of time around noon.

Sustained winds of 40 to 50 mph with gusts of 60 to 80 mph occurred in the Upper Snake River Plain.  Blowing dust from the high winds caused visibility to be reduced to zero and interstate 15 closed from Idaho Falls to Roberts.

Sustained winds of 40 to 50 mph with gusts from 55 to 75 mph occurred throughout the Eastern Magic Valley.   The winds caused a semi-truck to flip around 1:30 PM on Highway 25 near milepost 55 near Paul.   There were some power outages in Paul, Rupert, and Richfield.   There was also reported some minor roof and shingle damage in Rupert and Declo.
A strong cold front brought significant winds to the South Central Highlands.   Gusts of 55 to 80 mph were frequent through the day.   There were power outages in Oakley due to the high winds.

A strong cold front moved through eastern Idaho and brought extremely strong winds to the Caribou Highlands.   The winds caused a semitrailer to overturn on interstate 15 just south of Arimo at around 11 AM MDT.   Widespread wind gusts of 50 to 60 mph occurred through the morning and early afternoon in the region.

Heavy wet snow fell through the morning hours on the 30th.   Power outages were reported due to the heavy snow at Rigby and Rexburg.   Measured snow amounts were 8 inches in Rigby, 8 inches in Ririe, and 7 inches in Idaho Falls.

Heavy wet snow fell through the morning on the 30th behind a cold front.   Blackfoot reported 6 inches of snow with 5.3 inches at the Pocatello National Weather Service Office and 5 inches in Chubbuck.
Ten inches of snow fell at the Pebble Creek Ski Resort.   6 inches of snow fell in Grace.  5 inches fell at the Pine Creek Pass SNOTEL with 6 inches at the Wild Horse Divide SNOTEL.
Strong winds caused blowing dust across interstate 15 and it was closed from Idaho Falls to Roberts during the afternoon of April 9th.
Strong winds caused blowing dust to close interstate 15 from Idaho Falls to Roberts from 1:30 through 6 pm.
Damaged and downed power poles reported throughout St Anthony.
Multiple downed and damaged power lines were reported from thunderstorm winds 1 mile south of Ashton.
A trailer house on the Bonneville/Jefferson County line in between  Rigby and Iona lost it's roof due to thunderstorm winds and 6 to 8 inch tree limbs were downed.

Non thunderstorm high winds knocked down 10 to 15 power poles in between Rexburg and Rigby on the US Route 20 corridor.  Interstate 15 in between Idaho Falls and Roberts also shut down due to blowing dust temporarily also during the afternoon on the 22nd.  3,000 area families lost power on the afternoon due to the power pole issue.
A brief tornado touched down 6 miles northwest of Monteview.  Tornado occurred over open land with no damage reported.
A strong thunderstorm caused a gas station  to be blown over in the city of Declo.

A tornado was spotted about 10 miles west-northwest of American Falls around 640 PM MDT and it moved slightly north-northwest until around 7 pm MDT.  It was located 1.2 mile north-northwest of the intersection of North Pleasant Valley Road and County Line Road at 641 pm MDT.   A damage survey showed damage to a residence on North Pleasant Valley Road between Schritter and County Line Roads.   Multiple trees were uprooted or had branches torn off.   Shingles were torn off the hours and a shed door was damaged and blown off its hinges.   There were also isolated reports of irrigation line damage as the tornado moved through mostly open fields.  No other damage was found.
One inch hail fell in Victor verified by a National Weather Service employee in the area.
Tetonia received 1.75 inch hail from a severe thunderstorm.
A severe thunderstorm wind at around 3:45 pm MDT on the west side of Idaho Falls near the intersection of Olympia St. and Washburn Ave. caused a large tree branch to be snapped off of a tree.
The Pocatello Regional Airport ASOS measured a wind gust of 69 mph.
Aberdeen Weather station recorded 69 mph wind gust.

A 796 acre wildfire caused by lightning burned for several days about 10 miles east of Firth.   No structural damage was caused by the wildfire in open terrain.   The fire began the evening of June 12th due to thunderstorms and was contained by June 18th.
A 115 acre wildfire which was ignited by thunderstorms on June 12th burned 115 acres 16 miles east of Blackfoot.   The fire was contained by June 16th.   No structural damage occurred.

events.cz_name: BIG AND LITTLE WOOD RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: The Dietrich wildfire began on the 13th and burned near the town of Dietrich covering 145 acres.    One power pole had to be replaced and 432 customers lost electricity from the fire on the 13th of June.    Other than power poles, no other structures were damaged.
Lightning on June 12th started the Burns Wildfire near Palisades Reservoir.  The fire was located 3 miles southwest of Hoffman Campground.  The fire burned 45 acres and was contained by June 18th.
Heavy rains flooded several streets in Pocatello including Alameda.
Four to 6 inch diameter  branches blown off trees 6 miles south southeast of Grace.

A thunderstorm dropped anywhere from 1 to 3 inches in the city of Rexburg.  A single thunderstorm cell moved over the city and heavy rain began at around 5:30 pm MDT.  Main Street was shut down with over a foot of running water on it.  Businesses on Main Street suffered damage.   15 businesses on the south side of Main Street and south 2nd West received minor flood damage consisting of a few inches of water entering their businesses.   ||The Hidden Valley neighborhood in northeast Rexburg had approximately 20 homes from a few inches in a basement up to a basement full in 2 of them.   The Mill Hollow  subdivision had 20 homes reported having water damage.  A few homes had 1 to 3 feet of water in their basements.  ||The BYU Idaho campus was hit hard by the flooding.    Three-quarters of the buildings on campus had water in them.   Apartments on campus had up to 6 feet of standing water in them.   Birch Plaza and Birchwood Apartments were the worst hit on campus.  Water was high enough that furniture was floating in the buildings.   ||Total damages of the flooding were estimated at $600,000.

A fire started around 6 pm west of Chubbuck on the Fort Hall Indian Reservation.   Several people were evacuated from homes on North Laughran Road between West Tyhee and West Siphon.   35 homes were threatened but the fire was contained by 10 pm with no damage occurring.
Lightning caused a fire start about 7 miles southeast of Arimo on July 16th and reached nearly 400 acres.  The fire was 100 percent contained by the evening of July 17th.
Lightning on July 22nd caused the 200 acre Flat Iron fire in the Arbon Valley.   The fire was contained by July 23rd.
Flooding of farmland occurred east of Rigby with standing water reported in pastures throughout the region.   1 to 2 inches of rain fell in less than an hour over the flooded areas.
One to 2 inches of rain in less than an hour flooded some farmland in the Taber area.
Idaho State Police reported accumulating water on interstate 86 near mile post 30.  Resources had to be called to remove water from the interstate.

One to two inches of rain in less than an hour caused extensive street flooding in Chubbuck and Pocatello.    Several inches reported at intersection of Yellowstone and Flandro roads in Pocatello.   Standing water was reported at the intersection of Yellowstone Road and Cedar.   The Chubbuck WalMart reported flooding inside the building with damage to merchandise.  Basement flooding was reported at the intersection of Hawthorne and Homestead Roads.   High Estates Trailer Park on Philbin Road in Pocatello was flooded with several inches of water.   Hawthorne Road at the interstate 86 underpass in Chubbuck was closed due to extensive standing water.   Garrett Way in Pocatello near Alameda was closed.
Heavy rains caused 2 to 3 meet of mud to ooze out of Castle Creek into Warm Springs west of the city of Ketchum.   This occurred between 2:30 and 3:30 pm MDT.

Nearly 2 inches of rain in less than an hour brought extensive flooding to the city of Blackfoot.   Extensive street and parking lot flooding occurred with standing water on roadways a problem throughout the city.   Several cars stalled out driving through water with one truck driving into an uncovered manhole   Several manhole covers in roads became uncovered as the amount of water was too much for the cities drainage system.   30 homes and 15 businesses reported damage with house basements receiving the most damage.   Several roads were also damaged.   Damage in Blackfoot was estimated at $300,000.
Flash flooding reported in American Falls with standing water on roadways and a basement flooded at one residence.
Flooding of farmland about 6 miles west northwest of Arimo was reported by spotters.   Road closures occurred between the towns of Arimo and Robin due to 12 inches of standing water on roadways.

Close to one inch of rainfall caused street flooding in Pocatello.   Water was 8 inches deep on some roads.   A manhole cover was dislodged on Jerome Street.   Flooding was reported with several inches of water on the corner of 13th Street and Hayden.
Flooding occurred in the basement of an apartment building in Inkom.
Multiple photographs of funnel cloud with a brief touch down 2 miles southeast of Mackay.
One inch hail photographed and placed on social media occurred in the city of Roberts.
One inch hail reported 4 miles west northwest of the town of Lorenzo.

COOP Observer reported 1 to 2 inches of water flowing across Highway 93 in the city of Arco.  Minor residential flooding occurred with some flooding at the hospital.  A city bridge on Era street washed out and the street was closed and minor flooding occurred on Highway 33.
Hail one inch in diameter fell in the city of Ketchum.   The hail accumulated up to a depth of 2 inches on sidewalks in spots.
Golf ball sized hail reported in Richfield.
Federal employee spotted a funnel cloud 5 miles south of the city of Bellevue.
The Lincoln County sheriff reported a funnel cloud near Kinzie Butte.
The Lincoln County sheriff reported a funnel cloud at mile marker 42 on Highway 24.
Near the Lincoln and Blaine County border the sheriff reported thunderstorm wind gusts blew a car off the road.
One inch hail reported in the city of Richfield.
The public reported an unconfirmed tornado west of Soda Springs and later a funnel cloud near the city.
One inch hail reported in Spencer.
A lightning strike to a power pole in between Hailey and Ketchum shut down power and also business in Ketchum from 5:35 pm MDT to 8 pm MDT on August 12th.

The Blackfoot schools closed on November 12th due to wind chill values of -20 to -25 degrees during the morning.

Twenty to 30 below zero wind chill readings occurred in the Upper Snake River Plain on the morning of November 12th.
The Mill Creek Summit SNOTEL site recorded 13 inches of snow .  Bear Canyon had 5 inches and Stickney Mill had 7 inches.

A spotter reported nine inches of snowfall at Driggs with the following SNOTEL amounts:  Island Park 9 inches, Phillips Bench 25 inches, White elephant 8 inches, Crab Creek 8 inches, Black Bear 19 inches.

Four to 6 inches of snow fell in the Upper Snake River Plain during the two days.   Over 50 accidents were reported in Bonneville County by the Sheriffs dispatch with them bulk of them in Idaho Falls.

Four to 6 inches of snow fell in the Lower Snake River Plain on the 13th and 14th with the main issue several traffic accidents with extensive damage occurring.   Many of the accidents occurred on interstates.  Around noon a major accident occurred on interstate 15 south of Blackfoot with another near 1 pm in south Pocatello trapping a motorist.   At 245 pm another accident on interstate 15 south of Pocatello again.   Two different rollovers occurred on interstate 86 in Power county.  One was near Rainbow Road and the other near the Pocatello Regional Airport.  Bingham County Sheriff reported several accidents on interstate 15 between Blackfoot and fort Hall with five injuries.

Extremely heavy snow fell in the South Central Highlands on the 13th and 14th.   Two day amounts at SNOTEL sites were the following:  Bostetter Ranger Station 11 inches, Howell Canyon 22 inches, Magic Mountain 12 inches, Oxford Springs 9 inches.

Heavy snowfall created dangerous road conditions and several accidents on interstate 15 near Inkom.   A three vehicle crash occurred at noon and rollovers reported at 1 pm and 250 pm again near Inkom.   Two more rollovers near Inkom were reported at 4 pm and 430 pm.  SNOTL snow amounts were the following:  Pine Creek Pass 19 inches, Sedgwick Peak 10 inches, Somsen Ranch 11 inches, Sheep Mountain 14 inches, Wildhorse Divide 12 inches.
Heavy snow fell on the 13th and 14th in the Idaho Wasatch with the following SNOTEL amounts:  Emigrant Summit 22 inches, Giveout 10 inches, Slug Creek Divide 12 inches.

Meado Lake reported 14 inches of snow and Morgan Creek reported 11 inches of snow.

The Sedgwick Peak SNOTEL recorded 11 inches of snow and the Wildhorse Divide SNOTEL recorded 9 inches.

The Slug Creek Divide SNOTEL reported 12 inches of snow.

Strong winds caused blowing dust and zero visibility on interstate 15 north of Idaho Falls near Roberts.   A nine vehicle crash occurred at around 240 pm south of Roberts.  The dust storm and near zero visibility occurred from around noon through 830 pm.   Interstate 15 closed for 7 hours after the crash between mile posts 119 and 135 in both directions.  Ten people were transported to the Eastern Idaho Regional Medical Center for treatment.

A 23 year old Washington man was killed in a one vehicle rollover on interstate 86 near milepost 56 and the Pocatello Regional Airport in Power County on December 17th at around 6:30 am.  Some ice was reported to have formed in the dense freezing fog on the interstate along with very low visibility.
Ten inches of snow fell at the Mill Creek Summit SNOTEL site.   6 inches fell at Smiley Mountain.
Twenty inches of snow fell at the Black Bear SNOTEL site.   Additional reports were 11 inches at Phillips bench and 18 inches at White Elephant.
The following SNOTEL snow amounts were recorded:  Bostetter Ranger Station 14 inches, Howell Canyon 19 inches, Magic Mountain 11 inches, Oxford Springs 15 inches.
Pine Creek Pass received 10 inches of snow and Sedgwick Peak received 12 inches.
Emigrant Summit received 17 inches of snow and Slug Creek Divide received 14 inches.

events.cz_name: BIG AND LITTLE WOOD RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: High elevation SNOTEL snow amounts were:  17 inches at Dollarhide Summit, 18 inches at Galena, 17 inches at Galena Summit, 10 inches at Hyndman, 13 inches at Lost Wood Divide, 10 inches at Swede Peak, and 28 inches at Vienna  Mine.   A trained spotter reported 9 inches at Hailey.
The following high elevation SNOTEL snow amounts were received:  8 inches at Hilts Creek, 14 inches at Meadow Lake, and 10 inches at Moonshine.

Four to 8 inches of snow fell in the Eastern Magic Valley with road conditions becoming dangerous with several accidents reported on interstates 84 and 86.  The westbound lanes of interstate 84 were closed between Burley and Twin Falls due to an accident involving a semi between 330 am and 530 am on Christmas Day.   White out conditions were reported on interstate 84.
The following snowfall amounts were reported by SNOTEL sites:  Bear Canyon 8 inches, Mill Creek Summit 7 inches, and Smiley Mountain 18 inches.

Heavy snow and strong winds made travel difficult Christmas day in the Upper Snake River Highlands.   Spotters reported 10 inches of snow in Island Park and 9 inches in St Anthony with extensive blowing and drifting snow.    High elevation SNOTEL amounts were the following:  20 inches Black Bear, 9 inches Island Park, 15 inches Phillips Bench, and 16 inches White Elephant.
Trained spotters reported 6 inches of snow in Idaho Falls and 7 inches in Rigby.

A powerful winter storm dropped 6 to 8 inches of snow in the cities of Chubbuck and Pocatello with 8 to 10 inches on the Pocatello east and west benches.   A fatal traffic accident occurred on interstate 15 in south Pocatello in which a mother and her daughter died with injuries to 5 other children in the vehicle.   The accident occurred around 11 am and closed interstate 15 in both directions for nearly two hours.  Another accident on interstate 15 in Pocatello occurred around 5 pm with three injuries.
Sixteen inches of snow fell at Bostetter Ranger Station with 18 inches at Howell Canyon.
The following SNOTEL snow amounts were recorded:  9 inches Pine Creek Pass, 10 inches Sedgwick Peak, 10 inches Sheep Mountain, and 13 inches at Wildhorse Divide.
Eleven inches of snow fell at Emigrant Summit with 8 inches at Slug Creek Divide.

events.cz_name: BIG AND LITTLE WOOD RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: Snow reports from spotters included 8 inches in Hailey, 10 inches in Bellevue, and 12 inches in Ketchum.   SNOTEL snowfall was the following:  9 inches at Chocolate Gulch, 11 inches at Garfield Ranger Station, 12 inches at Galena, 18 inches at Galena Summit, 9 inches at Hyndman, 9 inches at Swede Peak, 11 inches at Lost Wood Divide,  and 11 inches at Vienna Mine.
SNOTEL snowfall reports were the following:  11 inches Meadow Lake, 12 inches Moonshine, and 9 inches Morgan Creek.
A spotter reported 10 inches of snow in St Anthony.   SNOTEL reports were 14 inches at Black Bear, 10 inches at Crab Creek, 10 inches at Island Park, and 11 inches at White Elephant.
Snowfall reports in the Upper Snake River Plain werer 4 inches in Idaho Falls, 6 inches in Ammon, and 7 inches in Rexburg.
Heavy snowfall occurred in the Caribou Highlands with 9 inches at Pine Creek Pass, 8 inches at Sheep Mountain and 10 inches in McCammon.

SNOTEL snow reports were the following:  Island Park 15 inches, Phillips Bench 17 inches, and White Elephant 16 inches.   Idaho route 32 was closed in both directions due to drifting snow and low visibility from mile post 0 to mile post 28 between Ashton and Tetonia on the morning of January 5th.

SNOTEL snow amounts were 20 inches at Pine Creek Pass, 9 inches at Somsen Ranch, and 8 inches at Sheep Mountain.   A vehicle rollover occurred in Inkom on East Green Canyon Road due to icy conditions closing the road for two hours.   No serious injuries occurred.
One foot of snow fell at the Slug Creek Divide SNOTEL.

events.cz_name: BIG AND LITTLE WOOD RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: SNOTEL amounts were the following:  7 inches at Dollarhide, 6 inches at Galena Summit, and 15 inches at Vienna Mine.
Ten inches of snow fell at the Morgan Creek and Meadow Lake SNOTEL sites with 9 inches at Moonshine.
Eleven single vehicle accidents occurred on interstate 15 between Fort Hall and Blackfoot on January 24th due to freezing fog and drizzle causing icy roadways to develop.
Emigrant Summit received 16 inches of snowfall.
The Howell Canyon SNOTEL recorded 14 inches of snow.
The Phillips Bench SNOTEL recorded 18 inches of snow.
Pine Creek Pass recorded 7 inches of snow and Sedgwick Peak recorded 10 inches.

Two to 4 inches of snow fell in the Pocatello and American Falls areas with several slide offs and rollovers reported on interstate 86.  Interstate 86 east bound was temporarily closed off near Coldwater Rest area.
Five inches of snow fell in Driggs with 8 inches in Victor.
Three to 5 inches of snow fell with a car tipping over on Highway 89 near the town of Montpelier.
Three to 6 inches of hail accumulated in Roberts.  Several cars slid off roads and an INL bus got stuck in the ice.   Snow plows were called out to plow the roads in the Roberts area.

As much as 1 to 4 inches of small hail accumulated on interstate 15 between Firth and Shelley and several slide offs and accidents were reported by area law enforcement.   No injuries occurred in the accidents.

Bear Lake County experienced a 90 minute power outage due to high winds knocking down power poles and lines.  Rocky Mountain Power customers in Paris, Fish Haven, St. Charles, and Montpelier lost power on the afternoon of the 14th.

Rocky Mountain Power reported winds knocking down a transmission line affecting over 2,400 customers on the afternoon of the 14th.   Many were still without power as late as 9 pm MDT.  Customers without power resided in Preston, Clifton, Swanlake, Dayton, and Weston.

Two to 4 inches of snow in the lower Snake River Plain caused 4 slide offs and 5 accidents on interstate 15 in the Fort Hall, Chubbuck, and Pocatello areas.   One of the crashes south of Fort Hall involved a passenger car sliding into a snow plow.   No injures occurred in the accidents.

Heavy rain caused the closing of the Center Street underpass for several hours.   Sandbags were ordered to alleviate flooding at Hayes Avenue and Halliday Street.  Wyeth Street.  Flooding also occurred at Wyeth Street., Main Street, Custer Street and Lincoln Avenue.  Multiple weather related motor vehicle accidents were reported as well.
Funnel clouds seen near Paul on May 15th.
Several photographs of funnel cloud taken on May 16th in Blackfoot and Moreland.

Funnel cloud photographed just south of Malta.
Funnel cloud photographed near Minidoka.
Funnel cloud photographed in Oakley.
A funnel cloud was photographed just west of the Pocatello aiport.
A funnel cloud was photographed southwest of Declo.
A funnel cloud around noon at Sun Valley was photographed.
Over 2 inches of rain in one hour caused flooding mainly at the Grand Teton Mall where over one foot of water accumulated in the parking lot.
Funnel cloud photographed near Rexburg at around 2 pm MDT.
The Hailey airport reported a rotating cloud base near Bellevue and a county official in Bellevue submitted video of storm.    No witnesses of a tornado touchdown however occurred.
Funnel cloud viewed over Weston and Preston.
Fifty-nine mph wind gust at the Pocatello airport.
Six to 9 inch tree limbs blown off tree with 3 inch tree limb blown across road in Fort Hall.

Large tree downed by thunderstorm winds in Sterling.
Large tree uprooted and downed due to thunderstorm winds near American Falls.   Created 6 to 8 foot deep crater and landed on a home.

Small hail began accumulating on interstate 15 in Fort Hall and many cars slid off the interstate into ditches and the median with one collision occurring.   One individual received minor  injuries and was transported to a hospital.

A 1,750 acre fire began about 3 am on August 20th due to a lightning strike 4 miles southeast of American Falls.  It threatened about 30 homes in the Garden Subdivision and owners evacuated but the fire was controlled and contained without damaging the homes.

Winds from a severe thunderstorm of 70 mph or greater caused large waves and capsized a ski boat with 7 people on board on Bear Lake on the Idaho portion of the lake.   There were 4 fatalities with 3 survivors from the accident.
One inch hail near Leslie, Idaho.
Several reports of large hail were received from Chubbuck with hail size ranging from 1 to 2 inches.
Large hail measuring 1.25 inches was recorded in Tetonia.

One or more large pine trees snapped off near ground in Moreland with power out at 4 pm MDT which affected 1,350 people at one point.   Tree limbs also reported downed along with some siding blown off houses.
One and three-quarter inch hail fell 2 miles southwest of Fort Hall.
Idaho State Journal reported several large tree limbs down as well as power lines and road signs west of American Falls.
A COOP observer recorded a 76 mph wind gust in Bern.   Aspen tree felled by the wind.
Power lines reported downed over houses and roads with 4 to 6 inch trees downed as well near Clifton.
Trained spotter measured ping pong size hail southeast of Almo.

Between 4:30 and 6:30 on 6/1/2015 the Franklin County Sheriff's Office received several reports of power lines down with either broken power poles or trees fallen on lines, or power poles and lines fallen on houses.  Rocky Mountain Power and Utah Power are still working on restoring power, however, many residents are still without power.  Much of the damage was isolated to the West Side of Franklin County.  We had one report of a man electrocuted by a downed line, however, he was treated on scene by EMS and released.  We had many trees blocking roads which have now been removed, and other reports of property damage due to wind including one cargo trailer which was blown over.   We appreciate the help from the Preston Police Department, Franklin County Fire, EMS, Search & Rescue and Road & Bridge, Idaho State Police and Idaho State Fish & Game who all helped cover different calls.
One inch hail reported near the city of Preston.
The Juniper interchange mesonet site measured a 60 mph wind gust.
One inch hail recorded 6 miles south of Ririe.
One and three-quarter inch sized hail reported 4 miles north of Wayan.

On shift Pocatello NWS employee measured 1 inch hail at the Pocatello Regional airport.

Severe wind reports from Downey from channel 8 news in Idaho Fall.  We got a report of high wind knocking over an 80 foot tall tree last night around 7 pm on N Cambridge Road near Downey. It crippled a pickup truck, crushed a tractor and ripped a power box off a man's home.
By the morning of June 10th the Big Wood River was running across Colorado Gulch Road making it impassable. Colorado Gulch Rd. was closed on the East end at the vehicle gate.
Heavy rains from a thunderstorm caused several inches of water to collect on roads and residential areas in the town of Victor.   No damage reports were received.
A large tree was uprooted by thunderstorm winds in Albion.
Ths ASOS at the Burley Municipal airport recorded a 67 mph wind gust from a thunderstorm.
A tractor trailer was reported overturned on interstate 84 south of Rupert when strong thunderstorm winds passed through the region.
Strong thunderstorm winds blew over a wooden fence northeast of Heyburn.
Video and photographs received on social media tornado over in between Mud Lake and Sage Junction in Jefferson County on July 11th.
Pictures of funnel clouds received 1 mile northwest of Plano.

Photographs of funnel clouds east of Chesterfield received between 130 and 155 PM MDT.
Funnel clouds viewed and photographed in Declo.
Lightning started a fire in a grain field in Declo with 30 foot flames.   40 to 50 acres of a 140 acre field were destroyed by the fire.
A 59 mph wind gust was measured at Roberts.
A 64 mph wind gust was recorded at the Taber INL site.

Potato crop damage occurred from rain, hail and wind in Shelley.

A wildfire that grew to 10,451 acres started on August 24th due to a lightning strike.   The fire was located about 17  miles west of Challis.  A type 3 team was deployed and the following closures occurred:  Bayhorse Roiad, Trealor Creek Road, Custer Motor Way, Garden Creek Road, Kinnikinic Creek Road, Mill Creek Campground, Mosquito Flat Campground, and Eight Mile Campground.   The fire continued well into September before complete containment.

The 900 fire began August 14th due to lightning strikes and burned 2,245 acres of grass and brush.  It was located approximately 7 miles south of Shoshone and closed US route 93 to motorists for a lengthy period of time.   Traffic backups were up to a mile on the 14th.   The fire was contained by August 17th.

A fire near Island Park began with a lightning stirke on September 4th and continued through September 17th and grew to 553 acres. Several forest service roads were closed due to the fire but it was in open country and threatened no property and was allowed to burn. Rainfall ended the fire.
Twelve inches of snow fell at the Mill Creek Summit SNOTEL with 14 inches at Smiley Mountain.

events.cz_name: BIG AND LITTLE WOOD RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: Fifteen inches of snow fell at Galena Summit and 17 inches fell at Vienna Mine.
Eight inches of snow was recorded at Hilts Creek with 14 inches at Meadow Lake.
The McCammon mesonet site measured a 62 mph wind gust.    A 75 foot cottonwood was blown over in McCammon with damage to fence and power line and another tree.
Fifty-nine mph wind gust recorded at Idahome with 60 mph at City of Rocks and 61 mph at Moburg Canyon.
Storm amounts were the following:  10 inches in Richfield, 7.5 inches in Heyburn, and 9 inches in Dietrich.

Several automobile accidents were reported on interstate 15 especially in Bingham County.  5 inches of snow fell in Pocatello and Chubbuck and the Pocatello Airport with as much as 7 inches on the Pocatello benches.   15 slideoffs and 15 accidents were reported with many on interstate 15 and major traffic slowdowns on interstate 15 Wednesday evening.
Five inches of snow was reported in Idaho Falls with many traffic problems WEdnesday afternoon and evening in interstate 15 near Shelley.
Eleven inches of snow fell at Wildhorse Divide with 8 inches at Sheep Mountain, 6 inches at Somsen Ranch, and 6 inches at Sedgwick Peak.
Nine inches of snow fell in Oxford Springs with 8 inches at Howell Canyon and Bostetter Ranger Station.
A fatal accident occurred on Highway 20 14 miles north of Ashton due to snow and ice on the roadway. A man driving westbound near milepost 375 slid into oncoming traffic.

events.cz_name: BIG AND LITTLE WOOD RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: Ten inches of snow fell at Mt Baldy with 10 inches at Galena Summit, 12 inches at Lost Wood Divide, and 15 inches at Vienna Mine.
Twenty inches of snow fell at the Black Bear SNOTEL site with 13 inches at White Elephant.

events.cz_name: BIG AND LITTLE WOOD RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: An avalanche occurred at 2:30 am December 8th at 955 Warm Springs Road near Frenchman's Bend west of Ketchum.

events.cz_name: BIG AND LITTLE WOOD RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: Thirteen inches of snow fell at the Chocolate Gulch SNOTEL site and 11 inches fell at Vienna Mine.   8 inches were reported in Ketchum with 6 inches in Hailey.
The Bear Canyon SNOTEL recorded 13 inches of snow with 14 inches at Mill Creek Summit, 24 inches at Smiley Mountain and 9 inches at Stinckney Mill.
Nineteen inches of snow was recorded at the White Elephant SNOTEL site.  Multiple slideoffs were reported on US Highway 20 through the Island Park area.
Heavy snowfall amounts at SNOTEL sites:  Bostetter Ranger Station  23 inches, Howell Canyon 25 inches, and Oxford Springs 13 inches.

Heavy snowfall occurred during the entire day on December 14th mainly in the local Pocatello area.    Snowfall amounts ranged from 6 inches at the Pocatello Regional Airport, to 8 to 10 inches in the cities of Chubbuck and Pocatello with 12 inches on the Pocatello benches.   58 traffic accidents and slideoffs were reported in the Pocatello area with many minor injuries and extensive automobile damages.

A winter storm dumped generally snow amounts in the 3 to 5 inch range from Idaho Falls to Rexburg.   Idaho State Police reported a large number of accidents and slideoffs in the Idaho Falls area as of 5 pm on the 14th.
Fifteen inches of snow fell at Sedgwick Peak and 21 inches fell at Wildhorse Divide.
Eleven inches of snow fell at the Emigrant Summit SNOTEL site.

events.cz_name: BIG AND LITTLE WOOD RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: A strong winter storm brought extremely heavy snow to the Wood River region.   Spotters reported 16 inches of snow in Bellevue, 24 inches of snow 4 miles north of Hailey, and 15 inches in Ketchum through the evening on the 13th.   Some SNOTEL amounts were 18 inches at Chocolate Gulch, 14 inches at Garfield Ranger Station, 19 inches at Lost Wood Divide, 25 inches at Galena Summit, 20 inches at Galena, and 19 inches at Swede Peak.
Seven inches of snow fell in the town of Moore.   SNOTEL reports were 14 inches at Meadow Lake, 16 inches at Moonshine, and 25 inches at Morgan Creek.
A fatality occurred on the evening of December 20th on interstate 15 northbound just north of the Shelley exit during a light snowfall which caused icy road conditions.

events.cz_name: BIG AND LITTLE WOOD RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: Ten inches of snow fell at Chocolate Gulch with 12 inches at Galena and 10 inches at Galena Summit.

Only 4 to 8 inches of snow fell in the region but it was accompanied by very strong winds which closed US Route 30 between Lava Hot Springs and Soda Springs from the evening of the 21st around 11 pm to the morning of the 22nd.  A Salt Lake City Express van flipped on its side on interstate 15 near McCammon around 5 pm on the 21st.   No major injuries occurred due to the crash.

Six to 10 inches of snow fell in the Upper Snake Highlands on the 21st with 10 inches reported on Ashton Hill and 7 inches in Island Park.   Winds were very strong causing limited visiblity and horrible driving conditions.   Several slideoffs occurred in the Island Park including one semi on its side.  Idaho Highway 32 was closed due to the conditions in between Ashton and Tetonia.
Ten inches of snow fell at Bostetter Ranger Station and 9 inches fell at Howell Canyon.
A thunderstorm moved through Pocatello and downed trees and power lines and thousands of people were reported without power in the Pocatello and Chubbuck area through 11 pm on the 21st.
Four to 7 inches of snow combined with wind gusts of 40 to 60 mph closed interstate 84 from Burley to the Idaho/Utah border for the majority of December 23rd.

Four to 8 inches of snow combined with high winds with gusts over 30 mph caused extemely difficult travel conditions with one fatality in an accident on US Highway 20 near milepost 367 on Ashton Hill at 8 am on the 23rd.   This caused the road to be closed for several hours.

Wind gusts of 50 mph combined with 3 to 6 inches of fresh snowfall created hazardous travel with numerous traffic accidents in Bear Lake County including a 7 car pileup.   US HIghway 89 was closed from Ovid to the Utah border.

Strong winds combined with 3 to 7 inches of snow led to extremely hazardous driving conditions in the Caribou Highlands.  A three car head on accident occurred on US Highway 30 in Soda Springs in the morning on the 23rd.   The highway was also closed for several hours in the afternoon from milepost 371 to the Highway 34 junction.
Heavy snow fell in the Upper Snake River Plain with 7 inches in Taber, 5 inches in Rigby, and 4 inches in Idaho Falls.

Snow amounts reported by spotters were 10 inches at Victor and 9 inches in Driggs.  SNOTEL amounts were the following:  25 inches at Black Bear, 13 inches at Island Park, 16 inches at Phillips Bench, and 19 inches at White Elephant.
SNOTEL amounts were 15 inches at Bostetter Ranger Station, 21 inches at Howell Canyon, 10 inches at Magic Mountain, and 9 inches at Oxford Springs.

Spotters reported 12 inches of snow in Inkom.   SNOTEL amounts were the following:  13 inches at Pine Creek Pass, 11 inches at Sedgwick Peak, 10 inches at Sheep Mountain,   and 18 inches at Wildhorse Divide.
Eight inches of snow fell in Franklin.   SNOTEL amounts were 17 inches at Emigrant Summit.

events.cz_name: BIG AND LITTLE WOOD RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: Heavy snow amounts at SNOTEL sites were 11 inches at Dollarhide Summit, 12 inches at Galena, 14 inches at Galena Summit, and 10 inches at Lost Wood Divide.
Heavy SNOTEL amounts were 10 inches at Meadow Lake and 10 inches at Moonshine.
Twelve inches of snow fell at Sedgwick Pean and 11 inches fell at Sheep Mountain . Other amounts were 6 inches at Pine Creek Pass and 5 inches at Somsen Ranch.
Heavy SNOTEL snow amounts were:  Bear Canyon 13 inches, Mill Creek Summit 9 inches, and Smiley Mountain 17 inches.

events.cz_name: BIG AND LITTLE WOOD RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: Heavy SNOTEL amounts were:  9 inches at Dollarhide, 11 inches at Galena Summit, 9 inches at Hyndman, and 10 inches at Swede Peak.

events.cz_name: BIG AND LITTLE WOOD RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: An avalanche blocked a portion of Highway 75 north of Ketchum at 1 pm.  ||By 2:50 p.m. the page indicated that it had been cleared. The avalanche occurred between North Bigwood Drive and West Sage Road.

One to 3 inches of snowfall caused problems with morning rush hour traffic.  Around 8 am a semi truck rear-ended an Idaho Department of Transportation snow plow near mile post 108 on interstate 15 south of Idaho Falls.   Extensive damage occurred to snow plow equipment as well as the front end of the semi.  Several slide offs were reported on Highway 20 between Idaho Falls and Rexburg.
Heavy SNOTEL snow amounts for the storm were:  Bear Canyon 18 inches, Mill Creek Summit 16 inches, and Smiley Mountain 21 inches.
The Phillips Bench SNOTEL received 11 inches of snow and the White Elephant site received 16 inches.
Heavy snow amounts recorded were 10 inches at Bostetter Ranger Station and 17 inches at Howell Canyon.

events.cz_name: BIG AND LITTLE WOOD RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: SNOTEL snow amounts were:  17 inches at Dollarhide Summit, 12 inches at Galena, 16 inches at Galena Summit, 18 inches at Lost Wood Divide, 12 inches at Swede Peak, and 24 inches at Vienna Mine.

A strong upper level low moving through Utah brought extremely heavy and wet snow to the Eastern Magic Valley.   The snow caused extensive tree damage due to its very wet nature.   All schools in Minidoka and Cassia Counties were closed on March 29th.  Amounts recorded were 14 to 16 inches in Declo, 10 to 14 inches in Rupert, 9 to 13 inches in Burley, 10 to 12 inches in Paul and 10 inches in Heyburn.    Several slide offs and traffic accidents were reported including on Interstate 84.

Not much snow fell in the Pocatello area.   Generally 1 to 3 inches of snow fell but it all fell between 7 and 10 am making morning rush hour traffic very difficult.  Many traffic accidents and slide offs occurred in Pocatello and on interstate 15 and early morning travel was extemely hazardous.   Some School District 25 school buses in Pocatello were unable to pick up children due to the road conditions and many students were very late to school due to the timing of the snowfall and road conditions.

An upper level low moving through Utah brought extremely heavy snow to the region.   Spotters reported 12 inches in Malta with drifts over two feet.   13 inches were reported in Albion.   SNOTEL mountain amounts were 14 inches at Bostetter Ranger Station, 29 inches at Howell Canyon, and 13 inches at Magic Mountain.
Spotter measured 16 inches of snow total from storm south of Soda Springs in Bear Lake County just south of Caribou County line.   Emigrant Summit SNOTEL site also recorded 16 inches of snow.

Very heavy snowfall fell in the Caribou Highlands with spotters reporting 10 to 16 inches in Soda Springs, 9 inches near Grace, and 8 inches in Bancroft.   The Sedgwick Peak SNOTEL recorded 16 inches of snowfall.
A cold air funnel cloud was photographed near Idaho Falls late in the morning on March 28th.

Lightning struck a power pole in the northern part of Idaho Falls and left 1,700 Rocky Mountain Power customers without power for just over one hour on April 10th.  A power line was arcing on the ground and caused a brief fire.
Multiple photographs were received of a funnel cloud west of American Falls between 1 pm and 1:30 pm MDT on April 11th.
Photographs were taken of a funnel cloud near Blackfoot on April 29th.
Hail of 1.25 inches reported by Emergency Manager in Ashton.
Facebook pictures revealed 1.50 inch hail hear Poplar.
Facebook photographs revealed 1.75 inch hail in Rexburg.

Strong winds at 40 mph with gusts to 60 mph downed power lines and trees with many without power in Ammon and Rigby.   Multiple large trees were downed in Idaho Falls and Rigby.  Several road and traffic signs were also downed and extensive damage to yard items like trampolines, greenhouses and playgrounds also occurred.

Interstate 15 closed between Idaho Falls and Roberts from mile post 119 to mile post 134 due to blowing dust and visibility one quarter mile or less at 11:50 am and was closed until 6 pm.    Sustained winds of over 40 mph were measured at Osgood.

A post cold frontal wind storm affected the Upper Snake River Highlands on May 9th.    Several power poles in Ashton were downed with many residents losing power for several hours in Ashton, Chester, Marysville, and Newdale.   Blowing dust dropped visibility to 0.3 miles in Marysville.
One inch hail in Rexburg.
One inch diameter hail also accumulated 1 to 2 inches on US Route 20.
Spotter measured a 65 mph wind gust west of Montpelier.
One inch hail in Montpelier with small branches stripped off trees.
One inch hail in Geneva.
A 61 mph wind gust was measured at 4:05 PM 2 miles north of Driggs with 4 power poles downed along 2500 N.  Power was out for 6 hours north of the airport.
A 60 mph wind gust was measured at 4 PM MDT at Aberdeen.
Power outage occurred from a thunderstorm extending from Chester north to Ashton.

An early morning storm moved through Bingham County and downed trees and power lines.   Wind speeds of 56 mph were measured in Blackfoot with 2,100 people without power according to Rocky Mountain Power and Idaho Power.   The storm moved through around 2 am in the morning with most power restored by 11 am.   Several power lines were downed as well as large trees including a 70 foot spruce in Groveland.
Public reported one inch hail 2 miles east southeast of Lund.
The public reported one inch hail in Island Park on June 28th at around 445 pm.
Sixty mile per hour winds moved through Butte County on the 30th with Arco recording 63 mph at 2:55 pm MDT.   Several small limbs were torn off trees in the city.
Lightning on June 29th started a fire west of Island Park in wilderness.   The fire was managed and not put out by the forest service.
A 60 mph wind gust was recorded by the ASOS at the Pocatello Regional Airport.
A 74 mph wind gust was recorded at the Kettle Butte ARL Site.
A 72 mph wind gust was recorded at the Roberts ARL Site.
A 73 mph wind gust at Tom Cat Summit.
A 67 mph wind gust 1 mile northwest of Craters of the Moon.

A 58 mph wind gust at Moburg Canyon RAWS.
A 70 mph wind gust measured 9 miles northwest of Atomic City.
A 69 mph wind gust measured 11 miles east southeast of Butte City.
A 65 mph wind gust measured at Atomic City.
A 61 mph wind gust measured 11 miles west southwest of Atomic City.
A 65 mph wind gust measured 13 miles south of Craters of the Moon.
A 63 mph wind gust south southeast of Howe.
A 62 mph wind gust measured 3 miles west of Taber.
A 62 mph wind gust 12 miles northwest of Atomic City.
A 70 mph wind gust was measured 7 miles south of Howe at the ARL Station.
A 70 mph wind gust measured 9 miles south southwest of Mud Lake.
A 68 mph wind gust measured at ARL station Sand Dunes east of Howe.
A 60 mph wind gust measured 11 miles west of Osgood.
A 63 mph wind gust measured 8 miles northwest of Atomic City.
A trained spotter in Swan Valley reported several tree branches snapped off pine trees.
A 68 mph wind gust measured 1 mile from Terreton.
A 62 mph wind gust near Camas was measured.
Four to 5 inch diameter tree limbs broken near Niter in Caribou County.
A 2,000 wildfire located 5 miles west of Arco began on July 4th and was completely contained on July 9th.  No damage to structures was reported.

events.cz_name: BIG AND LITTLE WOOD RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: The 116 acre Lane's Creek wildfire actually started on June 30th and was allowed to burn the entire month of July.    It was damaging no property and was located on the eastern border of Idaho about 10 miles northwest of Thayne, Wyoming.  An Emergency Closure Order was in effect, closing the Lau Creek Trail from the Pine Bar Campground to the confluence of Brush Creek.
A 27 acre wildfire was started due to a blown tire on interstate 15 near Blackrock Canyon south of Pocatello.   It was started and contained on July 27th.
A 12 acre wildfire started about 8 miles south of Pocatello on July 25th and was contained by fire crews on July 27th.
A video of a weak tornado was posted on social media in open country just north of Soda Springs at 3:35 pm MDT on July 31st.
A large tree snapped due to a strong thunderstorm wind on July 4th.

A 37 year old woman and her 11 year daughter died in accidents near Fish Haven on Bear Lake.    Winds allegedly played a factor in causing flotation devices to drift from shore.    Highest recorded wind speeds at the Bear Lake airport near the time of accident were 29 mph.
A fire near Ballard and Hawthorne roads reached 150 feet of some houses but was extinguished before damaging any house. The fire was only one acre.
A vehicle fire started a 77 acre fire southeast of Fort Hall.    The fire damaged no homes.

The Lone Pine wildfire began on August 6th and was lightning caused.    It grew to 9,226 acres and was located about 7 miles east of Fort Hall.   No evacuations were required and although threatening some homes, no damage occurred.   The fire was considered contained and controlled on August 10th.
A 203 wildfire 5 miles north of Grace began just off of Highway 34.   The fire was likely started by lightning and was contained on August 8th.

A 3,106 acre fire began in the Arbon Valley in the Starlight Creek area.  The fire began on August 10th and was likely caused by lightning strikes a few days earlier.   The fire was contained and controlled on August 11th.   It was on the Fort Hall Indian Reservation and no evacuations were required and no property damage occurred.
A wildfire north of Soda Springs near the Monsanto plant grew to 365 acres The fire began August 8th  and was controlled and contained late that same night.

Lightning began a wildfire 6 miles northwest of Stanley on August 6th and burned nearly 800 acres.  Many hiking trails were closed due to the fire as well as Stanley Lake campground which was used as a command post.    The fire was contained on August 12th.

The Rocky Peak Fire was located about 10-miles north of Preston.   It was reported at 6:40 PM on August 4th.     It grew to 950 acres and was considered contained on August 5th.   Resources on the fire included 5 engines, a dozer, air attack, 11 smoke jumpers, and fuels crew.  Franklin County also provided fire support and traffic control.  The fire damaged no structures.
A strong thunderstorm wind downed a tree at the Pine Street and McKinley Avenue in Pocatello.   There were reports of other downed trees in Pocatello.

The Toponce fire began August 15th due to lightning strikes and burned 265 acres.   It was  considered 100 percent contained by August 30th.    It was located near Chesterfield Reservoir in Caribou County.   No damage occurred due to this wildfire.

The Laidlaw fire began August 18th southeast of Carey due to lightning strikes and burned 39,000 acres in open land.    It did start to spread into the Craters of the Moon National Monument but was slowed by rock formations.    The fire was considered controlled by August 20th.

A wildfire began August 21st 5 to 10 miles east of Idaho Falls and eventually grew to 53,000 acres  It was later determined to be human caused.   High winds on August 22nd and 23rd caused the rapid growth of the wildfire.   Over 4 million dollars were spent battling the wildfire.   Road closures were the following:  East Sunnyside from Crescent Drive, the intersection of Bone and Lincoln, Long Valley Road, and roads leading to Ririe Reservoir, including Blacktail, Tex Creek, Meadow Creek and Fall Creek.   Residents in the Birch Creek Loop east of Ririe and Moss Avery road were encouraged to evacuate their homes.   A disaster declaration was declared for Bonneville county by the Idaho governor.   785 homes were threatened in the Irwin and Swan Valley areas along with Palisades.   In the end no lives were lost and no injuries occurred.   No houses or cabins were destroyed and only some damage occurred to shed like structurres and telephone poles.   Property damage was very minimal.    the fire was considered contained and controlled on September 1st.

The Tie Canyon Fire was detected on August 22nd at 6 pm and was located in between Swan Valley and Victor.    The fire grew to 1,014 acres.   No mandatory evacuations were ordered.   Level one evacuation notices were in effect for residents and property owners south of 10000 South, east of HIghway 31, west of 1000 West (Pole Canyon Road) and west of Highway 31, south of 9000 South.    Tie Canyon Road 252 and Upper Rainey Creek Road 253 were closed.    black Grove Trail 047, Power Line Trail 321, and Blanchard Ridge sTrail 014 were closed by the United States Forest Service.    The fire was considered 100 percent contained by September 5th.

A fire began in Franklin County 50 miles north of the Utah border on August 23rd at around 1230 pm.   The fire burned 2,314 acres and was considered contained On August 25th.   Residents in the towns of Clifton and Dayton were evacuated to save homes and livestock.   No property damage was reported.

The Peterson Hollow Wildfire started in Utah on August 22nd and crossed into Idaho on August 24th. It increased to 1,121 acres and closures included the Beaver Creek and Sink Hollow Trails in both Utah and Idaho. Gibson Basin (FS Road 466), FS Road 316, and FS Road 411.

The Black Fire began On August 19th and was lightning caused.    It was located about 12 miles northwest of Swan Valley in Bonneville County and grew to 770 acres.  It was allowed to grow and burn naturally.    The fire continued well into September.
Lightning caused a wildfire about 5 miles north of Carey on August 31st and it grew quickly to 3,000 acres.   Full containment occurred on September 1st.   Lava rock helped to contain further growth.
Severe thunderstorm winds blew over two pine trees into a power line which started a small fire at East Pie Haven Drive in Island Park.

A lightning strike on August 18th caused damage at the Carey School in Blaine County. Problems occurred with the operations of the fire systems, the water irrigation system pump and the school district's connection to the heating and cooling systems.|No events found.
A 60 mph thunderstorm wind gust in Chubbuck.
A 773 acre wildfire began on August 29th due to lightning in Caribou County and continued through much of September.   It was in open land and was visible from Highway 34.

Lightning started the Grape Creek Fire on September 1st and continued into mid | September.   The fire grew to 1,580 acres near Elba.  The Independence Lake Trail was closed as well as Logger Springs Road.   It was considered completely contained on September 9th.
A 62 mph wind gust measured by Richfield.
A funnel cloud was photographed near Malad on September 14th.
Vehicle accident on US Highway 26 east of Ririe due to reduced visibility in blowing dust due to high winds.
A large tree was blown down by thunderstorm winds on September 14th at Highland Golf Course in Pocatello.
One inch hail in northwest Roberts.
Funnel cloud reported in Roberts.
A 60 mph wind gust recorded at the Rexburg airport ASOS.
A 60 mph wind gust measured at Sugar City mesonet site.
Golf ball sized hail reported at Chesterfield.
Two large cottonwood trees reported downed in Chester along with several tree limbs from other trees.
Blown over semi reported by spotter on Hog Hollow Road near Highway 33.
Funnel cloud near Lund.
Funnel cloud reported near Lava Hot Springs.   Radar indicated to south southeast of the town.

A fast moving hail storm caused multiple cars to slide off Highway 20 south in Rigby causing traffic to be blocked for miles in the southbound lanes.  Several vehicles were involved including one rollover and an RV and semi-truck.

Heavy snow fell in southeast Idaho from the evening of the 16th of October into the morning of the 17th.   12 inches were reported at the Emigrant Summit SNOTEL site.   9 inches were reported at the Slug Creek Divide SNOTEL with a spotter reporting 10 inches in Montpelier.
A funnel cloud was photographed at 1:58 pm MDT near Mt Putnam.
Atomic City mesonet reported 64 mph wind gust.
Idaho Falls airport ASOS reported 55 knot wind gust.
A 64 mph wind gust measured in the desert south southeast of Arco.
A 72 mph wind gust measured 30 miles northwest of Blackfoot.
A 68 mph wind gust at the Rover ARL site.
A 60 mph gust measured at the Rover ARL site.
A 66 mph wind gust measured at the Sand Dunes ARL site.
Estimated 60 mph wind gust in Thornton with power flickering on and off.

Two large trees were reported downed or uprooted in Pocatello.   A 12 to 18 inch diameter tree was uprooted 1 mile east of Popcatello and a two foot diameter tree was downed 2 miles northeast of Pocatello.   Siding was blown off one house in American Falls.
A large evergreen was blown over on 1000 North in the town of Hibbard closing one lane of traffic.  A large tree was also uprooted in Idaho Falls which also reported power outages.
Snow amounts were 12 inches in the Drake Creek area of the Teton valley and 8 inches in Victor.   At 4 am Highwy 32 was impassable from Ashton to Victor.

Two to 4 inches of snow fell in the region creating extremely icy road conditions the morning of the 28th.   A rollover caused one fatality on Highway 20 near Rexburg at around 8 am.   Several other crashes and slideoffs were also reported.   One rollover on interstate 15 near Shelley caused several to be taken to a local hospital.

Around 2 to 4 inches of snow fell creating very icy road conditions for the morning commute on November 28th.   There was a rollover on interstate on interstate 86 near Pocatello shortly before 7:30 am and 4 people were transported to a local hospital.  State police reported 6 crashes and 26 slide offs in the Pocatello  and surrounding areas during the morning commute.    There were also many slide offs reported in the Blackfoot area on interstate 15 during the morning commute.

events.cz_name: BIG AND LITTLE WOOD RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: High elevation snowfall amounts were 11 inches at Dollarhide Summit, 10 inches at Galena and Galena Summit, 12 inches at Lost Wood Divide, and 16 inches at Vienna Mine.   Six car crashes were reported in Blaine County.
