Interstate 15 was closed from exit 118 to exit 143 from Idaho Falls to Roberts due to blowing dust caused from the winds.  A boat was blown off a trailer near Ririe on US Highway 26.   Several trees were reported downed in Idaho Falls including one that fell on top of Holy Rosary Elementary School.  Some structural damage was reported in Idaho Falls due to trees falling on homes.   Damage to power lines resulted in over 2,500 customers without power reported by Rocky Mountain Power.   Power poles were downed in Terreton with nearly 200 customers without power.  Power poles and lines downed in Iona.  A large evergreen tree in Idaho Falls uprooted and took down power lines.  Siding was ripped off one home in Ucon and one home in Ririe.   A shed roof was destroyed in Rexburg.   Damages from the winds was estimated at near $275,000 for the wind storm.

Strong winds behind a powerful cold frontal passage knocked down power lines in McCammon.    Rocky Mountain Power reported 715 customers in the city without power.   an irrigation pivot was blown over and damaged in Robin.

Wind gusts of 50 to 73 mph occurred behind the passage of a strong cold front.   Some power lines were downed in Chester with 353 customers without power.   Power line damage caused 679 customers in Teton to lose power.   US Highway 20 was closed 3 miles east of Island Park with several accidents due to the high winds causing blowing snow and low visibility.   State Highway 87 north of Island Park was also closed due to the blowing and drifting snow.
Wind gusts of 54 to 64 mph were widespread behind the cold frontal passage.   A tree was downed southeast of Dietrich.
Funnel cloud viewed by NWS employee southwest of Atomic City.
KIFI News 8 posted picture of funnel cloud 7 miles west of Taber.
Tumbleweeds and tree limbs lifted into the air.

At least 28 reports of 1 to 2 inch hail were reported in the Ammon and Idaho Falls area and extensive damage was reported to residential and business structures.   Extensive automobile damage was reported as well.   Emergency management and insurance company reports estimated the damage from the large hail at $29,750,000.  Approximately 2,600 structures and 1,800 vehicles sustained damage from the hail storm.
Outflow winds from severe thunderstorms caused extensive property damage in Jefferson County with damage estimates at $90,000.
Thunderstorm outflow winds caused damage in Madison County with the Emergency manager reporting costs of $35,000.

In an odd occurrence, Idaho Fish and Game gathered 50 dead geese which were struck by lighting over the city of Idaho Falls.   They believed the geese were killed by lightning based on investigation of the geese's bodies.   The dead geese fell from the sky.  No monetary damage occurred, it was listed to be able to enter this event into the history of events.
A 61 mph wind gust was measured at the Rover ARL site at INL.

Seasonal snow melt flooding along with heavy rain caused significant damage to the levee near Lorenzo  as it was eroding 500 feet per day.    The Snake River and Henry's Fork of the Snake flowed at action stage for several weeks causing the event.   Jefferson County declared disaster as it was costing 9,000 dollars per day for seven days.  The County used all of their 40,000 dollars for the repairs to the levee and required further assistance from the US Corps of Engineers.
Several photographs from the public showed a funnel cloud near the Utah and Idaho border near interstate 84 just north of Snowville, Utah.   The funnel nearly reached the ground.
A 67 mph wind was recorded at the INL Puzzle site.
The Kettle Butte INL site recorded a 64 mph wind gust associated with a thunderstorm gust front.

Heavy rainfall of more than an inch caused flooding of streets in Pocatello.   Garrett Way was closed between N Main Street and W Cedar Street and Marlu Street was closed in front of Lewis and Clark Elementary School and Alameda Middle School.
Multiple reports of quarter sized hail in Burley.
One inch hail reported in Heyburn.
One inch hail reported in Rupert.
Severe thunderstorm winds damaged power lines in Rupert causing power outages for many Rupert residents.
A tree snapped at the tip with a second tree downed on house but no damage reported in Hailey.
A tree was downed and fell into a roadway blocking one lane of traffic in Ketchum.
A very heavy rainfall of over 2 inches in 30 minutes from a strong thunderstorm caused basements to flood and street flooding in Malad City.
Thunderstorm winds downed a power pole with wired across a road in St Anthony.
An inch and a quarter size hail reported 6 miles south of Murtaugh.
The Crystal RAWS measured an 89 mph wind gust.
The Atomic City ARL site recorded a 68 mph wind gust.
A spotter witnessed a rope tornado 15 miles south southwest of Mud Lake that quickly dissipated.
The Goose Creek RAWS site measured a 73 mph wind gust.
An inch and a quarter sized hail fell in Roberts.
A funnel cloud reported by spotter west of Parker.
One inch hail reported 4 miles west of Rexburg.
A spotter reported a funnel cloud 13 miles west of Rexburg on highway 33 at mile marker 64.
Spotter reported 1 inch hail on Highway 33 at mile marker 64 thirteen miles west of Rexburg.
One inch hail reported in St Anthony.
One inch hail reported at Island Park village Resort.
Several photographs received of a funnel cloud west and northwest of Idaho Falls around 5 pm MDT.
One inch hail in Rupert.
One inch hail in Ammon.
One inch hail in Roberts.
Extensive street flooding occurred from heavy rain from severe thunderstorms in Idaho Falls.   Minor basement flooding also occurred.
One inch hail near the Lowes in Idaho Falls.

A tornado crossed portions of the Idaho National Laboratory (INL) around East and Middle Buttes to the north and east across US 20 (including near the MFC facilities) between 400 and 430 pm MDT.  Due to sparseness of population and terrain, the only damage observed was at mile marker 277 on US Highway 20 at approximately 419 pm MDT.  At this point, large sections of 2 snow fences were heavily damaged  Multiple steel beems were bent and twisted to varying degrees, with portions of those beems that were below the surface and moved approximately one inch.   The horizontal part of these fences, make of vinyl and steel cable, were ripped apart and strewn for several yards.  Large metal pieces used to hold these together were snapped and/or thrown several yards away from the fence.   Other indications of tornado damage included a sign snapped off at the ground, sagebrush that was partially or completely ripped from the ground, and several small size lava rocks tossed an unknown distance.  ||Based on that evidence, the tornado was assigned an EF-1 rating.
The Big Lost Wood River flooded at Leslie on Highway 93.  Two homes were affected at the foundation with flooding.   They were upstream of the Highway 93 bridge over the Big Lost River.

A 500 acre wildfire occurred over Massacre Rocks about 5 to 10 miles southeast of American Falls. on June 9th and 10th.   The fire was driven by wind gusts of 40 mph and spread rapidly.   Cooler temperatures and lighter winds slowed growth and it was contained quickly over open land.   No structures were threatened.

Flooding of the Big Wood River for several months occurred in the Della View neighborhood of Hailey.   It finally ended in June but the total cost of the extensive flooding period resulted in $750,000 of insurance claims in the neighborhood and $200,000 for flood response and public property cleanup.
A wildfire began near American Falls on June 14th and quickly grew to 800 acres.   It was contained on June 15th.  No structures were threatened.
Quarter to half dollar sized hail was  reported in Wilford.
Heavy rains caused flash flooding in St Anthony with street flooding over curbs onto sidewalks and the edge of the parking lot at Wells Fargo Bank collapsed into the river.

A damage assessment team from the Pocatello National Weather Service Forecast Office traveled to Darlington, Idaho on June 22, 2018. The tornado was believed to have touched down around 1:15pm MDT on June 21, 2018, approximately 5 miles northwest of Darlington, Idaho.  The assessment team found several large hardwood tree limbs down along Huston Road. The largest diameter limb was 1 foot in diameter. About 1.5 miles down Huston Road from Highway 93, a residence on the south side of the road experienced extensive tree damage as well, including a hardwood tree split near the trunk. A second tree was completely uprooted although the root system appeared to be somewhat shallow, perhaps only a couple of feet deep. A third tree was nearly uprooted. A camper was overturned and a large section of the metal roofing had been peeled back. Some of the trusses off of a garage with a metal roof were ripped off. Video of the tornado showed it traveling to the north of Leslie Butte, although it is not clear if it was still on the ground at this point.  ||A second video shows the tornado on the ground approximately 1 mile northeast of Darlington around 1:32pm. The video shows the tornado on the ground for at least 3 minutes while east of Darlington. The damage team found a 40 to 50 foot section of barbed wire fencing down along with several metal fencing posts bent over or ripped out of the ground about 1.5 miles east of Darlington. The tornado lifted around 1:38pm MDT. The National Weather Service received reports of wheel lines, a chicken coop, pig pen, a shed destroyed, and a screen door ripped off. However, the damage assessment team was unable to find this damage. ||Based on the damage, the final assessment for this tornado is a high-end EF0 with winds of 75 to 85 mph. The tornado is estimated to have been 250 feet wide, 7 miles long, and lasted up to 23 minutes.
Heavy rains from a thunderstorm brought neighborhood street flooding to Idaho Falls with ankle deep water.  The main flooded area was the Stonebrook subdivision off of Sunnyside Road.

A strong thunderstorm dumped heavy rain and hail on Montpelier.   Washington Street, one of the main streets in the city, had several inches of water running on it.  Extensive hail fell as well with some small branches and limbs downed from trees and minor crop damage reported.

Extremely heavy rain caused mud slides and flooding mainly across the Squired Dugway area.  A lot of gravel roads suffered damage.  The Squired Dugway area had three homes and several outbuildings damages with livestock threatened.
Sixty mph wind gust measured at Idaho Falls Airport.
A 65 mph wind gust was meaasurede at the Idaho Falls ITD site at the interstate 15 and US highway 20 intersection.
Multiple trees and power lines reported in Idaho Falls.  2,000 customers were without electricity .
Vehicles reported submerged under water at the Northgate Mile Overpass. Additional reports of flooding from Lomax Street, Melody Street, Holmes Avenue and other streets.
A wildfire of about 200 acres began 1 mile southeast of Malad City on July 7th and burned grass, brush and juniper with no threat to structure east of interstate 15.
A 500 acre wildfire was started by lightning near Treasureton on Highway 34.   It was contained on July 12th.
A 77 acre fire began 5 miles southwest of Howe via a vehicle boat trailer dragging.   It grew to 77 acres before being contained.

A wildfire began on July 15th 5 miles east of Sage Junction south of Highway 33 due to exploding targets from gunfire practice.   It was near Menan Butte.   The fire grew to around 1,000 acres over grass and brush.  Highway 33 was closed for a short time.
A lightning induced fire began on July 16th north of the St Anthony Sand Dunes and grew to over 4,300 acres in grass and brush .
At 2:16 pm MDT a tree was reported blown down into a house on 3rd and Poplar in Bellevue.
A lightning induced wildfire began July 16th 5 miles southeast of Carey and burned over 4,000 acres of grass and brush before it was contained.  No property damage occurred.

The North Heglar fire was induced by lightning on July 16th and grew to 2,300 acres 24 miles southeast of the interstate 84/86 interchange.   IT was grass, brush and timber with some structures threatened.   North Heglar Road and Mill Flat Campground were closed to the public.

The 600 acre Twin Butte Fire started 5 miles west of Rexburg south of Highway 33 near Menan BUtte.  It was a grass and brush fire and Highway 33 was closed for a short time.   The fire began at around 1:45 MDT on July 24th.  No structures were threatened.
Several large trees reported snapped off near base near Idaho Falls airport, including on Singletree Circle.   Tree also reported down at Old Butte Soccer Complex.
Tree downed destroying a fence along East 97th North southwest of Ucon.

Numerous large trees reported down in Idaho Falls.   Homes and vehicles damaged.   One wood and sheet metal shed destroyed.   Several fences were blown down.  At least 9,000 electric customers were without power.
Power pole downed near Utah Avenue.
A large Wendy's sign blown out with debris in the roadway near the intersection of N Holmes Ave and N Yellowstone Highway.
Two trees downed on University Place campus.
A row of partially constructed storage units collapsed on East Iona Rd near North 15th East.
Multiple large trees downed at Pinecrest Municipal Golf Course.
Power lines downed near the intersection of 33rd St and 5th E.
A tree was downed at Rose Hill Cemetery.
The Jim Sage fire began July 26th and was caused by lightning 5 miles southeast of Elba.    It burned about 2,000 acres of grass, brush and juniper.
A 63 mph wind gust at ARL site 12 miles northwest of Atomic City.
A 62 mph wind gust was recorded by COOP Observer in Bern.
A 64 mph wind gust was measured at the Craters of the Moon mesonet site.
A 60 mph wind gust was measured at the mesonet site 11 miles west southwest of Atomic City.
A 59 mph wind gust was measured 10 miles south southwest of Howe.
One inch hail in the town of Franklin.
One inch hail reported in Weston.
Quarter to half dollar sized hail 1 mile west of Soda Springs.
Inch and quarter hail measured in Soda Springs.
Ping pong ball sized hail reported in the town of Clifton.  Some damage to siding reported on homes.
One inch hail in Oxford.
Quarter sized hail at the Treasureton Reservoir.
A 77 mph thunderstorm wind gust measured 14 miles north northwest of Holbrook or near Roy.

The Sharps fire began by human cause on July 29th via exploding targets.   It continued through a good part of August and grew to 64,853 acres and located approximately 6 miles east of Bellevue on Sharps Canyon Road. The BLM closed public lands in and around the Sharps fire in Blaine County. This included all BLM-managed lands east of Highway 75, south of East Fork Road, then south of the Sawtooth National Forest Boundary, west of Fish Creek Road, and north of US Highway 20, and east of Gannett Road.   Other closures were the following:  Muldoon Canyon Road is closed from EE-DA-HO Ranch (east of Bellevue). East Fork Road is closed at Triumph. Little Wood Reservoir Road is closed at the Hunt Lane. Quigley, Slaughterhouse Creek Roads, Indian Creek, and Ohio Gulch Roads are closed where the pavement ends. High Five, Road Canyon Road and Baugh Creek, are also closed.   No structures were damaged.  Mandatory evacuations were ordered for Little Wood recreation Area campground and all residences on Little Wood Reservoir Road and Flat Top Road north of the reservoir.

A lightning caused fire began August 2nd and continued through the month of August north of Challis.  The fire was predominately in Lemhi County but also burned in parts of northern Custer County as well.   The fire burned lodgepole pine and douglas fir and higher elevation subalpine fir and whitebark pine.  Also grass and brush burned.  THe fire grew to over 35,000 acres by the end of August.

Lightning began a fire at around 7:30 AM on August 13th 1 mile north of the Chesterfield Reservoir on the Fort Hall Reservation .  The fire burned grass and brush in steep terrain and burned 2,380 acres .  It was contained by 7 pm on August 16th.   It was in open land.
A 2,500 acre wild fire began on August 16th on the Fort Hall Indian Reservation east of interstate 15.   50 homes had to be evacuated as the fire spread rapidly.

The Indian Butte wildfire began September 12th at around 6 pm MDT and burned 13,072 acres in Clark County.   It began on Indian Creek Road 9 miles northwest of Dubois and was human caused.  Dry Creek road and a portion of Pleasant valley Road were closed.    Campers were evacuated on the 13th in the Dry Creek and Pleasant Valley area.  One home was evacuated on the 12th but did not get damaged.  The fire burned in grass, brush and timber.   The fire was considered 100 percent contained on September 20th.

A fire began about 2 miles south of the Pocatello Regional Airport near Michaud Creek Road.   The fire began around 1 pm MDT on the 15h and 40 mph winds spread the fire rapidly to 254 acres on the Fort Hall Indian Reservation.  The fire destroyed two mobile homes and two sheds but none were primary residences.   The fire also downed multiple power lines and 70 Idaho Power customers were without electricity.   The fire was contained by the evening of September 16th.

Fire began at around 4 pm MDT on September 19th on private land and quickly spread to 911 acres before being contained.   It burned in grass, brush and maples on steep ground.   The fire was 100 percent contained on September 20th.

A fire which was begun 5 miles southeast of Soda Springs by sparks from a welder repairing a mail box, burned 1,066 acres and destroyed 2 summer homes and 2 trailers. The fire began September 22nd at around 2 pm MDT and was 100 percent contained on September 25th. It burned in grass, brush and scattered timber.

A fire which was an escaped agricultural burn grew to 13,500 acres 4 miles southeast of Malta.  It began September 22nd and was controlled don September 27th.   It burned grass, brush and timber but caused no structural damage.
Spotters recorded 6 inches of snow in Burley, 7 inches in Minidoka and 13 inches in Shoshone with extensive road closures including interstate 84.
Six inches of snow fell in the city of Rockford and interstate 86 closed the evening of the 31st west of Chubbuck.  Amounts of 3 inches were reported in American Falls and 4 inches in Aberdeen.

Only 3 to 5 inches of snow were reported in the Upper Snake River Plain with 3 inches at Idaho Falls, but winds combined with the snow to cause the closure of route 20 west of Idaho Falls through the INL site.
Ten inches of snow were reported at the Mill Creek Summit and Bear Canyon SNOTEL sites.
Heavy snow fell in the Upper Snake River Highlands.  Some snow amounts were 13 inches in Ashton, 18 inches in Island Park, and 9 inches at St. Anthony.

Very heavy snow fell in the South Central Highlands with 15 inches reported by spotters in Holbrook.  Over two feet of snow fell at elevations above 7500 feet with 28 inches at the Bostetter SNOTEL and 30 inches at the Howell Canyon SNOTEL.  Fourteen inches fell at Oxford Springs.

Heavy snow fell in the Caribou Highlands with 10 inches at Pine Creek Pass, 20 inches at Sedgewick Peak, 15 inches at Sheep Mountain, 10 inches at Wild Horse Divide, and 12 inches reported by a spotter in Wayan.
Heavy snow fell above 7,000 feet with 16 inches reported at the Franklin Basin SNOTEL and 17 inches at the Emigrant Summit SNOTEL.

events.cz_name: BIG AND LITTLE WOOD RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: Eleven to 12 inches of snow were reported by spotters in Ketchum and Hailey.  Heavy SNOTEL amounts were 15 inches at Dollarhide, 16 inches at Galena, 19 inches at Galena Summit, 20 inches at Lost Wood Divide, and 22 inches at Vienna Mine.

Over three feet of snow fell at SNOTEL sites with elevations near 8,000 feet.  Amounts were 39 inches at Bear Canyon, 22 inches at Stinckney Mill, and 35 inches at Smiley Mountain.  Spotters reported 15 inches in Hailey.

The heaviest SNOTEL snow reports were 36 inches at Black Bear, 18 inches at Crab Creek, 14 inches at White Elephant and 10 inches at Island Park.  Interstate 15 was closed from Dubois to the Montana state line.  US route 20 was closed from Island Park to the Montana state line.
Strong winds and 2 to 5 inches of snow closed US Route 20 from Idaho Falls to Howe Junction.

Three to seven inches of snow combined with strong winds closed interstate 84 from the junction of interstate 86 to the Utah state line on the morning of the 28th.  Whiteout conditions were widespread.
Heavy snow fell above 6,000 feet with 12 inches at Sedgewick Peak and 9 inches at Somsen Ranch SNOTELs.
Heavy snow fell in the Idaho Wasatch with 12 inches at Franklin Basin and 14 inches at the Giveout SNOTEL.

events.cz_name: BIG AND LITTLE WOOD RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: Widespread snow amounts over 1 foot fell at SNOTEL sites in the Wood River Reigon.  Heaviest amounts were 29 inches at Dollarhide, 18 inches at Chocolate Gulch, 22 inches at Galena Summit, 37 inches at Lost Wood Divide, 23 inches at Swede Peak, and 23 inches at Vienna Mine.  15 inches were reported in Hailey by spotters.
Four feet of snow fell at the Hilts Creek SNOTEL with 23 inches at Meadow Lake and 18 inches at Moonshine.
Heavy snow fell in the Upper Snake Highlands with 12 inches at Island Park, 14 inches at White Elephant, 22 inches at Black Bear, and 23 inches at Crab Creek.
A spotter reported 13 inches of snow in Holbrook.  SNOTEL amounts were 17 inches at Bostetter, 38 inches at Howell Canyon and 12 inches at Oxford Springs.
The Sedgewick Peak SNOTEL recorded 12 inches of snow.
Fourteen inches of snow were recorded at both the Emigrant Summit and Franklin Basin SNOTEL sites.

events.cz_name: BIG AND LITTLE WOOD RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: Twelve inches of snow was recorded at the Galena Summit SNOTEL site.
Wind chill readings below 25 degrees zero were recorded in Fremont County with many schools closed.
Wind chill readings fell below 25 degrees below zero at many locations in the Upper Snake River Plain.
Wind chill readings were below 25 degrees below zero at many locations in the morning hours on the 16th.
Wind gusts up to 75 mph were recorded at the POcatello REgional Airport and in the city of Chubbuck causing power outages, 60 foot trees downed and store signs were destroyed.

events.cz_name: BIG AND LITTLE WOOD RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: Heavy snow and winds caused four avalanches along Warm Springs Road. A garage and patio were destroyed with road closures.
Heavy snow in the Sawtooths measured 23 inches at Bear Canyon, 11 inches at Stinckney Mill, 24 inches at Smiley Mountain, and 15 inches at Mill Creek Summit.
Snow totals from SNOTEL sites in the Upper Snake Highlands were 13 inches at Crab Creek and 8 inches at Island Park.
Ten inches of snow fell at the Franklin Basin SNOTEL site.

events.cz_name: BIG AND LITTLE WOOD RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: Snow totals in the Wood River region were 20 inches in Ketchum, 30 inches at Vienna Mine, 19 inches at Swede Peak, 23 inches at Lost Wood Divide, 26 inches at Galena Summit, and 15 inches at Chocolate Gulch.
The heaviest snow amounts were 26 inches at the Hilts Creek SNOTEL and 14 inches at the Moonshine SNOTEL.

The southern hills and Albion Mountains were hit with a significant fall snow storm. The snow fell on October 9th and 10th and 32 hour totals were 13 inches at Pomerelle Ski Resort at the top of the mountain and 8 inches at the base, 8 inches at Bostetter Ranger Station and 12 inches at Howell Canyon.

A strong cold front moved through eastern Idaho with strong winds behind it. Interstate 15 was closed due to blowing dust from 2 pm to 4 pm between exits 118 and 150. Wind gusts of 50 to 60 mph were widespread.
