Extremely heavy winter snows caused continued road closures in Clark County closing two roads for several days. The roads closed were Kilgore A2 and Old 91 from McCullough Ranch to Spencer.
Extremely heavy winter snows caused continued road closures in Clark County closing two roads for several days. The roads closed were Kilgore A2 and Old 91 from McCullough Ranch to Spencer.

The Pebble Creek ski area mid mountain measuring site recorded the greatest seasonal snowfall of 339 inches through March 15th breaking the record of 330 inches set in 2016-2017.    This amount was recorded from December 1st through March 15th.   The ski resort is located south of the city of Pocatello.
Heavy snow fell in the northern parts of the Eastern Magic Valley with 9 inches in Shoshone and 14 inches in Richfield.
Storm total snow amounts reported by trained spotters in the Upper Snake Highlands were 12 inches at Island Park, 11 inches at Macks Inn, and 16 inches at Marysville.
A wide variety of snow amounts were measured in the Upper Snake River Plain.  Four inches fell in Idaho Falls with the heaviest amounts measured of 6 inches in Hamer and 12 inches in Taber.

Two periods of heavy snow fell in the Pocatello region.  One on the morning of the 3rd then overnight on the 3rd and 4th.  Generally 3 to 6 inches fell in both periods.  Total amounts measured were 6 inches in the cities of Pocatello and Chubbuck with 8 to 12 inches on the eastern and western benches.  School district 25 covering the city of Pocatello was closed on February 4th due to the snow.
Heavy snow fell above 6,000 feet in the South Central Highlands with 18 inches at Oxford Springs and 23 inches at Bostetter.  Twelve inches of snow were reported by spotters in Malad City.
Sixteen inches of snow measured 10 miles east of Pocatello.  Nineteen inches of snow fell at Wild Horse Divide, 9 inches at Sheep Mountain, and 15 inches at Sedgewick Peak.
Sixteen inches of snow were reported by COOP observer in Weston with 3 foot drifts.  One foot of snow was reported in Preston.
Heavy snow fell in the Idaho Wasatch with 15 inches at Franklin Basin and 12 inches at Emigrant Summit.

events.cz_name: BIG AND LITTLE WOOD RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: Snow amounts of 11 inches at Galena Summit and 9 inches at Vienna Mine were reported.

Snowfall fell throughout the day on the 13th in Pocatello with amounts of 6 inches measured at the Pocatello Regional Airport by the National Weather Service.  Six inches also were measured in Chubbuck and the city of Pocatello.
Heavy snow fell in Madison County.  Seven to nine inches of snow was reported in Rexburg with 6 to 8 inches in Lorenzo and 8 inches in Sugar City.  Idaho Falls in Bonneville County reported 5 inches.
Nine inches of snow fell in Island Park.
Ten inches of snow was reported at Wild Horse Divide.

events.cz_name: BIG AND LITTLE WOOD RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: Nine inches of snow was reported at Galena Summit.

Although listed as sleet this was a heavy rain and small hail event.   It was listed as sleet to ensure a zone forecast area rather than counties as it covered multiple counties.  ||Very heavy rain combined with accumulating very small hail caused many traffic accidents on interstates 15 and 86 from Fort Hall to Pocatello and from Pocatello to American Falls.  Some injuries occurred and traffic was backed up for several miles.

Multiple avalanches occurred near Ketchum on April 8th.   The first one was around 2:30 PM and severely damaged two homes believed to be unoccupied on Warm Springs Road west of Ketchum.   It was a large wet slab avalanche.   The total assessed value of the damaged homes was approximately $200,000.   A second avalanche in the same location occurred at around 6:45 PM but no houses, or vehicles were involved.

Several roads were closed by Blaine County Road and Bridge on April 8th in Hailey due to heavy snow melt.  They were Parker Gulch, Rock Creek Rd, W. Glendale Rd, Road Canyon, Meacham Lane, and Dry Creek Rd.

Snow fell in Fremont County during the morning of the 15th with 2 to 4 inches. The snow caused very dangerous road conditions. A semi truck rolled off US Highway 20 near Elk Creek Station around milepost 388. Other crashes occurred north of Ashton and near Mack's Inn between 8 and 9 am MDT.
Minor flooding began April 21st on War Eagle Drive in Hailey. Through access through the Della View neighborhood was shut down in western Hailey.

Winds gusted to 60 mph along interstate 15 north of Idaho Falls and Roberts on April 27th.   Interstate 15 shut down due to the wind and blowing dust in a 16 mile stretch between Idaho Falls and Roberts.   The wind gusted to 55 mph at the Idaho Falls airport ASOS.   The interstate closed at around 5 pm MDT.   A semi tractor trailer rolled on interstate 4 miles north of Roberts possibly due to the high winds at around 3:30 pm MDT.
Fourteen inches of snow was reported at Mill Creek Summit.
Ten inches of snow fell in Island Park.  Ten inches of snow fell in Marysville.  Nine inches fell in Victor and Ashton.  US Route 26 was closed from Ririe to Swan Valley to Alpine, Wyoming.
US Highway 20 was closed from Carey to Arco and from Butte City to Idaho Falls.  Zero visibility reported in Taber with 4 foot snow drifts.  Total white out conditions reported in Bingham County.
Interstate 84 was closed from the Interstate 86 junction to the Utah state line with white out conditions reported.
Twelve inches of snow fell at Pine Creek Pass with ten inches at Sedgewick Peak.  State Highway 36 was closed from Malad to Weston with white out conditions.
State Highway 36 was closed from Malad to Weston due to heavy snow and reduced visibility creating white out conditions.
Twelve inches of snow fell in Franklin Basin.  Four inches of snow fell in Montpelier with 4 hours of sustained 50 MPH winds.

events.cz_name: BIG AND LITTLE WOOD RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: Heavy snow fell throughout the Wood River region.  18 inches fell at Dollarhide, 9 inches at Galena, 10 inches at Galena Summit, 10 inches at Lost Wood Divide, and 16 inches at Vienna Mine.
Moburg Canyon recorded sustained 40 to 55 mph winds for 8 hours with gusts of 70 to 80 mph.
A spotter recorded sustained 62 mph winds at 730 am on the benches one mile east of Pocatello.
State Highway 22 from the State Highway 33 intersection to Dubois was closed due to blowing snow with wind gusts over 50 mph occurring in Dubois from midnight through 8 am.
US Route 20 was closed from Butte City to Idaho Falls due to blowing snow and white out conditions.

events.cz_name: BIG AND LITTLE WOOD RIVER REGION
events.event_narrative: Nine inches of snow fell at Dollarhide and 11 inches fell at Swede Peak in the Big and Little Wood River area.
Thirty to 40 mph wind gusts closed interstate 15 from Idaho Falls to Roberts at 1:20 pm MDT on the 2nd through 10 pm.   Blowing dust reduced visibility to zero on that stretch of interstate.

Thunderstorm winds caused a a tree to come down onto a power line and crews worked quickly to remove the obstruction and restore power to affected customers.  The reported outage affected over 3,800 Idaho Power customers in Chubbuck for approximately 45 minutes Tuesday.||The outage occurred around 2:30 p.m. and was resolved around 3:10 p.m.

Five to 6 power poles were snapped down 1 mile south of Darlington due to strong thunderstorm winds.  The poles were snapped off just above the ground.  It occurred near the mouth of Antelope Springs.
A 59 mph wind gust was measured at the  mesonet station ITD95, intersection of US-20 |and US-26.
The mesonet station PBF - Critical Infrastructure Complex recorded 58 mph wind gust .
One inch hail reported in Ketchum taking leaves off trees.
Mesonet station NFFI1 recorded a 63 mph wind gust 7 miles north northwest of Ketchum.
One inch hail photographed in Aberdeen.

An EF0 tornado touched down 2 miles south of Riverside nd moved north for 1.8 miles crossing the Snake River before dissipating just south os W 100 S (Thomas Road) and between S 275 W and S 670 W just south of Riverside.  Damage consisted of a mix of several young and mature cottonwood trees that were wither snapped or uprooted on both private and BLM land . One downed live tree measured a foot in diameter.  Another much larger downed tree was found with a diameter close to two feet.  Minor damage was reported to a greenhouse.  Maximum wind speeds were estimated at 80 to 85 mph with path width of 50-100 yards.  It was on the ground for 1.8 miles.
Funnel cloud photographed from Arco.
Funnel cloud photographed from Sugar City.
Funnel cloud photographed from Aberdeen.
Funnel cloud photographed in Rexburg.
A funnel cloud was spotted near Rockland on the afternoon of the 28th .

The public took several pictures of a tornado located 4 miles south-southeast of the town of Bone in Bonneville County but the tornado occurred in Bingham County near the county border.  It occurred completely in open field and no damage occurred.
Funnel cloud photograph taken by public.

Some minor flooding occurred for several days in the Della area in Hailey with water reaching housed and some roads closed. Significant damage was not reported. The City of Hailey has placed hard road closures in the Della area from the West end of Cedar Street past Della Vista Dr ending at Triumph Dr. Water is running from the Draper Preserve area from the river.
Multiple trees were reported downed in St Anthony with one across a power line.  400 customers were without power for a couple of hours.
A funnel cloud was observed on Porterville Road just north of Blackfoot.
Sugar City mesonet site recorded 58 mph wind gust.
The mesonet site 6 miles northwest of Atomic City recorded a wind gust of 60 mph at the intersection of US Highway 20/26.
The trained spotter in Bern recorded a 64 mph thunderstorm wind gust.
The mesonet station ITD37 at Rocky Point on Highway 30 recorded a wind gust of 62 mph.
One inch hail reported 4 miles northeast of Shelley.
Rain amounts of 0.80 inches caused flowing water across roads on the south side of Hailey near Friedman Memorial Airport.
One inch hail 4 miles west southwest of Parker.
Several funnels spotted with rotating wall cloud.
Funnel cloud seen over the Rexburg LDS temple.
A storm chaser estimated 60 mph wind gusts in Rexburg.
A tree fell down and damaged a house in Thornton.   A shed on Teton Road in eastern Madison County was destroyed.

Large shed and adjacent concrete pad thrown across the road along E 500 N in the area of n 1800 E.  Irrigation pivot overturned just sough of e 500 N and just west of N 1800 E.  Portion of a sheet metal rood peeled back and damaged on a barn.
A survey found large tree limbs down along E 400 N.

Over a dozen trees were down in the area of N 1900 E just north of E 400 N.   Many snapped off at various heights.  Portion of sheet metal roof and adjacent plywood removed from building and found in ditch.
Several large tree limbs and one large healthy tree snapped near Lyman-Union Road.
A large tree was downed in the Heise area.
A storm survey found several large cottonwood limbs removed from trees near Archer.

Strong winds accompanied a cold front with widespread gusts over 50 mph with some over 65 mph.   Two miles northwest of Idaho Falls a large tree blew onto a car at the Idaho Falls Activity Center at 4:30 pm MDT.    AT 5 pm MDT a small tree was downed onto a vehicle at E Tawzer Way near E Barton Lane 2 miles south southeast of Ammon.   A large tree and Power lines were down on S 5th W near Mesa Falls Apartments in Rexburg at 6:27 pm MDT.  The road was closed by fire and law enforcement.   A large pine tree approximately 3 feet in diameter was uprooted at Pinecrest Gold Course in Idaho Falls.
About 200 people were without power in Idaho Falls in the Holmes and Cleveland street areas due to strong winds damaging power lines.
A 68 mph wind gust was measured during a thunderstorm at Big Southern Summit.

A lightning strike caused a fire in Jefferson County near Table Butte on BLM property.   The grass and brush fire burned over 800 acres.   The fire began around 2 pm MDT on the 2nd and was controlled by July 3rd.  No structures were threatened and no evacuations occurred.  The Camas Monteview Road in Jefferson County was closed briefly during the fire .
A nearly 9,500 grass and brush wildfire was started by lightning on July 6th at 5:30 MDT.  No structures were threatened and no evacuations were required.  The fire was controlled on July 9th.

Lightning caused an 8,272 acre fire 7 miles north of Raft River on BLM property.  It was a grass and brush fire that began on July 6th at around 3 pm MDT.  It was controlled on July 8th with no structures threatened and no evacuations required.

The Shady wildfire began with a lightning strike on July 10th and burned over 3,600 acres by the end of July in northwestern Custer County.  The fire burned subalpine fir and lodgepole pine.   Many closures occurred including Sheep Mountain Road beginning at the junction of FS Road 40008 at Seafoam Guard Station ending at road 40172.  Forest trail 4005 was closed (Sheep Creek Trail).   Duffield Trail, and Bernard Creek Trail were also closed.  The fire was a semi-contained fire and continued burning through August.

A 71 mph wind gust occurred around 9 pm MDT on July 12th on interstate 15 southbound near the Northgate interchange.   It picked up a large Idaho Transportation Department portable digital sign and hurled in into traffic on Interstate 15 southbound.  The sign struck a car and a SUV heavily damaging both vehicles and both had to be towed from the interstate.   No injuries occurred to the drivers or passengers.

The twenty mile fire began on July 12th at around 8:30 pm MDT just over 20 miles west of Idaho Falls.   It was caused by lightning and burned around 200 acres of grash and brush.  No structures were threatened with no closures or evacuations.  It was controlled by July 14th.   Rain on the 13th helped with containment.

On July 12th at about 9:15 pm lightning hit a chimney at the ARTitorium in downtown Idaho Falls.   The Destinations Inn which shares a building with the ARTitorium was evacuated by all 24 guests until fire fighters could inspect the building.   One vehicle was hit by a brick from the chimney. Damage amounts were estimated.
Thunderstorm winds blew down trees near 5th West and Rockingham Streets on July 12th at around 9 pm MDT in Idaho Falls.
A 71 mph wind gust was recorded at the Pocatello ASOS and a large pine tree was snapped and fell into the parking lot at the National Weather Service Office.
Lightning caused the Ridgeline fire 7 miles northeast of Albion.   It was 1,000 acres of grass, brush and juniper.   Structures were threatened but not damaged.

The Vader Fire was located 13 miles northwest of Stanley south of Highway 21.  Thatcher Creek Campground and Vader Creek Day-Use Area were closed.  Highway 21 was also closed for a short time.  It burned 443 acres.   It burned lodgepole pine and the cause was not known.

The Sheep wildfire began on July 22nd northeast of the Material Fuels Complex on the Idaho National Laboratory Complex.   It was caused by lightning and by the afternoon of July 23rd had spread to near 90,000 acres all on the complex.    By the morning of the 24th it was estimated at 110,000 acres.  Strong southwest winds Tuesday afternoon caused rapid spread of the fire.  Some work operations at the Complex were affected with some employees not reporting for work the 23rd and 24th.   Full operations resumed by the 25th.   No significant damage occurred.

The 1,300 acre fire 3 miles northeast of Shoshone began by lightning on July 22nd and burned grass and brush was controlled by July 25th.   No structures were threatened.  Highway 75 was shut down for a very short time on July 23rd.

The Tincup fire began July 30th due to a lightning strike and burned the entire month of August.  It was located approximately 30 miles northeast of Soda Springs.  It was allowed to burn naturally and grew to 264 acres by the end of August.  It reduced heavy dead and down fuel loading that was above historic range to to past fire suppression.

A lightning strike caused the 4,889 acre Spud Fire approximately 12 miles southwest of Carey.  It burned grass and brush and threatened no structures.  It began around 5:30 PM MDT on August 1st and was controlled on August 5th.
A National Weather Service photographed a tornado southwest of Lake Wolcott at 1:55 PM MDT on August 2nd.  It occurred over open land and no damage occurred.
Three branches were downed from a cottonwood tree 4 miles north of Lago.  The largest was 4 inches in diameter.
On August 9th a mud slide occurred one mile past the east fort of Baker Creek.   Warm Springs Road was impassable from the west of the Hot Springs in Ketchum.  3 to 5 inches of mud covered the road.

The Treasureton Fore was started bu farm equipment on August 15th at about 3:30 pm MDT about 13 miles north of Preston near Treasureton .  It grew to 363 acres in rugged terrain covered by grass, brush and juniper.  No structures were threatened and it was contained on August 16th.
A 61 mph wind gust measured in Challis.
A spotter measured 1.25 inch hail 12 miles southeast of Almo.
A 60 mph wind gust was measured at the Osgood ITD site 6 miles north northwest of Idaho Falls.
Cold air funnels were reported by spotters and the tower at the Pocatello Regional Airport.  No touchdowns reported.

Lightning caused a 10,000 acre 12 miles northwest of Aberdeen on September 5th.  It burned grassland in remote areas on Bureau of Land Management property.  No structures were threatened.  Rain stopped a spread of the fire.
Six trees down On Yankee Fork River in Clayton. Metal roof torn off the Yankee Fork Ranger Station .
Four to 5 inches of snow fell near Island Park on the 28th and 29th and several crashes occurred on US Route 20 near Island Park.

Four to six inches of snow was reported by COOP observers and the public in Dubois.  The snow was accompanied with high winds and extensive blowing and drifting snow.   Interstate 15 was closed from Dubois to the Montana border.  A-2 Road and Old 91 Route North were also closed at the same time.   Multiple slide offs occurred prior to the roads being closed.

Very heavy early autumn snow fell in the Island Park area with 6 inches measured at the Island Park Ranger Station with 6 to 8 inches at SNOTEL sites above 6,000 feet.   Many slide offs reported on US Highway 20.
Four power poles snapped in half between N Apple St and N Birch St.  Large tree downed at W 4th St and N Cherry St.  An outside ice storage bin flipped over and reports of multiple trees downed.
Multiple power poles down south of Shoshone along US Route 93.
Large metal and wood barn door broken in half along S 900 W north of W 400 S.  Some sheet metal peeled off roof of structure.
A 64 mph wind gust measured at the Rock Lake RAWS site.
A large tree snapped off 7 feet above the ground in Burley.
Large evergreen tree snapped off near the base in Heyburn.
A tree was downed 5 miles west northwest of Paul.
A 60 mph wind gust measured at the Minidoka mesonet station.
A large section of a tree down on 3rd st just east of H St in Rupert.  Sheet metal debris strewn about the city.
Two power poles snapped off near their bases on S Pole Line Rd just north of W 800 S.

A very large tree over 3 feet in diameter was uprooted and crashed into a residence on E 400 S just west of S 350 E.  Roof and the back half of residence were destroyed.  A second large tree next to the residence also uprooted.   Large trees were snapped off approximately half way up along E 400 S near S 250 E.  2 other large trees 2-3 feet in diameter uprooted half way in between S 350 E and S 250 E and power pole was snapped in half.
Several large trees downed at residence along S Pole Line Rd between W 900 S and W 1000 S.
Four power poles snapped off near their base along Highway 27 between W 800 S and W 900 S.  Long row of irrigation pivots blown over nearby.  All damage indicative of straight line winds.
A private weather station measured a 65 mph wind gust near W 700 S and S 300 W.
A large electronic construction sign blown over along Interstate 84 east bound just west of the interstate 86/84 interchange.
The top half of a large pine tree snapped off just west of highway 24 near Acequia.  Numerous other branches broken off nearby trees.
Tree reported by broadcast media in Jackson area.   Near Cassia/Minidoka County border.
The RPTI mesonet site recorded a 59 mph wind gust.
A private weather station recorded a 66 mph wind gust near E 600 N and 700 Rd E.
A private weather station measured a 58 mph wind gust near the intersection of N 100 |E and E 300 N.
A private weather station near E 600 S and S 650 E measured a 62 mph wind gust.
A private weather station measured a 65 mph wind gust near Highway 77.

About 30 large hardwood trees either uprooted or snapped due to a likely microburst.  One tree caused moderate damage to a RV, while another destroyed a pickup truck parked nearby.  Another tree fell onto a baseball field fence.  An open ended trailer rolled one turn on it's side significantly damaging it.   A nearby heavy metal picnic table was flipped and shingle damage noted on a marina facilities building.
A 1 foot diameter tree snapped off approximately half way up.   It damaged an irrigation pivot.

A residence with 7 large healthy trees uprooted or snapped off.   Several were at least 2 feet in diameter.   Two trees fell on and damaged a back deck and several pieces of flashing were blown off of the house.
Mesonet station TR256, Sawtooth Portable No 2 recorded 64 mph wind gust.
Media reports power outages in Shoshone and Dietrich.
Mesonet station MOFI1, Moburg Canyon recorded a 61 mph wind gust.
Nine inches of snow fell at the Bear Canyon SNOTEL and 10 inches fell at Smiley Mountain SNOTEL.
Ten inches of snow fell at the Franklin Basin SNOTEL.
Nine inches of snow fell at the Galena Summit SNOTEL with 11 inches at Galena, and 12 inches at Lost Wood Divide.
Eleven inches of snow fell at the Mill Creek Summit SNOTEL.
Ten inches of snow fell at the Smiley Mountain SNOTEL.
A total of 17 inches of snow was estimated at the Vienna Mine SNOTEL.

Although the entire Pocatello forecast area experienced the all time coldest October on record will focus on the Lower Snake River Plain for a single event report.   Here are some of the highlights in the data recorded by the Pocatello ASOS located at the Pocatello Regional Airport:  ||The monthly average temperatures of 38.4 degrees was 4.1 degrees colder than the previous monthly low average of 42.5 degrees set in 2002.||10 record low temperatures were set during the month on the 3rd, 10th, 11th, 12th, 24th, 27th, 28th, 29th, 30th, and 31st.   ||The -6 degrees on October 30th was the first ever below zero temperature recorded in October in Pocatello and 13 degrees colder than the previous coldest October temperature recorded of 7 above.
Heavy snow fell in the Caribou range with 10 inches falling at the following SNOTEL sites:  Giveout, Slug Creek Divide, and Somsen Ranch.

Snow began on the 28th ahead of an arctic cold front and roads froze quickly on the evening of the 28th.   2 to 4 inches fell in the Pocatello/Chubbuck region through the event and impacts were significant.   Interstate 86 eastbound was shut down from the Yellowstone Ave exit east to the interstate 15 interchange.   40 to 50 vehicles were stranded or off the road.   Multiple vehicles off the road along interstate 15 as well just north of the interstate 86 interchange.   Multiple tractor trailers also stuck on interstate 15 south of the interchange.   This occurred between 9 and 10 pm on the 28th.    The 20 to 35 mph winds caused snow drifts up to 20 inches on some roads in Blackfoot.  A tractor trailer overturned on interstate 15 in Blackfoot a couple of miles south of exit 89.   The Pocatello/Chubbuck School District #25 closed schools on the 29th due to the hazardous road conditions.

Although only 1 to 3 inches of snow fell, strong northerly winds caused extensive blowing and drifting snow and travel impacts.   US Highway 20 was closed for one hour on the morning of the 29th from Argon National Engineering Lab Road at the INL site to Croft Road west of Idaho Falls due to the drifting snow and multiple slide offs.
Heavy snow fell in the Bear River Range with 13 inches recorded at the Franklin Basin SNOTEL site.
Heavy snow fell in the Upper Snake Highlands with 12 inches in Marysville and 10 inches in Ashton.

A quick snowfall at the rate of 2 to 2.5 inches per hour fell in the Pocatello and Chubbuck areas with amounts as high as 7.5 inches in the benches surrounding the city. The snow began at 3 pm and amounts of 5 inches were measured by National Weather Service personnel in the cities of Pocatello and Chubbuck by 5:30 pm. As much as 7.5 inches of snow were measured in the benches by 6 pm. Less than 10 miles west of the city, only 1.5 inches fell at the Pocatello Regional Airport.

Very heavy snow fell in the Wood River Foothills the day before Thanksgiving.   the COOP observer in Bellevue recorded 12.5 inches of snow with several spotters in Hailey recording between 13 and 17 inches of snow.

The Ketchum Ranger Station recorded 9.5 inches of snow with 17 inches measured at Bald Mountain just southwest of the city at the Sun Valley Ski Resort.  SNOTEL amounts were:  16 inches at Dollarhide Summit  and 17 inches at Galena Summit.
The Vienna Mine SNOTEL recorded 21 inches of snowfall.
Snow amounts from the following SNOTEL sites occurred:  25 inches at Garfield Ranger Station and Smiley Mountain.   14 inches fell at Swede Peak.

Very heavy snow fell in the Arco-Mud Lake Desert region.    COOP observers reported 18 inches at Craters of the Moon National Monument and 9 inches 46 miles west of Idaho Falls.  A car hit a snow plow on route 28.
The Sedwick Peak SNOTEL recorded 11 inches of snow.
Heavy snow fell in the Bear River Range with 18 inches at Emigrant Summit and 24 inches at Franklin Basin.
Eleven inches of snow fell at Giveout, Slug Creek Divide, and Somsen Ranch.
Twelve inches of snow were reported in Kilgore.   20 inches fell at the Crab Creek SNOTEL and 12 inches fell at the White Elephant SNOTEL.
The Hilt's Creek SNOTEL reported 13 inches of snow.
The COOP observer in Preston recorded 10 inches of snow and the one in Malad City recorded 9 inches.

Interstate 15 closed down near the Blackfoot exit at around 7 pm . This was due to multiple weather related crashes which began around 445 pm.  A three vehicle crash shut down Yellowstone Avenue in Pocatello Friday morning.  Snow amounts of 2 to 4 inches were reported in the Lower Snake River Plain.

The Desert Ride Fire about 12 miles west of Rexburg began August 11th and was human caused. West winds of 15 to 20 mph caused the grass and brush fire to grow to 7,500 acres in the Menan Butte area and was caused by a man shooting a 22 caliber rifle at a firework on the ground causing it to ignite. The fire was contained on August 13th.

A fire began between 1 and 2 pm MDT due to sparks from a broken drive line on a vehicle and spread to both sides of US Highway 26. Highway 26 closed for a period of time due to the fire near mile marker 300. although strong winds drove the fire and threatened structures it was able to be contained with no damages.

Freezing drizzle caused a glaze on untreated roadways in the Idaho Falls area.   One collision occurred at the intersection of North Holmes and Hemmert Ave.  Two vehicles hit power poles.  Freezing drizzle reported in Ammon, Rigby, and Ucon as well.  Interstate 15 was reported icy from Shelley to Idaho Falls at 8 pm MST.
Ten inches of snow was reported by the public in Island Park with 12 inches estimated at the White Elephant SNOTEL site.
The following SNOTEL snow amounts were estimated:  Dollarhide Summit 10 inches, Galena 12 inches, Galena Summit 12 inches, Hyndman 9 inches, and Lost Wood Divide 16 inches.

Interstate 15 southbound shut down south of Blackfoot due to a crash and fire of a pickup pulling food truck.  Slippery roads were thought to be a factor.  Multiple crashes were reported on the morning of the 11th between Blackfoot and Pocatello.  Generally an inch or less of snow fell in the region but it still caused major travel issues.
SNOTEL snow estimates were 21 inches at Bostetter Ranger Station and 23 inches at Howell Canyon both above 7,500 feet.
Very heavy snow fell in the Bear River Range above 7,000 feet with SNOTEL estimates of 18 inches at Emigrant Summit and 17 inches at Franklin Basin.
The Pine Creek Pass SNOTEL estimated 18 inches of snowfall.
A total of 15 inches of snow was estimated at the Mill Creek Summit SNOTEL site.
A total of 25 inches of snow was estimated at the Vienna Mine SNOTEL site.
The following snow amounts were estimated at SNOTEL sites in the Sun Valley region:  Dollarhide Summit 17 inches, Galena 12 inches, and Galena Summit 12 inches.
A total of 6 inches of snow fell in Rupert with 8 inches reported in southwest Minidoka.

The heaviest snow thus far of the winter season fell in the Lower Snake River Plain with 5 inches at the Pocatello Regional airport, 5 inches in Chubbuck, 4 inches in Aberdeen, and 5 inches in American Falls.
Many slide offs were reported south of Pocatello between Pocatello and Downey in interstate 15. 3 inches fell in Downey and 5 inches in Inkom causing the very slick roads.

Heavy snowfall fell on New Year's Day.   Widespread amounts of 5 to 8 inches were recorded in the Upper Snake River Plain including 6 to 8 inches in Idaho Falls, 5 to 7 inches in Rexburg, 6 inches in Rigby, 7 inches in Menan.   The city of Idaho Falls enacted parking restrictions on New Year's Day to clear room for snow plows.

A strong Pacific storm and associated cold front brought very heavy snow to the Centennial Mountains and Island Park.   Trained spotters and COOP observers reported 10 inches in Island Park.   SNOTEL amounts were:  12 inches Crab Creek, 16 inches Island Park, and 19 inches White Elephant.
A strong Pacific storm brought 8 inches of snow to Chilly Barton Flat and 7 inches in Mackay.

A strong Pacific storm brought heavy snow to the Caribou Range.   The COOP observer in Swan Valley recorded 10 inches of snow.    SNOTEL amounts were 9 inches at Giveout, 8 inches at Slug Creek Divide, and 12 inches at Somsen Ranch.
Snow amounts were 8 inches at Bostetter Ranger Station and 11 inches at Howell Canyon.
Ten inches of snow fell at Emigrant Summit and 9 inches fell at Franklin Basin.
Sheep Mountain recorded 11 inches of snow.

A long lasting winter storm closed roads and schools and began late on the 10th and continued to the 15th.   Some of the snow amounts over the period were 30 inches at the Island Park COOP site, 33 inches 2 miles north of Macks Inn, an estimated 58 inches at the White Elephant SNOTEL site, and 32 inches at the Crab Creek SNOTEL.  Road closures from the 11th through the 14th were US Highway 20 was shut down from Ashton to the Montana state line, ID 47 was closed from Ashton to Bear Gulch, ID Highway 87 was closed from US 20 to the Montana state line.   Fremont County Schools were closed from the 11th through the 14th due to the extreme winter weather conditions and road closures.  The heavy snow combined with strong winds caused extensive blowing and drifting snow and was the main cause for the several day road closures.

Heavy snow combined with winds to cause extreme travel conditions across the region.  Craters of the Moon National Monument reported 16 inches of snow from the multi day storm and the snow combined with winds to cause Jefferson County School District to close on the 11th and 12th.

Heavy snow combined with winds to cause hazardous travel in the Bear Lake Valley.   The Bern COOP site reported 21.5 inches of snow with the storm including 13 inches on the 13th.   Bear Lake School District 33 was closed due to the hazardous travel on the 14th.   Montpelier received over a foot of snow on the 13th as well.
A multi day winter storm brought significant snowfall to the Bear River Range.   Estimated snow totals at SNOTEL sites were 28 inches at Emigrant Summit and 35 inches at Franklin Basin.

A powerful winter storm combined snow with strong winds to create extremely hazardous travel conditions.   Interstate 15 closed from Dubois north to the Montana border on the 12th through the 14th before reopening on the 14th.   Snowfall total at Dubois through the period was only 6 inches but the winds made snow removal nearly impossible for road crews.  The snowfall total at Small was 10 inches including 8 inches on the 11th.
A powerful winter storm brought heavy snow and very strong winds to the region.   A trained spotter 4 miles west of Victor recorded 17.5 inches of snow through the 13th with the storm.

A multi day powerful winter storm brought extremely heavy snow to the region.   Estimated SNOTEL amounts over the period were the following:  Bear Canyon 28 inches, Garfield Ranger Station 39 inches, Smiley Mountain 44 inches, Stickney Mill 23 inches, and Swede Peak 29 inches.

A long lasting winter storm dumped heavy snow and combined with high winds to make travel very difficult for nearly a week.   The COOP observer in Bone recorded 12 inches of snow including 8 inches on the 12th-14th.  An estimated 25 inches fell at the Sheep Mountain SNOTEL site.
A long lasting winter storm brought very heavy snow to the Caribou Range.   SNOTEL snow estimates were 21 inches at Giveout, 25 inches at Slug Creek Divide, and 18 inches at Somsen Ranch.
Very heavy snow fell during this long lasting Pacific storm.   31 inches fell at the Mill Creek Summit SNOTEL site.
Very heavy snow fell over an extended period of time in the Lost River Range.  The Hilts Creek SNOTEL snowfall estimate for the storm was 28 inches.

A prolonged winter storm with snow and strong winds affected the Lower Snake Plain from the 11th through the 15th.   Although snow amounts were not extreme, the combination of wind with the snow caused extremely hazardous travel conditions.   The following schools were closed on both the 13th and 14th:  Aberdeen district 58, Blackfoot district 55, Firth district 59, Shelley district 60, and Snake River district 52.   9 inches of snow fell in Aberdeen through the storm's duration with 5 inches in American Falls, and 4.5 inches in Pocatello.

A long lasting winter storm dropped heavy snow and very hazardous travel conditions to the Marsh and Arbon Highlands.  18 inches of snow fell in Inkom with 5 inches in Downey and 9 inches in McCammon.   The Sedgwick Peak SNOTEL received an estimated 21 inches and the Wildhorse Divide SNOTEL an estimated 22 inches.   The Marsh Valley School District 21 was closed on the 14th.

A long lasting winter storm brought extremely heavy snow to the region.   An incredible 78 inches of snow was estimated at the Vienna Mine SNOTEL site at 9 thousand feet.   The Stanley COOP site recorded 18 inches of snow.
A strong Pacific storm persisted for several days and the Richfield COOP observer recorded 12 inches of snow including 8 inches on the 13th and 14th.
The multi day storm system dropped an estimated 32 inches at the Bostetter Ranger Station SNOTEL  and an estimated 41 inches at the Howell Canyon SNOTEL.

A multi day snow storm brought 13 inches of snow to Ketchum with the following estimated SNOTEL amounts:  Chocolate Gulch 36 inches, Dollarhide Summit 39 inches, Galena 31 inches, Galena Summit 40 inches, Hyndman 20 inches, and Lost Wood Divide 33 inches.

A multiple day winter storm with heavy snow and high winds shut down many roads in the Teton Valley.   12 to 20 inches fell in the Victor area for the duration of the storm.   Strong winds caused extensive blowing and drifting snow on roadways and made them impossible to clear.  Idaho 32 closed from Tetonia to Ashton on the 11th through the 14th.  Idaho 33 closed from Tetonia and Newdale.   US 20 closed from Ashton to the Montana border.  Fremont County School District 215, Madison School district 321, and Teton School District 401 were closed from the 13th through the 15th.

A multi day storm brought heavy snow and strong winds which shut down schools and roads in the Upper Snake River Plain.   Storm  total snowfall for the duration were 11 inches at Idaho Falls, 9.5 inches at Sugar City and Rigby, and 5 inches at Saint Anthony.  Interstate 15 shut down between Idaho Falls and Roberts on the 12th through the 14th due to the very strong winds causing extensive blowing and drifting snow .  School closures on the 13th through the 15th were Bonneville Joint District 93, Idaho Falls District 91, Jefferson District 251, Madison District 321, Ririe District 252, Sugar-Salem District 322, West Jefferson District 253.
Extremely heavy snowfall occurred in this long duration winter storm with Hailey, Picabo, and Bellevue all receiving between 15 and 22 inches of snow through the storm.
An avalanche in the Baker Creek area in Blaine County killed a 50 year old man of Jerome Idaho.   Two snowmobliers were caught in the avalanche at about 9,000 feet in elevation and only one survived.

A fast moving cold front brought snow and high winds to the Raft River Region.   Interstate 84 was closed from 11 miles east of Heyburn to the Utah border due to the 1 to 4 inch snowfall and wind gusts of 50-60 mph making it impassable.  It re-opened at 2 pm.   Idaho route 81 was closed from Malta to the Cotterell port of entry due to the high winds and Idaho 77 was closed from Malta to Albion due to the winds as well.   Visibility was reduced to zero for much of the morning .

A strong cold front brought only 1 to 3 inches of snow but combined with wind gusts up to 60 mph made travel extremely hazardous.   Idaho Route 77 from Malta to Albion closed due to the drifting snow and zero visibility.

A strong cold front moved through the Upper Snake River Plain with high winds and light snow making travel extremely hazardous.   Snow amounts generally only ranged from a half inch to 3 inches but combined with 40 to 50 mph wind gusts made snow removal difficult.   Idaho Route 33 closed from Newdale to Tetonia and US Highway 26 was closed from Ririe to Swan Valley.   The following schools were closed on the 17th:  Bonneville Joint District 93, Idaho Falls District 91, and Jefferson District 251.

A strong cold front moved through the Magic Valley and produced light snow with high winds causing hazardous travel conditions.   Snow amounts in the Eastern Magic Valley generally ranged from 2 to 4 inches with 3 inches reported in Heyburn.  Interstate 84 was closed for much of the day from 11 miles east of Heyburn to the Utah border due to the wind gusts causing zero visibility and significant drifting snow.

A strong cold front brought light snow but included very strong winds which created very hazardous travel.   Snow amounts were widespread in the 1 to 3 inch range with extensive blowing and drifting snow.   The following schools closed on the 17th:  Aberdeen District 58, American Falls District 381, and Blackfoot District 55.  It was a scheduled day off for Pocatello District 25 but the following private schools closed in Pocatello:  Connor Academy, Gem Prep, and Pocatello Community Charter School.

A strong cold front brought light snow and high winds to the Teton Valley.   Snow amounts were light in the 1 to 3 inch range but strong winds again brought extensive blowing and drifting snow which caused road and school closures.   Idaho Highway 47 was closed from Ashton to Warm River and Idaho Highway 32 was also closed from Ashton to Tetonia.  Ashton Elementary School and North Fremont Junior and Senior High  Schools in Ashton were also closed.  The town of Driggs was completely isolated for a short period on the 17th with no open roads in or out of the city.

Due to it's unique valley location, Challis rarely sees heavy snowfall, but this latest Pacific Storm system brought the heaviest snowfall in the region to Challis.   Spotters reported 7 inches of snow fell in the city on the 26th and overnight into the 27th which was by far the most reported in the region with the storm.

It is believed a month of heavy snow loading caused the collapse of a vacant building at 1017 Washington St in Montpelier at around 4 pm on January 28th.   No one was in the building and no injuries occurred.

Snow and wind closed US Highway 20 to the US 26 intersection at the Idaho National Lab site.  Craters of the Moon National Monument recorded 6 inches of snow and the West Jefferson School District 253 closed on February 3rd.
Bern and St Charles recorded 5 inches of snow and combined with wind gusts up to 40 mph caused the Bear Lake School District 61 to close on February 3rd.

Snow and strong winds combined to close Interstate 15 from Dubois north to the Montana border.   Although snow was not heavy, 4 inches fell 6 miles north of Small and 2 inches fell in Dubois winds gusted to 50 mph causing very dangerous travel.   Clark County School District 161 closed on February 3rd due to the wind and snow.

Only 2 to 4 inches of snow fell but wind gusts of 40 to 50 mph caused extensive blowing snow.  Because of travel concerns the Grace School District 148, the North Gem School District 149 and Soda Springs School District 150 were all closed on February 3rd.
Strong winds and snow with gusts up to 40 mph caused extremely hazardous travel.   The Somsen Ranch SNOTEL estimated 9 inches of snow and the Slug Creek Divide SNOTEL measured 6 inches of snow.

Snow and strong wind gusts caused extremely hazardous travel and the Fremont County School District 215 was closed on February 3rd.   Island Park received 4 inches of snow and the White Elephant SNOTEL site received 17 inches of snow.

Interstate 84 was closed from the Interstate 86 intersection to the Utah border.  Snow was not heavy with Minidoka Dam receiving 3 inches but wind gusts of 30 to 40 mph caused extensive blowing and drifting snow.
The Butte County School District 111 shut down on February 3rd due to snow and very strong winds causing hazardous travel conditions  The Hilt's Creek SNOTEL had a 6 inch snow estimate.

Snow and very strong winds caused very difficult driving conditions and the Butte County School District 111 closed on February 3rd as did the Mackay School District 182.   Chilly Barton Flat received 5.4 inches of snow with 2 inches at the Mackay Ranger Station.   Wind gusts of 40 to 50 mph caused the extensive blowing snow.

Very heavy snow in the Pocatello/Chubbuck region fell and combined with high winds caused Pocatello Chubbuck School District 25 to be closed on February 3rd.   A variety of spotters/NWS employees and COOP observers recorded 6 to 9 inches of snowfall in the Pocatello and Chubbuck region.   American Falls recorded 6 inches of snow and Aberdeen 5.5 inches.   Other school closures on the 3rd were:  Firth School District 59, Aberdeen School District 58, Shelley School District 60, and American Falls School District 381.
The Pebble Creek ski resort reported 16 inches of snow with the city of Inkom 6 inches.  The North Gem School District 149 closed on February 3rd due to the hazardous travel.

Snow and very high winds caused the closing of interstate 84 from the intersection of interstate 86 all the way to the Utah border.   Wind gusts of 50 to 60 mph caused the strong wind gusts that closed the interstate and also the closing of Rockland School District 382 on February 3rd.  .
The Pomerelle ski resort reported 11 inches of snow and wind gusts as high as 49 mph were recorded in the Albion Mountains.

Snow and wind caused extensive travel problems in the Teton Valley and all roads to the north were shut down.    Idaho Route 33 from Newdale to Tetonia was shut down.   Idaho Route 32 from Ashton to Tetonia shut down and Idaho 47 east of Ashton closed.   Snow amounts were not heavy and accumulated 2 to 4 inches but wind gusts of 40 to 50 mph and blowing and drifting snow made roads unpassable.

A strong cold front produced 1 to 4 inches of snow with 40 to 50 mph wind gusts to cause extremely hazardous travel weather.   US Highway 20 was closed from Idaho Falls to INL and US Route 26 intersection and Idaho 33 was closed from Newdale to Tetonia.   The following schools closed on  February 3rd:  Sugar-Salem School District 322, Idaho Falls School District 91, Madison School District 321, Ririe School District 252, and Jefferson School District 251.
An avalanche closed US Route 89 from Montepelier to Geneva on the afternoon of the 6th to remove snow.

During the day on the 5th 2 to 4 inches of snow fell then overnight on the 5th into the morning hours on the 6th a quarter inch of freezing rain accumulated at the Pocatello Regional Airport.   Several traffic accidents and slide offs were reported both days.  Blackfoot School District 55 closed on the 6th as did Sho-Ban High School and Bingham Academy District 485.
Four to 6 inches of snow fell and an avalanche caused the closing of US 89 from Montpelier to Geneva on the 6th.
Very heavy snow fell in the Bear River Range with SNOTEL estimates of 25 inches at Emigrant Summit and 28 inches at Franklin Basin in the 7 thousand foot to 8,200 foot elevation range.
Six inches of snow was reported in Dubois and Small with the storm.
Very heavy snow fell in the Big Hole's with an estimated 18 inches at Pine Creek Pass which webcams indicated a long period of snow covered roads along US Route 30 through the period.
Nine inches of snow was recorded at the COOP site  in Bone and was estimated at the Sheep Mountain SNOTEL site.  The North Gem School District 149 was closed due to travel conditions on the 6th.

Very heavy snowfall occurred and caused very hazardous travel.   An accident caused US Highway 26 to close for a period of time from Swan Valley to the Wyoming border.   16 inches of snow fell at the Swan Valley COOP site with the following SNOTEL estimates:  Giveout 17 inches, Slug Creek Divide 22 inches, and 15 inches in Somsen Ranch.

Very heavy snow once again fell in the Centennial Mountains with 13 inches reported by the Island Park COOP site.   SNOTEL estimates were:  16 inches at Island Park, 18 inches at Crab Creek, and 21 inches at White Elephant.

Heavy snow caused very difficult travel especially overnight on the 5th and the morning of the 6th.   The Oneida School District 351 closed on the 6th due to the conditions.   Snow amounts reported by COOP sites were:  5 inches at Malad City, and 5 inches at Preston.   The Oxford Springs SNOTEL estimated 11 inches of snow.

Heavy snow fell in the Marsh and Arbon Highlands disrupting travel.   17 inches of snow fell in Inkom in the storm Other amounts were:  7 inches in Downey, 8 inches in McCammon, an estimated 19 inches at the Sedgwick Peak SNOTEL and 7 inches at Wildhorse Divide.  The Marsh Valley School District 21 was closed on the 6th due to the hazardous travel and North Gem District 149 was also closed.
Very heavy snow fell in the Southern Hills.   Amounts estimated at SNOTEL sites were Bostetter Ranger Station 18 inches and Howell Canyon 16 inches.
The Vienna Mine SNOTEL estimated 17 inches of snow.
Eight to 12 inches of snow fell in the Teton Valley with 9 inches reported by the COOP observer in Ashton.

Another round of snow brought hazardous travel conditions to the Upper Snake River Plain again.   Amounts for the storm were:  4 inches Idaho Falls, 5 inches Menan, 6 inches Rexburg, 6 inches Rigby, and 11 inches at Saint Anthony and Sugar City.
Idaho Route 34 closed from Soda Springs to the Wyoming border due to 30 to 40 mph wind gusts.
Idaho Route 32 was closed from Tetonia to Ashton and Idaho Route 33 was closed from Newdale to Tetonia due to strong wind gusts of 30 to 40 mph causing extensive blowing and drifting snow.
Idaho route 33 was closed from Newdale to Tetonia due to wind gusts of 30 to 40 mph causing extensive blowing and drifting snow.
Idaho Route 34 was closed from Soda Springs to the Wyoming border due to 30 to 40 mph wind gusts causing extensive blowing and drifting snow making snow removal difficult.

Heavy snow fell with wind gusts in the 30 to 40 mph range.   US Highway 26 was blocked due to a tractor trailer jack-knifing 5 miles east of Irwin.   Highway travel became very difficult.   Swan Valley COOP site reported 10 inches of snow.  Idaho Route 34 was also closed from Soda Springs to the Wyoming border due to snow and wind.

Heavy snow fell over the extended weekend with 9 inches reported by the COOP observer in Inkom.   Travel was most hazardous on the evening of the 17th as many roads refroze with many slideoffs and accidents reported on interstate 15 from Fort Hall to McCammon and on US Route 30 from McCammon east to Georgetown.
Snow was not heavy with 1 to 3 inches falling but combined with 30 to 40 mph wind gusts closed Idaho Highway 32 again between Ashton and Tetonia by the afternoon of the 16th.

Heavy snow and strong winds caused hazardous travel.   Pine Creek Pass recorded 7.4 inches of snow overnight on the 15th into the 16th with more through the day.   Idaho Route 33 closed east of Victor to the Wyoming border due to the avalanche threat caused by the heavy snowfall in strong winds.

Idaho route 34 was closed by the afternoon of the 16th from just north of Soda Springs to the Wyoming border.   Snowfall and snow melt and re-freezing caused very hazardous travel on the evening of the 17th with several slide offs reported on US Route 30 from McCammon to Georgetown.   Snowfall amounts were generally in the 3 to 7 inch range.

Very light snow freezing at sunset caused very hazardous travel on interstate 15 from Blackoot to McCammon during the evening of the 17th with several slide offs reported.  One five car slide off was reported between Fort Hall and Pocatello.

A 300 yard avalanche which was 6 to 7 feet caused the death of a man at Pebble Creek Ski Resort on March 15th.   He was skiing at an out-of-bounds run near the north boundary of the ski area when he was trapped under snow without a beacon to aid ski patrol.   The avalanche was believed to be caused by heavy, wet snow at high elevations of the ski resort.
Heavy snow fell above 7500 feet with 16 inches estimated at the White Elephant SNOTEL. Under 4 inches fell at elevations under 6500 feet.
The Franklin Basin SNOTEL estimated 13 inches of snow with the storm.
The Mill Creek Summit SNOTEL estimated 20 inches of snow fell during the storm.
The Mill Creek Summit SNOTEL estimated 28 inches of snowfall during the storm.  Nearly 8 inches of snow fell at the Stanley COOP site.

The forest service reported 13 inches of snow 5 miles west northwest of Galena.  SNOTEL snowfall estimates during the storm were the following:   Dollarhide Summit 18 inches, Galena 11 inches, Galena Summit 14 inches, and Lost Wood Divide 14 inches.
Twelve inches of snow was estimated at the Bear Canyon SNOTEL with 20 inches at Smiley Mountain.

Dense fog was determined the cause of a child rear ending the child's mother in a two car collision causing extensive damage.   No injuries occurred with the accident occurring on Idaho Highway 33 near mile marker 45.  The accident occurred around 7 am MDT.
A 28 year old man was killed snowboarding in a back country avalanche near Taylor Mountain and Teton Pass during the afternoon of April 1st.   His rescue beacon was turned off.

A 46 year old back country snowmobiler was killed in an avalanche during the afternoon of April 3rd.   It occurred in the Austin Canyon area north of Mount Baird and Palisades Reservoir.  The individual was wearing a rescue beacon but it was not activated.
Pine trees were snapped with shingles blown off a home.   Occurred just north of Roberts.
A lightning strike to a power pole left 3,300 customers without power in Idaho Falls, Menan, Lewisville, Roberts, and Rigby.
Six foot by 8 foot section of shingles were blown off a roof.
A 1 foot in diameter tree was uprooted and damaged a fence and outbuilding.
A sheet metal roof on and outbuilding was blown off with wood built walls collapsing near N 3700 E just north of E 400 N between Rigby and Lewisville.
A tree was blown down onto a shed also taking down power lines near Rigby.
Three trees were reported downed at Rigby Community Presbyterian Church at N State Street and W 1st Street.   No damage to the church was reported.

Thunderstorm winds caused major damage to vehicles at Tadd Jenkins Chevrolet in Rigby.  Thunderstorm driven winds picked up rocks and shattered the windows on 15 vehicles with 20 to 30 other vehicles with other rock damage caused by the winds.  Damage was estimated near 15,000 dollars.
Wooden stockade fences were blown over in Ririe.
A pine tree was snapped off near it's base 1 mile southeast of RIrie.  Tree limbs and fences also torn down along 2nd St West but no major damage reported.

Interstate 86 closed interstate 86 for an 8 mile stretch from the Seagull Bay exit and the Arbon Valley exit between the Pocatello airport and American Falls.  The interstate closed from 1230 PM MDT until 9 PM MDT.  Numerous traffic accidents caused a pileup.   Visibility was zero in blowing dust in 45 to 55 mph wind gusts which likely caused the accidents.   Several personal vehicles and semi trucks were involved.   Several injuries occurred and many individuals were transported to hospitals.   No deaths occurred.   One semi was carrying a load of fertilizer and this spilled.   Hazmat crews were called in to respond to the chemical spill.
Lost River Rest Area recorded 66 mph wind gust.
A 65 mph wind gust measured at Radioactive Waste Management site at INL.
Arco mesonet site recorded 58 mph wind gust.
Sixty mph wind gust estimated by spotter.
Seventy mph wind gust at Atomic City.
A 69 mph wind gust  at Rover mesonet site.
A 65 mph wind gust measured at the base of Howe Peak.
A 64 mph gust at Reactor Technologies Complex at INL.
A 63 mph wind gust measured at Telegraph Hill.
A 62 mph gust measured at Terreton mesonet site.
A 62 mph wind gust measured at Materials Fuels complex at INL.
A wind gust of 61 mph measured at Specific Manufacturing Capability at INL.
A 61 mph gust measured at Sand Dunes.
A 60 mph wind gust measured 6 miles northwest of Atomic City.
A 58 mph gust measured at Potter Butte.
A 63 mph gust measured at Botts mesonet station.
A funnel cloud photographed in Samaria.

A large tree fell on the hood of a car on Main Street in downtown Hailey near the northwest corner of Silver Street.   It fell on the hood of a car and closed main street for about 60 minutes as crews worked on removal.
A 57 mph wind gust measured at Tom Cat Summit.

Interstate 15 closed due to blowing dust at 2:30 PM MDT on May 3rd from milepost 119 to milepost 135 between Idaho Falls and Roberts.   Sustained winds of 25 to 35 mph with gusts of 35 to 45 mph caused visibility to near zero in that stretch as dust from freshly plowed fields affected that stretch of interstate.  The interstate re-opened early in the evening.
Between 2 and 4 pm MDT several mesonet sites in the Arco and Mud Lake desert region recorded wind gusts over 60 mph with the highest reaching 74 mph at the Telegraph Hill site.

Wind gusts reached 68 mph in Roberts with widespread 50 to 70 mph gusts.   Interstate 15 closed at 1:58 PM MDT from Idaho Falls to Roberts between exit 118 and exit 143 due to blowing dust and zero visibility.   Four miles south of Lewisville a downed power line was reported with a tree blocking the road near 3431 E and 100 N near the Grant Church.  Power poles were reported arcing in Ririe.  Three miles west of Egin a tree fell on a house with power lines wrapped in the tree.  A semi-trailer was blown over on Idaho Route 33 near Teton.   Idaho Route 33 shut down from Newdale to Tetonia due to zero visibility and blowing dust.  Power lines were downed in Parker at 133 East Main.   A tree was downed at 205 West Main in Saint Anthony.  1200 customers lost their power in the event.

Interstate 86 closed between milepost 40 and milepost 52 east of American Falls at 1:54 PM due to zero visibility in blowing dust.  Winds gusted between 50 and 60 mph from noon to 7 pm.   Two accidents occurred on the interstate within the closed area.
Widespread wind gusts of 50 to 60 mph occurred and Idaho Highway 27 was closed due to zero visibility caused by blowing dust from Burley to Oakley.

A wind gust of 70 mph was measured near Clementsville.   Idaho Highway 32 was shut down from Tetonia to Ashton and Idaho Highway 33 was shut down from Newdale to Tetonia due to blowing dust and zero visibility.   Both were shut down around 4:30 PM MDT.
Multiple wind gusts of 65 to 70 mph were measured on interstate 15 one mile south of Dubois.
Portions of a 2 by 4 storage shed had sheet metal and wood blown across a yard 1 mile east of Carey.

Three trees along with power lines were downed across Little Wood Reservoir Road just north of Carey.   It was very near N Main St or US Highway 20.  700 customers were without power in the towns of Carey, Picabo, and Gannett.
A 61 mph wind gust measured just south of Fort Hall.
A 61 mph wind gust at Atomic City.
A 70 mph gust measured at Kettle Butte site.
A 74 mph wind gust measured at Deadman Canyon.
A 57 mph wind gust at Moburg Canyon.
A 57 mph wind gust measured at Cotton Ridge RAWS site.
An 83 mph wind gust measured at the Camas ITD site.
A 61 mph gust measured at Challis ASOS.
A 64 mph wind gust reported in Hamer.
A 64 mph wind gust reported in Terreton.
A 58 mph wind reported in Roberts.
A 71 mph gust measured 4 miles north of Holbrook.   Some tin on tops of silos blown off haystacks and some boat damage reported.
A 57 mph wind gust measured at the Juniper interchange ITD site.
A 60 mph wind gust measured at the Pine Creek Pass ITD site.

Idaho Power reported 38 downed power poles from thunderstorm winds.   It occurred along 1700 S between 1800 W and 3100 W about 3 miles west of Aberdeen.  About 2,000 customers lost power and as of 12 PM MDT on May 31st about 800 customers were still without power.
Large tree limbs downed in Stone with shingles removed from one home.
Trees downed 7 miles northwest of Holbrook from thunderstorm winds.

At least 14 power poles snapped off at various heights along road 009 and attendant power lines were down across road 009 and across Idaho Highway 38.  Highway 38 was closed for a 2 mile stretch until the lines were removed.
Multiple trees and large tree limbs down along S 5400 W between W 3000 S and W 500 S.
Between the towns of Pleasantview and Malad City numerous trees were uprooted with one damaging a house and multiple power lines damaged and down.
A tree and power lines were down on a house.   Large sections of sheet metal were blown out or peeled off of 2 large barn structures in the area of the intersection of S 5400 W and W 500 S.
Multiple trees were down including on a house along N 3100 W.
Two large trees were uprooted, one of which partially fell on a pickup truck along 5600 W just west of N 5400 W.  Trees and tree limbs were down across the area.

Widespread wind damage occurred across the valley west of Malad City with a total of at least 40 trees down from the Pleasantview area and Idaho Highway 38 at southern end, to the west side of Malad City at the eastern extent, to 2800 N at the northern extent.  Damage was noted at nearly every property.   Maximum winds were estimated at 75 to 90 mph based on observed damage.  Multiple homes had roof shingles blown off with wagon wheel irrigation systems blown around and damaged usually be wrapping against trees or power poles.
A portion of a well built shingled roof blown off a 2 story residence along W 1000 N west of N 3400 W.  Tree limbs were downed as well.

N 3400 W was closed by law enforcement from W 2000 N south to W 1000 N due to multiple trees, tree limbs, and power lines down blocking the road at various locations.   Several power poses were damaged or leaning.  A large tree was uprooted and down on a house along W 2000 N between N 3400 W and 3100 W along with a power line.  Numerous trees and tree limbs down across the area with tree debris covering several roads.  Tree branches were hanging from power lines.
A roof was blown off a large outbuilding along W 2800 N between N 3900 W and 3100 W.
The upper half of a large pine tree snapped off along N 500 W south of 8th st N.
Numerous large trees were downed across Malad City.
A large tree over 2 feet in diameter snapped off just above the base near the intersection of Center St and Main St.  Additional large tree limbs were down throughout Rockland.
Multiple large trees down along Wildcat Rd.   An irrigation pivot overturned and was damaged.
The Kettle Butte site recorded a 58 mph wind gust.
The Rover station recorded a 63 mph wind gust.
Large tree limbs were down and minor damage to sheet metal roofs on 2 barns along N 2800 E.
A tree was downed on Highland St near S 3rd St.  Highland St was partially blocked.
The Fall River site recorded a 58 mph wind gust.
The Terreton mesonet site recorded a 58 mph wind gust.
The Hamer site recorded a 58 mph wind gust.
The Camas site recorded a 63 mph wind gust.
Numerous trees were reported down mainly in and around Ashton.
Thunderstorm winds removed a sheet metal roof from an outbuilding and dropped it onto another building nearby.

The Howe Peak fire approximately 4 miles southwest of Howe began on July 2nd around 1 pm  MDT and was human caused.   It was along Highway 33 and burned grass, shrubs, and juniper in steep terrain.   No structures were threatened other than right at the start of the fire and no evacuations occurred other than voluntary in Howe initially.   The power in the town of Howe was out.  140 firefighters were used and the fire reached 7,300 acres.   17 power line poles were damaged.   Idaho Highway 33 closed for a short time on the 2nd between Butte City and Howe.  The fire was contained by July 7th.

The Howe Peak fire approximately 4 miles southwest of Howe began on July 2nd around 1 pm  MDT and was human caused.   It was along Highway 33 and burned grass, shrubs, and juniper in steep terrain.   No structures were threatened other than right at the start of the fire and no evacuations occurred other than voluntary in Howe initially.   The power in the town of Howe was out.  140 firefighters were used and the fire reached 7,300 acres.   17 power line poles were damaged.   Idaho Highway 33 closed for a short time on the 2nd between Butte City and Howe.  The fire was contained by July 7th.

The Chinese Peak fire began 1 mile south of Pocatello on July 19th and was 100 percent contained by July 21st.   The fire was human caused by sparks from a grinder landing in dry grass near Sparkman Road.   The fire burned 1,546 acres of grass, brush and juniper.   It began at 3 pm MDT on July 19th.   No structures were threatened and no evacuations occurred.   Some road closures were in effect on the 19th along Barton Road to Chinese Peak.

The Chinese Peak fire began 1 mile south of Pocatello on July 19th and was 100 percent contained by July 21st.   The fire was human caused by sparks from a grinder landing in dry grass near Sparkman Road.   The fire burned 1,546 acres of grass, brush and juniper.   It began at 3 pm MDT on July 19th.   No structures were threatened and no evacuations occurred.   Some road closures were in effect on the 19th along Barton Road to Chinese Peak.
Lightning caused a 371 acre fire 6 miles southwest of Malad City.   It began on July 25th and was contained by July 27th.  No structures were threatened in the uninhabited fire area.
A 57 mph wind gust measured at the Blue Dome Mesonet site.
A 62 mph wind gust measured at the Kettle Butte mesonet site.
A 60 mph gust measured on Bald Mountain.
Two trees downed including one on top of building at Idaho Falls Country Club.
A 68 mph wind gust measured at the Richfield mesonet site.
A tree was downed at a residence causing some shingle damage.
Two trees were downed at a Burley area golf course.
A 60 mph wind gust measured at the KSUN Hailey Airport.
Several trees were reported down in the town of Bellevue.  Occurred on 5th and 8th Streets as well as Tendoy Street just north of Bellevue.
Three funnel clouds were spotted near Neely by sheriffs deputy.

At least three boats were reported capsized due to winds caused by a thunderstorm on Palisades Reservoir on August 1st. Times are estimated and the exact wind speeds are unknown but a significant event to document.

A 1,500 acre fire occurred at the Idaho National Laboratory Site on August 6th   No structures were threatened and it began near mile marker 259 adjacent to the rest area on US Highway 26 and about 1 mile northeast of the Radioactive Waste Management Complex.   Seven fire trucks and 4 bulldozers from both INL and the BLM responded to the fire.   It was contained by the afternoon of August 6th.
The Muldoon wildfire began August 16th and burned 374 acres of timber about 20 miles southwest of Mackay.    It was fully contained by August 25th and threatened no structures.  Cause was unknown.

The Michaud Creek fire  began August 18th only 3 miles south of the Pocatello airport and burned 72 acres.  It burned grass, brush and torching juniper.   Bureau of Indian Affairs, Bureau of Land Management, and Caribou-Targhee were rapid in their response and prevented significant spread.  No structures were threatened.   Several local roads were closed to prevent the fire spread.

The Black Pine Fire was a lightning induced fire on August 18th that burned 1,000 acres 6 miles north of the Utah border near interstate 84 mile marker 270.   It burned grass, brush and juniper and spread very rapidly.   It was finally contained on August 21st.

A severe thunderstorm snapped football stadium light poles at the base at Butte County High School in Arco.  Broken tree branches were widespread in Arco and many power outages occurred in rural Butte County.

It is believed lightning struck transformers  creating sparks that caused two fires in Pocatello.   The first occurred in a field outside the School District 25 main office building on Pole Line Road.  A second fire occurred at the 500 block of North Ninth Avenue.  Sparks from a transformer ignited a grass fire that destroyed a car and spread to the exterior of a house destroying the attic.   The home was unoccupied and was declared salvageable.  About 1,000 Pocatello residents also lost power.

Lightning caused the Black Sand Fire near the St Anthony Sand Dunes,  It burned 129 acres but firefighters stopped the spread rapidly.   It began around 6 pm on August 28th and was contained on August 29th.
The Miner Creek fire burned 400 acres about 20 miles east of Blackfoot.   It was caused by lightning around 5 pm on August 25th.  It was quickly contained.
The Rye Grass fire was started by a lightning strike on August 25th and burned 150 acres about 8 miles northeast of the American Falls Reservoir.  Spread was stopped quickly.

A SUV pulling a camper/trailer overturned on interstate 15 south of Malad Summit due to high crosswinds.   The two passengers suffered minor injuries.  A 52 mph wind speed was measured 4 miles east southeast of Weston at 7:49 PM MDT.  A metal roof was blown off a hay barn in Clifton at around 745 pm MDT.

A powerful cold front brought damaging winds to the Arco-Mud Lake Desert region. The Badger Fire began on September 12th at around 5 pm MDT and continued through the rest of September.   It grew to near 90,000 acres and was located 20 miles southwest of Oakley.   High winds and extremely dry fuels caused rapid spread including long range spotting and fire whirls.   There was an evacuation order for all residents on private land in Rock Creek Canyon and Dry Creek on the 18th but was lifted on 8 AM on Sunday, September 20th.  The Sawtooth National Forest issued the Badger Fire Road, Trail and Area closure on September 15th.   Drones were prohibited over the area.   Main fuels were timber (litter and understory), heavy logging slash, sub-alpine fir, lodgepole pine, juniper, mountain brush and grass.  The fire was around 85 percent contained by the end of September.

The high temperature at the Pocatello Regional Airport on September 5th was 100 degrees.  This was the first 100 degree temperature ever recorded in September and broke the old hottest temperature record for the month of 98 degrees set in 2017.
The high temperatures reached 97 degrees at Idaho Falls Regional Airport on September 5th.   This tied the previous record for hottest September temperature ever set in 1950.
The high temperatures of 98 degrees at the Burley Airport on September 5th was the hottest September temperature ever recorded in the city.   It broke the previous record of 97 set in 1998.

The high temperature of 98 degrees in Challis on September 5th was the hottest September temperature ever recorded in the city breaking the previous hottest temperature of 96 degrees set the day before.

The Trap Creek fire began September 14th and burned over 2,000 acres located 9 miles northwest of Stanley near the Trap Creek Campground in the Sawtooth National Recreation Area.  The fire jumped Highway 21 and necessitated a closure of the road between Grandjean and Cape Horn Roads for a period of time.  The fire engulfed lodgepole pines in flames and caused them to fall on the road.   A forest area closure was put into effect and included Valley Creek Road by September 19th.    The fire was 41 percent contained by the end of the month but 100 percent contained along Idaho Highway 21.
