Eight inches of heavy, wet snow fell in Ashton and Fall River Rural Electric reported thousands of customers with power outages on March 20th due to the snow weight.

The Island Park COOP observer recorded 9.4 inches of snow.   5 inches fell in Marysville.  Fall River Rural Electric reported thousands of customers in Fremont County without power on March 20th due to the heavy snow on power lines.  The White Elephant and Island Park SNOTEL sites recorded an estimated 8 inches.

Six inches of snow fell in Sugar City and 6 inches fell in Saint Anthony.  2 inches fell in Idaho Falls.   The very heavy and wet snow caused power outages to nearly 2,000 customers in the Idaho Falls area on March 20th.
Seventy to 80 mph wind gusts were common across the Arco Desert in the Atomic City to Craters of the Moon corridor.
Fifty to 60 mph wind gusts were widespread with a peak gust of 60 mph near Alton.
Widespread wind gusts of 50 to 60 mph occurred on teh 20th with a peak gust of 60 mph in southwest Clark County.
Widespread wind gusts of 50 to 60 mph occurred with a peak of 63 mph near Palisades on US Highway 26.
Widespread wind gusts of 50 to 60 mph occurred on the 20th with a peak of 60 mph near Lund.   Rocky Mountain Power reported 429 customers without power in the Grace, Niter and Thatcher areas.

Widespread 50 to 60 mph wind gusts caused blowing and drifting snow and closed US Highway 20 from Ashton to the Montana border and closed Idaho route 87 from US 20 to Raynolds Pass.   Rocky Mountain Electric reported multiple power outages in the Island Park area.
A wind gust of 65 mph was recorded just north of Challis.
Sixty to 70 mph wind gusts were widespread with a peak gust of 66 mph near Minidoka.  United Electric CO-OP reported a power outage west of Paul and Heyburn.
Several high profile vehicles were blown over on interstate 15 near Malad Summit including a semi tractor trailer.  Interstate 15 north bound was closed near mile marker 28.
Widespread 55 to 65 mph wind gusts occurred with a power outage reported in the Howe area by Rocky Mountain Power.

Power lines were downed over interstate 15 near Blackfoot and both north and south bound were closed the morning of the 20th.   Power outages caused the following schools to close:  Bingham Academy 485, Blackfoot School District 55, Idaho Science and Tech Charter School, Blackfoot Charter Comm Learning Center, Chief Targhee elementary Academy, and ShoBan High School.   Several downed trees were reported across roadways with the 50 to 60 mph wind gusts very widespread.
Widespread 60 to 75 mph gusts occurred along interstate 84 southeast of Burley.  The highest recorded was 75 mph at the Idaho Transportation  Department Yale site.
Fifty to 60 mph wind gusts were widespread with the highest gust 60 mph at Almo.
Strong winds occurred throughout the early morning into the afternoon on the 20th.  The peak gust was 63 mph 4 miles west of Galena.
Sixty to 70 mph gusts occurred with the highest recorded 66 mph at the Idaho Transportation Department site near Clementsville.

Widespread 60 to 70 mph winds caused power lines to be downed with several large trees uprooted across roads.   Rocky Mountain Power reported over 14,000 customers without power in Rexburg, Shelley, Ammon, Iona, Idaho Falls, and Ririe.   The Idaho Falls airport recorded a 61 mph gust and the Idaho Transportation Department site in Poplar recorded a 67 mph gust.
Two to 4 inches of snow fell in the Pocatello, Blackfoot, and Fort Hall areas with several minor traffic accidents and slide offs.

Two to 4 inches of snow fell in the Idaho Falls and Rigby area and several slide offs occurred on interstate 15.  One of the slide offs resulted in an unfortunate indirect accident.   An indirect death occurred on interstate 15 in Idaho Falls when a car slid off the highway into the median and a pedestrian walking across the highway was hit and killed by a pickup truck.

A 72 mph wind gust was measured 6 miles northwest of Atomic City at the ITD RWIS weather station at the INL Puzzle site.  Several gusts of over 60 mph were recorded including 69 mph at Craters of the Moon and 67 mph at Rover.

A peak wind gust of 68 mph was measured at the Idaho Falls Airport ASOS site.  Interstate 15 was closed in both directions from Idaho Falls/US 20 north to Idaho route 33 due to zero visibility in blowing dust.  A sheet metal shed was destroyed and blown into a road in Ammon . A large tree was uprooted in Rigby.  An Idaho Falls business had part of their roof peeled off.  The Idaho Falls fire department reported a tree down on their station near the intersection of 8th St and S Holmes.  A power pole was snapped off north of Osgood blocking W 113th north . A sports field light pole snapped off at Sandcreek Middle School in Ammon . A large pine tree was uprooted crushing a pickup truck in Idaho Falls.  A power pole was snapped off in Rexburg.
A 62 mph wind gust was recorded at the Dead Man Canyon mesonet site.

The Pocatello ASOS recorded a wind gust of 62 mph.   Other sites also recorded over 60 mph.  Interstate 15 near Fort Hall had reduced visibility due to blowing dust and a semi tractor trailer blew over.   A large highway sign also blew over near Blackfoot.   Idaho route 39 had zero visibility between Aberdeen and American Falls around 530 PM.

A strong cold front brought wind gusts as high as 74 mph to the Arco Desert.  Craters of the Moon mesonet recorded 74 mph as well as the Rover site.   At least 20 mesonet sites recorded over 60 mph gusts through the day .

The Roberts mesonet site recorded a 68 mph wind gust.   The Idaho Falls ASOS recorded a 66 mph gust.   Interstate 15 closed by noon from US 20 in Idaho Falls to Idaho 33 near Roberts.  Blowing dust reduced visibility to zero.  Siding was ripped off an exterior wall of a car dealership in Idaho Falls.  A large pine tree was uprooted in Kate Curley Park in Idaho Falls.  A tree fell on a  home along the Salem Highway east of Plano.  A roof was partially ripped off a business in Rexburg.
The Botts ITD site recorded a 69 mph wind gust 1 mile northeast of Clementsville.
A 65 mph wind gust was measured at the base of Howe Peak and a 61 mph wind gust measured at Dead Man Canyon 9 miles east of Butte City.
The Taber mesonet recorded a 60 mph wind gust.

A wildfire began on April 21st near Firth and strong southwest winds grew the fire from 100 acres on the 21st to 1,200 acres on the 22nd.  Winds shifted to the northwest during the evening of the 22nd and the fire ran a different direction.  Residents near and around Firth were evacuated.   One home was destroyed along with several outbuildings.  Most of the burned land was private land.  The home that was destroyed was along 700 North which is where most of the evacuations occurred were homes along 700 North.  The wildfire was a controlled burn that became out of control due to the strong winds.  The fire was controlled by April 25th.
Wind gusts of 50 mph brought dust and debris across interstate 15 between Idaho Falls and Roberts and it was shut down in both directions from 3:30 PM May 7th until 10 AM on May 8th.
A large tree branch was snapped in two along with some roof damage in Holbrook with strong thunderstorm outflow winds.
Sixty mph winds estimated near Holbrook with blowing dust reducing visibility to 1/4 mile or less.
A 58 mph wind gust was measured at the Raft River RAWS site.

A surprise snow event dropped 3 to 5 inches of snow in the Island Park region with US Highway 20 closing from milepost near Island Park to the Montana border by 6 pm on the 21st. The road was blocked due to a truck accident for several hours.
A wildfire south of Oakley and Goose Creek Reservoir grew rapidly to 578 acres before being controlled.  No structures were threatened.

A human caused wildfire was started about 5 miles south of American Falls and spread rapidly on June 14th.  It was noticed at about 3:30 PM.   Two homes were destroyed by the fire.   Evacuations were ordered for the areas of Cold Creek Road, Ferry Hollow Road, Sunbeam Road, Indian Springs Road, Moonlight Lane, Hornbacher Road, Mayer Road, Garden Road, and all offshoots of those roads.   Residents were relocated to American Falls High School.   The fire downed several power lines.  Strong winds initially occurred and the fire grew rapidly to 3,843 acres.  It was a grass, brush and juniper fire.

The North Monument Fire was detected at 4 pm on the 15th and burned  about 7 miles west of Arco.  US 20/26/93 were temporarily closed due to the fire.  Three power poles were destroyed.  Some power outages reported at Craters of the Moon National Monument.  Fire grew quickly to 150 acres due to wind before being contained.
The Black Knoll Wildfire began on the 21st just north of Saint Anthony and grew to 443 acres before being contained.

On June 25th video of debris flow running over north bound interstate 15 just north of the Utah border in Oneida county was seen.    Radar estimated 2 inches of rainfall in that area resulting in the debris flow and flooding.
One inch hail reported near Moore.
It was the hottest June ever recorded at the Pocatello Regional Airport with an average monthly temperature of 69.9 degrees which was 7.7 degrees above the monthly normal.
It was the hottest June ever recorded at Burley with an average monthly temperature of 71.2 degrees which was 7.8 degrees above the monthly normal.
It was the hottest June ever recorded at Challis with an average monthly temperature of 70.1 degrees which was 9.2 degrees above the monthly normal.
It was the hottest June ever recorded at Stanley with an average monthly temperature of 58.3 degrees which was 6.7 degrees above the monthly normal.
A tornado was reported 2 miles north of Challis.  It removed and destroyed a roof on a house.
A 64 mph wind gust was measured at the China Point ITD site.
A 70 mph wind gust was measured at the Dubois ARL site.

Thunderstorm winds blew down a tree on a main transmission line south of Macks Inn knocking out power in the Island Park area reported by Fall River Rural Electric.  Some residents had a power outage until after 11 PM.
One inch hail in Ashton.
One and a half inch hail measured in Ashton.
One inch hail recorded in Ashton.
A 66 mph wind gust was measured at the Pocatello aiport.
A 342 acre fire was detected July 14th 15 miles southeast of Burley.  The fire burned timber, grass, and brush.  Aerial resources utilized with 100 personnel on the fire.

A 1,620 acre fire began  via a lightning strike on July 21st and was contained on July 23rd.  It was 4 miles southeast of Pauline.   It was mainly fueled by grass and brush and had about 100 personnel fighting it with aerial suppression involved.

A boat carrying 14 people including 11 children capsized in 6 foot waves created by strong winds on Bear Lake on July 22nd.    No injuries occurred and the boat passengers were rescued by park rangers 15 minutes after capsizing.
Several inches of mud, rocks, and debris flowed over Baker Creek Road that closed the road.   This was a burn scar area and the first of two road closing slide events.

A 60 year old man was struck by lightning at 1240 PM in the back parking lot of Love's Travel Stop in Idaho Falls at South 45th West.  He was taken to Eastern Idaho Regional Medical Center for treatment.
Flooding along Trapper Creek Road with excessive runoff from Squaw Creek and Little Squaw Creek drainages.   Several inches of rocks, mud and debris on the roadway.
Several washouts along Highway 37 south of Rockland including one along King Lane found in NWS storm survey.
Significant flash flooding occurred across a gravel road, and water was overtopping a small bridge along a paved road in the area of S 2950 E and Heglar Canyon Road west  northwest of Heglar.
Significant street flooding in the area of E 17th Street and Ammon Rd.

Significant street and yard flooding occurred in Iona.  The intersection of E Lincoln Rd and Crook Rd and the intersection of E Tanner Dr and N Aubree Way were flooded with over 1 foot of water in the roads in some areas.
Significant street and yard flooding occurred on the west side of Idaho Falls including Saddle Court, Troy Ave, and around Skyline High School.  Water was over the bottoms of vehicles.

A National Weather Service Storm Survey found evidence of high water along several stretches of Arbon Valley Road.  Road and Bridge crews called out to clear off extensive debris caused by the flash flooding on the roadway.
A NWS storm survey found flooding had occurred on Highway 36 with damage to culverts.  Idaho Transportation Department was cleaning up debris.

The US Forest Service reported Trapper Creek Road washed out in the area of FS Road 538 to Trout Creek Pass.  A 12 foot deep gully was running down the center of the road.  This was due to excessive runoff from the burned canyon walls from the Badger Fire burn scar.
Idaho Transportation Department reported multiple mudslides and rock falls along US 93 between Evans and McKim Creek roads.
Several inches of mud, rocks and debris moved across Baker Creek road that closed the road.  The cause was heavy rain over a burn scar area.
Idaho Transportation Department reported a mudslide and running water across Idaho Route 75 between East Fork Rd and Malm Gulch Rd completely blocking the highway.
Idaho Transportation Department reported water running across Idaho Highwy 37 between Lawery Lane and Cow Canyon Road.
A NWS survey found evidence of an extensive mud slide along and across Highway 75 North of Clayton.
Heavy rains caused several rock and mud slides along Trail Creek Road for several days.
Raft River mesonet recorded 67 mph wind gust.
A 79 mph wind gust measured by public on Yale Road just south of 400 N.
Lost River Area mesonet recorded 61 mph wind gust.
Winds affected power lines and knocked out power to residents west of Aberdeen and Springfield.
A 64 mph wind gust at the Pocatello Regional Airport ASOS site.
A 60 mph gust at INL Radioactive Waste Management site.
Thunderstorms damaged power lines and knocked out power to parts of Michaud and Fort Hall Reservation.
INL Critical Infrastructure site recorded a 64 mph gust.
A 63 mph wind gust at the INL central facilities.
A 69 mph wind gust at INL Reactor Technologies Complex.
A 64 mph wind gust at at the INL Puzzle/US Highway 20 site.
Thunderstorm winds knocked out power to residents south and east of Ashton.
A 60 mph wind gust at the Ohio Gulch mesonet site.
Power lines reported down near Roberts.
Multiple power outages affecting over 500 customers near Milner, Hobson, and Hynes.
Thunderstorm winds knocked out power to 176 customers west of Idaho Falls airport.
Several trees downed in Pocatello with damage to a house and many branches in roadways.   Some damage near 500 block of North Garfield Road.
Funnel cloud reported in Pocatello.

Lightning caused a 5 acre fire 1 mile northeast of Hailey and prompted some evacuations in Hailey.   Rain overnight on August 5th and 6th helped suppression and no structures were affected.   The fire was controlled on the 6th and contained on the 7th.
Half dollar sized hail in Medowville area.
Hail damage reported on vehicle.
Multiple reports of ping pong ball and half dollar sized hail with many vehicles dented by the hail.
Quarter to ping pong ball sized hail along Panting Rd just south of Horsley Ln.
Hail reported at Conda town site.

A human caused fire began on September 5th and burned 510 acres about 23 miles south of Stanley and affected the Alturas Creek Campgrounds. It burned in brush, grass, ponderosa pine and Douglas fir. It was in very steep and complex terrain. Campsite closures were: Cabin Creek Trailhead, Perkins Lake, Alturas Lake, Pettit Lake Areas, Smokey Bear Alturas, North Shore Alturas, and Alturan inlet. The following roads were closed: Cabin Creek, Alturas Creek, and Beaver Creek. All Alturas Lake campers were evacuated. The fire was contained by September 20th.
A 65 mph wind gusts 6 miles south of Sun Valley.  There was a power outage in Blaine County affecting about 1,000 customers until about 5:30 PM MDT.
An irrigation wheel line was blown over and blown into an adjoining field.
Sixty five mph wind gust 11 miles west southwest of Atomic City.
Eighteen miles west of Osgood recorded a 65 mph wind gust.
A 59 mph wind gust near Richfield.
A 60 mph wind gust 12 miles southeast of Butte City.
Sixty mph 6 miles northwest of Minidoka.
A 60 mph gust 1 mile northeast of Terreton.
A 60 mph wind gust 9 miles south southwest of Mud Lake.
A 60 mph wind gust 1 mile north of Roberts.
ASOS at Pocatello Regional Airport recorded a thunderstorm outflow wind of 59 mph.
Idaho Power reported about 1,000 customers in Pocatello without power on the afternoon of the 18th.

A large wildfire began August 10th and burned into mid October before being 100 percent contained.   It burned 88,000 acres and advanced to 30 miles northwest of Stanley.   It damaged some back roads making them impassable and several closures including rafting put in points.  The fire was in very steep inaccessible terrain and very hard for fire fighters to deal with.   Eventually much more moist conditions by mid October ended the wildfire.

Generally 2 to 6 inches of snow fell in the Pocatello and Chubbuck areas with several slide offs reported on roads.  Tree branches snapped due to the weight of snow on leave covered trees damaging automobiles.   Snow fell during the day on the 11th turned to rain in the late afternoon then changed back to snow overnight.
An early autumn snow storm brought amounts of 6 to 8 inches from Idaho Falls through Rexburg with extensive slide offs and accidents reported on roadways.
Estimated snowfall amounts from SNOTEL sites were 8 inches at Bostetter Ranger Station and 10 inches at Howell Canyon.
Estimated SNOTEL amounts were 10 inches at Sedgwick Peak and 11 inches at Wildhorse Divide.   The McCammon COOP observer reported 5 inches of snow.
An estimated 9 inches of snow fell at the Oxford Springs SNOTEL site.
Estimated SNOTEL snow amounts were 11 inches at Emigrant Summit and 9 inches at Franklin Basin.
The COOP observer at Bone recorded 13 inches of snow.   Soda Spring reported 10.5 inches and the Sheep Mountain SNOTEL had an estimated 13 inches of snow.
An estimated 9 inches of snow fell at the SNOTEL sites Slug Creek Divide and Somsen Ranch.
Estimated SNOTEL snow amounts were the following:  Dollarhide Summit 20 inches, Galena 10 inches, Galena Summit 17 inches, and Lost Wood Divide 12 inches.
A 69 mph wind gust was measured at the Rover mesonet site 9 miles south southwest of Mud Lake.
A 64 mph gust was measured 1 mile east northeast of Howe.
A 61 mph wind gust was measured at the Kettle Butte site.
A 58 mph wind gust was measured at the Burley Municipal Airport.
A 59 mph wind gust was recorded at Moburg Canyon.

A 68 mph wind gusts occurred at the Pocatello Regional airport.   In the Pocatello region extensive damage occurred with several downed trees...one on top of a car with a passenger in it causing injury.   One tree went through a roof.   Multiple signs of businesses were blown over, several power lines downs with multiple power outages.   Roofs and shingles were blown off buildings.
Eight-hundred customers were without power in McCammon.  A power pole was downed in Lava Hot Springs with 1,200 customers without power.
Several 50 to 55 mph wind gusts were measured along interstate 84 between Burley and the Utah border.
A 59 mph wind gust was measured at the Burley airport.  Widespread gusts of over 50 mph occurred through the morning of the 14th.
Ten to 12 inches of snow was recorded by multiple observers in Bellevue with 17 inches recorded by multiple sources in Hailey.
AS much as 26 to 32 inches of snow was reported in Sun Valley and Ketchum.
Heavy snow fell in the Sawtooth region with the Stanley COOP observer reporting 13 inches and the public reporting 32.5 inches 14 miles west northwest of Stanley.

Very heavy snow reported by the public and spotters with the following amounts:  4 miles north northwest of Darlington 20 inches, Moore 18 inches, Mackey 16 inches, Darlington 15 inches and Mackay 14 inches.
The Island Park COOP observer recorded 30 inches of snow with 14 inches 14 miles north northwest of Macks Inn.
The COOP observer at Dubois measured 11 inches of snow and the one 6 miles north of Small measured 18 inches.
Heavy snow fell with 8.5 inches at the Preston COOP site, 8.5 inches at the Malad City COOP site, with 9 to 10 inches reported at Preston via the public and cocorahs.
An avalanche near Driggs and Relay Ridge killed two teenage boys at around 2:45 PM on December 17th. It was in a backcountry area with one snow mobiler and one skier killed in the avalanche.

Snow Squall.   Visibility below 1/4 mile from 400 AM to 500 AM with moderate to heavy snow observed and wind gusts of 25 to 38 mph.  ITD RWIS Station ITD88.  I-86 Raft River.

A 30 year old man was found dead in a field near Parker Idaho.   The cause was believed to be extended exposure to cold air.   At the time of death wind chill temperatures were in the teens.
An extended period of snow and wind closed US Highway 93 from Arco to Carey on December 26th.   Snow amounts in the extended period ranged from 2 to 10 inches.

An extended period of Pacific moisture influx created high winds and snow over the several days surrounding the Christmas Holiday.   6 inches of snow fell in Dubois.   Interstate 15 was closed from Dubois to the Montana border on December 26th.
The COOP observer in Bern recorded 15 inches of snow with 12 inches on the 25th and 26th.
A long period of heavy snow and strong winds occurred in the Big Hole's.  Idaho Highway 33 was closed at Teton Pass on the 26th.   High elevations reported over a foot of snow.

Several days of strong Pacific moisture influx brought heavy snow with periods of very strong winds over a 6 day period surrounding the Christmas holiday.  Travel was very difficult with Idaho Highway 34 closed from Soda Springs to the Wyoming border.  Soda Springs recorded 19 inches of snow and Bone recorded 14 inches of snow.

A long period of Pacific moisture streamed into the region with strong winds and heavy snow.   Idaho highway 34 was closed from Soda Springs to the Wyoming border on the 26th and US Highway 26 was closed from Ririe to Swan Valley.   At least 60 motorists were stranded in Swan Valley on the 26th due to the road closure.   Swan Valley received 7 inches of snow.

A long period of snow and and periods of strong winds over several days surrounding the Christmas holiday  brought extreme travel difficulties.  Idaho Highway 47 from Ashton to Warm River, Idaho Highway 87 from Island Park to the Montana border, US Highway from Ashton to the Montana border were all closed on December 26th.  The Island Park COOP observer recorded 24 inches of snow from the 24th through 27th.

Heavy snow and strong winds occurred over an extended period in the days surrounding the Christmas holiday.  The COOP observer at Minidoka measured 8 inches of snow with 6 on the 25th and 26th.  The Oakley COOP observer carried 16 inches of snow from the 25th through 27th.

An extensive period of Pacific moisture influx caused periods of snow combined with strong winds to create very difficult travel conditions over several days surrounding the Christmas holiday .  The Chilly Barton Flat COOP site measured 8 inches of snow on the 26th and 27th.  US Highway 93 was closed from Carey to Arco on the 26th.
Heavy snow fell with 11 inches in Inkom and 14 inches at Downey measured by the COOP observers.  17.5 inches was measured by the Cocorahs observer 3 miles north northwest of Lava Hot Springs.

An extended period of Pacific moisture pushing into Idaho caused snow and periods of strong winds over and extended period covering the Christmas holiday.  The Richfield COOP observer reported 11 inches of snow with US Highway 93 closed from Carey to Arco on the 26th.
The COOP observer measured 21 inches of snow at the Ketchum site over the 24th through 27th.

Ten inches of snow was measured 3 miles north northeast of Driggs.  On the 26th US Highways 20 was closed from Ashton to the Montana border.  Idaho Highway 32 was closed from Ashton to Tetonia.  Idaho Highway 33 was closed from Newdale to Tetonia.

A long period of snow and occasional strong winds surrounding the Christmas holiday brought difficult travel to the region.  Idaho Highway 33 was closed from Newdale to Tetonia.  US Highway 26 was closed from Ririe to Swan Valley.   The Idaho Falls COOP observer recorded 11 inches of snow from the 23rd to 27th.  9.4 inches fell in St Anthony.
Extremely heavy snow fell in the Wood River Foothills.   Amounts recorded were the following:  Bellevue 25 inches, Hailey 23 inches, Picabo 21 inches.
